500493|2026-03.headline: Bharat Forge FY26 consolidated revenue rose 11% to INR 16,812 crore, but standalone revenue fell 5% to INR 8,396 crore on US and CV demand headwinds.
500493|2026-03.overview: Consolidated FY26 revenue was INR 16,812 crore (up 11%) and EBITDA INR 2,921 crore (up about 6%), with consolidated net debt-to-equity at 0.41x. Standalone revenue fell about 5% YoY to INR 8,396 crore and standalone EBITDA was INR 2,312 crore (27.5% margin), though Q4 standalone revenue rose 8.5% QoQ to INR 2,260 crore on export recovery and domestic auto strength. Management is restructuring the German steel subsidiary (CDP Bharat Forge) over roughly 15-18 months, is taking an e-mobility investment write-off, and is pushing growth in aerospace, defence and JSA castings. Management guided to about 25% growth for India operations in FY27, barring geopolitical shocks.

segments.name: Standalone (auto + industrial components)

segments.name: Defence (KSSL)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 1,562 crore; order book close to INR 11,000 crore with stable revenue accretion expected over 3-4 years. Management expects 30-40% growth guidance from earlier call to be carried by ATAGS and CQB carbine milestones.

segments.name: Aerospace
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about INR 400 crore; now about 26% of Q4 industrial non-auto exports and the second-largest industrial export contributor. Margins stated as above company average; target INR 1,000 crore in about 3 years.

segments.name: JSA (castings)
segments.commentary: Secured INR 292 crore of new business in FY26; growth continuing despite weak wind export demand. Raised external capital from Premji Invest to fund capacity expansion as an independent business.

segments.name: K-Drive (axles)
segments.commentary: Acquired recently; secured about INR 500 crore of new business. Management sees revenue doubling in 3-4 years, with a goal of mid-teens margins.

segments.name: Europe and US subsidiaries
segments.commentary: Europe EBITDA margin 4% and US 3.5% in FY26. German CDP steel business is being wound up via solvent liquidation, to complete around end CY27, with losses expected to fall.

guidance_outlook: FY27 India operations (standalone plus Indian subsidiaries) expected to grow close to 25%, barring further geopolitical disruption; growth to come mainly from aerospace, defence and automotive components, with aerospace growing faster than defence.
Overseas losses expected to reduce as CDP losses fall away during restructuring, with completion around end of CY27.
Capex of INR 800-850 crore over a 15-18 month period across forging, casting and products platforms.
Defence revenue to see ATAGS and CQB carbine production start in H2 FY27; large project backlog to start in H2 of this year.

Data-centre orders to start contributing from Q3-Q4 FY27 and ramp up in FY28.
capex_capacity: Ongoing capex programmes across forging, casting and products platforms to total INR 800-850 crore over 15-18 months; management gave no FY28+ figure beyond this.
ATAGS initial production capacity about five guns per month; testing expected to complete in H2 FY27 before production and supplies start.
Explosives plant planned in Andhra Pradesh, subject to significant approvals; Orissa project environmental clearance still pending, expected in 2-4 months.

Acquired 30% stake in Fortuna Engineering (Nashik) for INR 130 crore; company has revenue about INR 380 crore and net cash about INR 20 crore, and plans to add new machining lines (mid-teens EBITDA/EBIT margin).
JSA capacity expansion funded by Premji Invest capital raise; plan to shift some manufacturing from Europe to India.
demand_pricing: US CV: management says outlook strong, citing aging fleet replacement and emission norms due early 2027; energy price rise a common industry issue.
India CV: demand expected to be reasonably stable as energy costs are passed along the value chain.
US passenger car market stable at about 16-16.1 million vehicles, similar to last year; Europe seen as more challenged due to prolonged war.
Energy cost is the biggest cost issue; management is negotiating compensation with customers for energy-intensive elements.
Aerospace: multiple new wins across jet engine structures and landing systems; selected as first Indian supplier of critical components by a global aerospace OEM.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 growth be broken down by defence, US CV, non-auto and domestic?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined granular split; said higher growth from aerospace, then defence, then components (auto and industrial). Outlook strong for both US and India CV.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 25% India growth is standalone versus Indian subsidiaries?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to split it; the 25% target is at overall India level, covering standalone plus Indian subsidiaries.

qa_highlights.question: Will German CDP losses disappear from operating numbers now that restructuring has started?
qa_highlights.answer: Losses go away as the entity is wound up, expected by end of CY27; restructuring is a 15-18 month process combining customer transition and solvent liquidation.

qa_highlights.question: What are the defence revenue timing and milestones from the INR 2,816 crore of new defence orders?
qa_highlights.answer: ATAGS and CQB carbine production to start H2 FY27; data-centre-related orders begin Q3-Q4 FY27 and ramp in FY28; large backlog projects in H2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Has the FY28 explosives capex been confirmed as the heavy spend year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the explosives plant in Andhra Pradesh is about 24 months from groundbreaking to pilot production, with construction starting by end-2026 after approvals.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise external capital in JSA when it could be funded internally?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the raise lets JSA grow with its own momentum, as it could become a multi-thousand-crore business, with plans to shift European casting manufacturing to India.

risks_watch: Middle East conflict and energy price spikes affecting costs, transport and demand; management says it is too early to say the worst is past.
Overseas losses (Europe EBITDA margin 4%, US 3.5%) must narrow as CDP is wound down, with completion around end CY27.
Defence revenue ramp depends on ATAGS testing completion and production start in H2 FY27; the order-book conversion timing remains open.
Explosives plant needs significant approvals; Orissa project environmental clearance still pending.
Management declined to disclose defence share of revenue, K-Drive/Fortuna-level detail, or a timeline for a possible defence listing ("will look at separately").

Management was evasive on segment-level FY27 growth splits, defence margins and capacity details, and declined several specific questions.

500493|2026-06.headline: Bharat Forge Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 18.7% YoY to INR4,640 crores, but EBITDA margin was 16.2% after a ~160 bps input-cost hit.
500493|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue rose 11.5% YoY to INR2,347 crores and EBITDA rose 4.5% to INR614 crores at a 26.2% margin, which management said absorbed about 160 bps of energy, input and logistics cost increases (normalised margin near 28%). Consolidated EBITDA was INR752 crores (up 10.3%). Overseas performance was mixed: Europe was EBITDA-positive, while US steel operations lost money after a multi-month press breakdown. Management announced a fundraise of up to INR2,500 crores for growth capex and said FY27 should be very good, with FY28 also strong.

qa_highlights.question: Asset turns, margins and returns for the new businesses, and the overall capex plan for FY27/28?
qa_highlights.answer: Organic India capex is about INR1,800 crores, with asset turnover above 1.5x and accretive margins; business is already tied up for initial ramp-up.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise equity when the balance sheet is strong, and is the INR2,500 crore raise over and above the INR1,800 crore capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management wants to keep about INR2,000 crores of cash on balance sheet and sees M&A opportunities in India (JS Auto Cast, K Drive cited). The INR2,500 crore raise funds the current capex and leaves room for further growth.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 22-23% margin guidance company-wide?
qa_highlights.answer: No, it applies to the defence business on a steady-state annual basis.

qa_highlights.question: Will the cost pass-through reverse margins immediately?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins will improve gradually. Recoveries add to both revenue and cost, so reported margin will look better but not fully return to 28% immediately; per-unit margin will recover.

qa_highlights.question: Why was domestic CV/PV growth below industry, and what caused the Q1 supply challenges?
qa_highlights.answer: Mid-quarter steel labour and supply issues, plus fuel switching during the energy disruption. Management says these were overcome.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the CDP restructuring and its orders?
qa_highlights.answer: The CDP entity will cease to exist after restructuring; a sizable part of its orders will move to India at good margins, while some are being phased out.

500493|2026-09.headline: Bharat Forge Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose about 30% YoY to INR2,526 crore, with EBITDA margin at 25.9%.
500493|2026-09.overview: Management reported record quarterly export and domestic sales, with standalone revenue of INR2,526 crore (up almost 30% YoY) and EBITDA of INR655 crore (up 20%, 25.9% margin). Consolidated revenue was INR4,870 crore (up 21%) with EBITDA of INR778 crore (up about 9%, around 16% margin). Freight, energy and input cost inflation compressed margins, with pass-through to customers lagging; management flagged an optical impact of about 0.4% on margins. Defence order book stood at INR10,950 crore as of September, and the ATAGS bulk production clearance has been received, with revenue recognition expected from Q1 FY28.

financial_highlights.change: legal and consultancy charges for Europe steel restructuring

financial_highlights.value: INR476 crore / about INR6.7 crore negative

segments.name: Standalone / export CV and automotive
segments.commentary: Export CV business recorded its highest revenue, driven by volume growth, market share gains and ramp-up of new businesses. Standalone revenue grew almost 30% YoY.

segments.commentary: JS Auto Cast revenue INR220 crore (up 16%) with record quarterly EBITDA up 35%. Combined JSA and K-Drive quarterly run rate is about INR600 crore, up from about INR400 crore at acquisition for JSA and about INR300 crore for K-Drive, with FY27 combined revenue guided above INR2,200-2,300 crore.

segments.name: Europe (steel restructuring)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR931 crore and EBITDA INR29 crore (about 3.1% margin), despite lower utilisation from holidays and a difficult operating environment. Restructuring expected to conclude by mid-next year.

segments.name: US subsidiaries
segments.commentary: Revenue INR476 crore with EBITDA about INR6.7 crore negative. Steel subsidiary hit by one-time breakdowns; aluminium subsidiary faces raw material cost issues.

guidance_outlook: H2 FY27 expected to be stronger than H1, with recovery of price and cost increases from customers and ramp-up of new businesses.
Management expects 20%-25% revenue growth guidance to be met, driven across aerospace, industrial exports, semiconductor, CV, passenger car exports, marine, JSA and K-Drive.
Excluding 2%-3% inflationary impact on top line, H2 EBITDA growth expected to be in line with or slightly better than top-line growth.
India manufacturing: expected to exceed INR5,000 crore quarterly sales by end of next year (from about INR3,000-3,400 crore per quarter at 22% margin), with at least 200-250 bps margin accretion.

qa_highlights.question: Is the new aerospace order the Pratt & Whitney contract for mission-critical engine components?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not name the customer; said it has won significant new business from multiple customers and products, and a new aerospace-dedicated facility is about 60% sold out.

qa_highlights.question: Drivers of H2 revenue jump to meet 20%-25% guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Broad-based: aerospace, industrial exports, semicon, CV, passenger car exports, marine, JSA and K-Drive, with many new programmes moving into revenue.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ATAGS timing and how long to deliver?
qa_highlights.answer: Order not deferred; production approval was delayed. Revenue from Q1 FY28; 184 guns to be delivered over about 4 years with ramp-up, and revenue split roughly 10%, 15%, 20% then remainder by year.

qa_highlights.question: How will CQB contract timing work?
qa_highlights.answer: CQB bulk production clearance not yet received; delivery expected to start 4-6 months after clearance. Capacity estimated at 120-150 guns a year.

qa_highlights.question: Sustainable margin for India manufacturing and K-Drive profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: India manufacturing margin expected to add 200-250 bps; K-Drive targets double-digit EBITDA margin within 2 years with 20-25% annual growth, expanding into passenger car, SUV, pickup and utility segments.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving US subsidiary losses?
qa_highlights.answer: Steel subsidiary had one-time breakdowns, with a fix targeted by December; aluminium subsidiary has raw material cost issues and new non-auto products expected to lift profitability in 6-12 months.

risks_watch: Pass-through lag on freight, energy and raw material inflation, with about 2%-3% top-line inflationary impact in H2.
ATAGS revenue depends on customer absorption and induction schedule; CQB bulk production clearance pending.
US steel subsidiary breakdowns and aluminium raw material costs; profitability target depends on fixes by December and new product ramp.
Europe steel restructuring (CDP) execution through mid-next year with legal and consultancy exceptional charges.

Management did not name the aerospace customer; disclosure of order details remains limited.

rows.why: Bulk production clearance received with revenue recognition expected from Q1 FY28; 184 guns over about 4 years, ramp split roughly 10%, 15%, 20% then remainder.

rows.label: US steel subsidiary fix and aluminium break-even
rows.why: Steel subsidiary solution targeted by December after one-time breakdowns, and aluminium expected above break-even within 6-12 months, but US EBITDA was about INR6.7 crore negative on INR476 crore revenue.

rows.label: Europe steel restructuring (CDP) completion
rows.why: Europe revenue INR931 crore with EBITDA INR29 crore (~3.1% margin); restructuring to conclude by mid-next year with exceptional charges (about INR20 crore in Q2).

tone.note: Management was confident on the 20-25% growth guide, Baramati capacity, defence order book and India manufacturing margin accretion, but cautious on freight/energy pass-through, US subsidiary losses and ATAGS phasing; analysts pressed on the unnamed aerospace customer and the order-book deferral que

500495|2026-03.headline: Escorts Kubota Q4 FY26 standalone EBITDA rose 31.8% YoY to INR386.0 crore (13.1% margin); FY27 tractor industry guided flat to ±3%.
500495|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 standalone operating revenue from continuing operations rose 21.4% YoY to INR2,950.7 crore, with PAT from continuing operations up 29.6% to INR324.8 crore (about 20% excluding a prior-year INR27.1 crore impairment). FY26 was a record year: tractor volume 1,33,670 units (+15.7%), revenue INR11,472.8 crore (+12.6%) and EBITDA INR1,513 crore (13.2% margin). Management guided FY27 industry flat to +/-3%, with H1 flat and H2 a substantial decline on a high base, low monsoon and El Nino risk, and rising input costs. Management expects input-cost pressure to be significant over the next two quarters, with only about 1.5% price increase taken in April.

financial_highlights.change: +29.6% YoY; ~20% YoY excluding prior-year INR27.1 crore impairment

segments.name: Agri Machinery (tractors, implements, engines, services)
segments.commentary: FY26 segment revenue INR9,709.6 crore (+15.8%). Domestic tractor volume 1,26,994 units (+14.9%); exports 6,676 tractors (+33.8%). Non-tractor share of segment revenue fell to 18% from 20%.

segments.name: Construction Equipment
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR556.5 crore (+22.6%), EBITDA margin 12.7% (+386 bps). FY26 volume 5,794 units (-10.6%); Q4 volume about 1,877 units (+9%) versus served industry about +4%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 domestic tractor industry guided flat to +2-3% or -2-3%; H1 FY27 at par, H2 a substantial decline on high base, sub-normal monsoon forecast and El Nino (about 65-70% probability).
Management expects market share and volume growth in FY27 irrespective of industry outcome, citing new products and channel fixes.
Input costs: management estimates a 5-6% cost increase; steel up 7-8%, tyres asked 15-20%, base metals double-digit. Significant pressure expected in the next two quarters.

Management aims to maintain full-year EBIT margin, but said this is too early to call; permanent labour and energy cost increases (Haryana contract wages up about 35%, UP vendor costs up 22-23%) will not reverse.
FY27 capex: normal capex INR350-400 crore; greenfield about INR500 crore in FY27; captive finance capital infusion about INR300 crore by year-end and INR200 crore next year.
Long-term tractor industry CAGR assumed 6-8%; FY28 seen as reasonably good given emission norm change from 1 April 2028.
capex_capacity: Normal capex about INR311 crore in FY26 (cash flow); FY27 normal capex guided at INR350-400 crore, of which majority is product development (about INR200 crore in FY26, INR200-250 crore planned FY27).

Greenfield plant: land initial payment made, balance payment expected within the quarter; Phase 1 more than INR2,000 crore; over 7-10 years total spend above INR5,000 crore covering tractors, construction equipment and possibly Agri Solutions.
Captive finance company: Board approval INR700 crore of capital, INR200 crore invested so far, portfolio above INR100 crore at end-March; balance INR500 crore over 12-15 months.
Construction equipment capacity utilisation was about 47% last year per analyst; mini excavators to be manufactured in India only after new plant is ready (currently imported from Japan).
demand_pricing: Regional FY26 tractor growth: North and Central about 16-17% versus about 30% in West and South, which management attributed largely to subsidies. FY27 headwind expected mainly in West and South; North flat to nil growth.
Product gaps: paddy special tractors for southern markets launched, with early signs of share loss in South stabilising; further launches planned over next 3-4 months across three brands.
Price increase of about 1.5% taken in April across tractors and construction equipment; management says this is not sufficient to offset cost inflation.
Around 70% of tractor sales are financed; captive finance launched to speed approvals.

Construction equipment: served industry down about 7% in FY26 (crane -13%, backloader -10%, mini excavator +38%, compactor +5%); Q4 served industry +4%. Crane market share gained 2.7%; number 1 in mini excavators.
Exports: Kubota Global channel about 60% of tractor exports; crane exports rising to 5-6% of revenue from about 3-3.5%, target 10% by 2030. Agri Solutions harvesting and planting portfolio expanding.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company planning FY27 tractor industry growth and new product contribution to share gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Neeraj Mehra guided FY27 industry flat to +/-2-3% and said volume and share growth look positive irrespective of industry, citing paddy special tractors and further launches over the next 3-4 months.

qa_highlights.question: What drove Q4 margin softness and what is the cost outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Bharat Madan attributed the QoQ dip mainly to mix (new products and higher non-tractor revenue, which carry lower margins) and noted commodity inflation mostly lands in the next two quarters; full-year margin maintenance is the aim, subject to geopolitics.

qa_highlights.question: What is the size of commodity impact and price hikes needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated a 5-6% cost increase versus revenue (base metals double-digit inflation); April price hike of about 1.5% was insufficient; some one-off costs may be amortised over time.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for construction equipment and the export opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjeev Bajaj expects a turnaround after monsoon if macro issues settle within 1-1.5 quarters; cranes exports rising; mini excavators are fully imported from Japan until India manufacturing starts.

qa_highlights.question: How will the large cash balance (about INR7,000 crore including investments) be deployed?
qa_highlights.answer: Bharat Madan said greenfield Phase 1 is above INR2,000 crore within a more than INR5,000 crore 7-10 year plan, plus the captive finance infusion, and some surplus will remain on the balance sheet for growth.

qa_highlights.question: Captive finance capital and ROE aspirations?
qa_highlights.answer: Up to INR700 crore capital approved (INR200 crore invested); long-term ROE for captive finance companies seen at about 1.5-2%, with the primary aim being to support tractor sales.

risks_watch: Input cost inflation (steel, tyres, base metals, energy, manpower) in the next two quarters, with limited pass-through so far.
H2 FY27 tractor demand decline from high base, sub-normal monsoon, El Nino and reservoir levels below last year and 10-year average.
West Asia conflict, shipping disruption and rupee depreciation affecting costs and supply chain.
Construction equipment recovery depends on government capex pace and resolution of macro uncertainty.
Execution of new product launches and greenfield plant (Phase 1 above INR2,000 crore) and captive finance AUM growth.
Ramp-up of component exports from India to Kubota (INR500-1,000 crore expected by FY30); delayed earlier due to quality issues.

So our effort will be to maintain the margin on a full year basis.

So, in both the segments, our market share growth is visible even in the last year where it was -- the industry was going down.

rows.why: Management sees FY28 as reasonably good on the emission norm change, with long-term tractor industry CAGR assumed at 6-8%; this sits beyond the 2-4 quarter window.

500495|2026-06.headline: Escorts Kubota Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 28% to INR3,178.9 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 11.2% from 13.1% on commodity inflation.
500495|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue from continuing operations grew 28% YoY to INR3,178.9 crore, with tractor domestic volume at a record 35,457 units (+22.9%) and market share up 36 bps. Standalone EBITDA rose 9.4% to INR355.4 crore, but margin compressed 190 bps to 11.2% as metal and rubber commodity inflation (about 5% on tractors per management) hit costs. Net profit growth of 4% reported is distorted by a INR76 crore land-sale gain and RED divestment in the base quarter; management cites 26% growth excluding the gain. Management raised its FY27 industry outlook to mid-to-mid-single-digit growth from a prior plus/minus 2-3% view, and flagged a further 1.5-2% cost pressure in Q2 with price hikes under discussion.

financial_highlights.change: +4% YoY; +26% excluding prior-year INR76 crore land-sale gain

segments.name: Tractors (domestic)
segments.commentary: Sold 35,457 units, record Q1 and +22.9% YoY vs industry +18.6%, gaining 36 bps share. South industry grew about 33% (overall 19%); Escorts South share about 6% after ~0.5-0.6 pp gain.

segments.name: Tractor exports
segments.commentary: Exports fell to 1,405 units from 1,733 (down about 19%) while industry exports rose 17.7% to 29,778; vessel availability and weak sub-40 HP compact exports (down ~8%) hurt. Kubota global network accounts for ~61% of export volume.

segments.name: Agri Machinery non-tractor business
segments.commentary: Agri Solutions, engines and spares/service parts were 19% of Agri Machinery revenue vs 18% a year earlier. Component exports were flat in Q1 and about INR160-170 crore last year.

segments.name: Construction Equipment
segments.commentary: Volume 1,344 machines (+27.4%) and revenue INR419.6 crore (+39.2%); EBIT impacted by commodity inflation. Crane industry grew 46% in Q1, partly on a low BS-V-affected base.

guidance_outlook: Domestic tractor industry FY27 now guided to mid-to-mid-single-digit growth (previously plus/minus 2-3%); Escorts expected to outgrow the industry via share gains.
Tractor cost pressure of about 5% continues in Q2 with a further 1.5-2% expected; management expects reversal from Q4 if geopolitical situation eases.
Price increases under discussion, not finalised; management said they will not fully offset material cost increases.
Tractor exports expected roughly flat in FY27 with Q1 shortfall recovered over the remaining three quarters; FY28 growth expected, including potential North America entry.
Construction equipment industry FY27 growth 12-15%: mini excavators and cranes high, backhoe loaders 5-7%, compactors 5-6%. Escorts CE expected to grow 12-15% for the full year.
FY27 capex INR850-900 crore: INR450-500 crore greenfield land (groundbreaking expected this month) plus INR350-400 crore normal capex. Total greenfield project INR2,000 crore.
Captive finance penetration 10-12% of dealers in Q1, nearing 15% in July; 40-50% of dealerships targeted by FY27 and pan-India by FY28.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex of INR850-900 crore: greenfield land INR450-500 crore (already paid, development starting) and normal capex INR350-400 crore.
Greenfield project total outlay about INR2,000 crore; FY28 spend could rise if construction is accelerated on strong demand.
Dealer channel holds about 30 days of inventory; company plans to build stock ahead of the festive season, which management says starts later this year from October.
Construction equipment: new models from October, and BS-V versions of backhoe loaders and compactors from September.
Captive finance covers limited states with about 250 dealers onboarded; southern states to be added in FY27.
demand_pricing: Industry record Q1 tractor volume of about 3.39 lakh units; management expects demand upside vs earlier guidance, with the last 45-50 days described as very positive.
Q2 growth may slow against a high base and the late festive season; monsoon distribution is the key monitorable.
Tractor price hike of about 1-1.5% taken in April; further hike being evaluated for Q2.

Construction equipment: cumulative price increases of about 6% effective (after channel discount adjustments) passed on in small tranches since the January 2025 BS-V hike; customers are negotiating longer, and prices are expected to stabilise in Q2.
Product gains: Promaxx contributes 20-22% of Farmtrac sales; Digitrac (incl. new 4x4) contributes 23-25% of Powertrac portfolio. Gap remains in 35-50 HP 4WD segment for Powertrac.
Escorts estimates Haryana contract-labour wage increase accounts for about 1% of the tractor cost impact.

qa_highlights.question: Is there upside to the FY27 industry outlook given monthly trends, and what is the festive-season sentiment?
qa_highlights.answer: Neeraj Mehra said there is upside in Q1 and July; the earlier guidance was plus/minus 2-3%, not negative, and the last 45-50 days were very positive. Current view is middle to mid-single-digit industry growth for FY27, with no quarterly or monthly estimate given.

qa_highlights.question: What was the Q1 metal cost headwind, and how will Q2 margins and pricing be handled?
qa_highlights.answer: Bharat Madan said the tractor business absorbed about 5% commodity cost impact, of which about 1% was Haryana contract-labour wages. Q2 faces a further 1.5-2%; a price hike of about 1-1.5% was taken in April, and the next hike is under discussion with timing expected in Q2. Relief is expected from Q4 if geopolitics ease.

qa_highlights.question: How much did Shaurya, Promaxx, Digitrac and Kubota new products contribute, and what product gaps remain?
qa_highlights.answer: Promaxx contributes 20-22% of Farmtrac sales; Digitrac including the new 4x4 contributes 23-25% of the Powertrac portfolio. Powertrac has a gap in 35-50 HP 4WD, to be covered in the next few months. Kubota focus is 20-30 HP and 41-50 HP segments, which make up roughly 70-80% of the industry.

qa_highlights.question: What price hikes and growth expectations apply to construction equipment cranes, and is there customer pushback?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjeev Bajaj said cumulative price increases are about 6% after channel discount adjustments, passed on in small tranches since January 2025. Crane industry grew about 45% in Q1 on a subdued base. Customers are negotiating longer, and prices are expected to stabilise in Q2. CE industry FY27 growth guided at 12-15%.

qa_highlights.question: How is the southern market share trending, and how is captive finance performing?
qa_highlights.answer: Neeraj Mehra said South share is about 6% on a 3-brand basis, gained about 0.5-0.6 pp in Q1, and new products and channel fill are expected to continue the trend. Bharat Madan said captive finance penetration was 10-12% of dealers in Q1, near 15% in July, across about 250 onboarded dealers; 40-50% of dealerships by FY27 and pan-India by FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export outlook for FY27 and FY28, and what is the component export trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Bharat Madan guided FY27 tractor exports roughly flat, with the Q1 shortfall expected to be recovered over three quarters, and FY28 growth including a possible North America entry. Component exports were flat in Q1 against about INR160-170 crore last year, with growth expected from H2 and more than doubling over two years.

qa_highlights.question: What are the capex plans, and could FY28 capex rise? Is a buyback possible?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex is INR850-900 crore: INR450-500 crore greenfield land (already paid, groundbreaking expected in August) and INR350-400 crore normal capex. Total greenfield outlay is about INR2,000 crore, and FY28 spend could rise if construction is accelerated. On buyback, Bharat Madan said promoters hold about 68%+, so scope is limited and promoter alignment is needed.

risks_watch: Q2 cost headwind of a further 1.5-2% on top of about 5% existing commodity inflation; price hikes not finalised and management says they will not fully offset material costs, so tractor margins may stay under pressure.
Demand normalisation against a high base and a late festive season (from October); monsoon distribution is the key monitorable, and management expects growth to slow in Q2.
Construction equipment customer pushback: buyers are taking longer to decide and negotiating harder after about 6% cumulative price increases; Q2 pricing expected to stabilise.
Tractor exports fell about 19% in Q1 on vessel availability and weak sub-40 HP compact exports; FY27 flat guidance depends on recovering the Q1 shortfall in the remaining three quarters.
Dealer inventory at about 30 days with build-up planned ahead of the festive season; a channel stock build could be a risk if demand slows.
Greenfield capex of about INR2,000 crore total, with FY28 spend possibly rising; captive finance expansion to 40-50% of dealerships by FY27 and pan-India by FY28 to be tracked.
key_quotes: So yes, you are absolutely right. We see an upside in the last quarter and also in July.
So we are contemplating how to pass it on. So the discussions are happening. The quantum is not yet finalized.
But the price increase will not compensate for the entire material cost increases.
So this year, FY '27, we expect the export to be more or less flattish in nature.

Cautious on margins, pricing and exports: management was non-committal on the size and timing of price hikes, said they would not fully offset cost inflation, and declined to give quarterly or monthly estimates.

500495|2026-09.headline: Escorts Kubota Q2 FY27 standalone EBITDA margin fell to 9.0% from 13.1% YoY on commodity inflation, despite revenue up 16.3% to INR3,231.4 crores.
500495|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from continuing operations rose 16.3% YoY to INR3,231.4 crores, but EBITDA dropped to INR292.4 crores and margin compressed to 9.0% (13.1% a year ago, 11.2% QoQ) on commodity inflation of roughly 8-9% against about 3.5% of price increases taken so far. Net profit fell to INR255 crores from INR321.2 crores. Domestic tractor volumes were flat-to-up at 32,628 units while the industry declined about 3%, and construction equipment grew strongly. Management guided to continued margin pressure in Q3, with recovery expected from Q4 as a new price increase of about 3-3.5% takes effect from mid-November.

segments.name: Tractors (domestic)
segments.commentary: Domestic volume 32,628 units vs 32,329 YoY while industry fell about 3% to roughly 2.66 lakh; market share up 48 bps. Exports fell to 1,389 units from 1,548 YoY.

segments.name: Agri Machinery (incl. non-tractor)
segments.commentary: Segment revenue INR2,690.1 crores (+10.6%); non-tractor (Agri Solutions, engines, spares and service) now 22% of segment revenue vs 17% a year ago. EBIT margin 7.8%.

segments.name: Construction Equipment
segments.commentary: Volumes 1,764 machines vs 1,146 (+54%); revenue INR536.2 crores (+58.6%); EBIT margin 7.9%, aided by operating leverage and four price increases in calendar 2026.

guidance_outlook: Tractor margins to stay under pressure in Q3 FY27 from a further 2-3% cost inflation; recovery expected from Q4 as a new price increase of about 3-3.5% takes effect mid-November (cumulative 6-7% pricing).
Management expects commodity prices to soften from Q4 but says further price increases are possible if pressure persists.
Domestic tractor industry guided to a marginal single-digit decline for FY27, implying a double-digit decline in H2; H1 industry growth was about 8%.
Construction equipment industry growth expected to moderate to high-teens in FY27; management said H2 could grow about 15-16%.
Exports expected to stay weak for the next 6 months given the existing order book; recovery more likely next fiscal year, with flat FY27 exports a good outcome.
Normal capex about INR350 crores in FY27 and about INR300 crores in FY28; greenfield project total about INR2,000 crores over 3-4 years, with INR400-450 crores already spent on land.
capex_capacity: Normal capex this fiscal about INR350 crores, broadly on track.
Greenfield project costed at about INR2,000 crores in phases: tractor factory first, then construction equipment plant, then spare parts warehouse, over 3-4 years.
Land acquisition for the greenfield project already done at roughly INR400-450 crores; construction to start next year.
Localisation of Kubota-brand tractors (using Escorts engines) and rice transplanters is on track, with launches in coming quarters.
Powertrac 4-wheel-drive product range planned for January (early Q4), targeting gaps in the 4WD segment.
Construction equipment: BLX75K backhoe loader (Kubota engine, jointly developed with Kubota Japan), F-25 25-ton and Hydra 16 Plus 16-ton cranes showcased.
demand_pricing: Industry: April-August tractor growth about 17%; September down about 18% and October down about 16-17% on high GST-cut base and El Nino monsoon (rainfall 13% deficit).
Regional: West industry down 21% in Q2; South marginally down; MP declining; North and East marginally up. Management expects the North to be flat to marginally down in H2.
Commodity inflation about 5% in Q1 rising to 8-9% by end-Q2; about 75-80% from commodities and 20% from manpower and conversion costs. Further 2-3% inflation expected in Q3.
Price actions: about 1.5% in April and about 2-2.5% in late August (3.5% total), with a further 3-3.5% from mid-November.

4WD tractors growing faster than the market (about 17-18% of industry by management estimate); 4WD volumes up about 3x over the last 6-7 months. Promaxx and Digitrac together contribute 20-23% of Farmtrac and Powertrac sales.
Construction equipment: pass-through of about 90% of inflation to customers in H1, per management; four price increases taken in calendar 2026.
Export industry up 16% in Q2 but Escorts exports fell; October exports recovered to about 500 units a month.
Inventory correction in October and expected in November ahead of Diwali/Dhanteras stock build; management acknowledged the stock correction risk.

qa_highlights.question: How much commodity headwind was there in Q2, what price hikes were taken, and how should margins evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Commodity inflation rose from about 5% in Q1 to 8-9% by end-Q2 against 3.5% price increases taken; a further 2-3% hits Q3 and a 3-3.5% increase follows mid-November, with the impact mainly in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: How much industry decline is expected in H2 and what is the regional split?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided to a marginal single-digit full-year industry decline, implying double-digit H2 decline; West and MP are the main drags, with North expected flat to marginally down.

qa_highlights.question: Will the non-tractor business margins be comparable to tractors?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the non-tractor business is broadly comparable to tractor margins overall, with imported harvester trading lower and parts and locally made engines at good margins; non-tractor is 18% of revenue, tractors about 65%, CE about 17%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise 22% YoY and 14% QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher production to build inventory for the season (production above sales by 20-25%) increased overhead absorption; there was a one-time inventory benefit of about 1.5% that reverses in Q3; contractual manpower costs in Haryana rose 35% from April.

qa_highlights.question: What are the capex and greenfield plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Normal capex about INR350 crores this year and about INR300 crores next year; greenfield project about INR2,000 crores over 3-4 years, with INR400-450 crores already spent on land.

qa_highlights.question: What is a sustainable CE margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the current CE margin level (7.9%) to be sustained given good demand momentum, with H2 typically about 60% of annual business; four price hikes were taken in calendar 2026.

risks_watch: Tractor EBITDA margin recovery depends on the mid-November price increase sticking amid a weak industry; management has not given a firm FY28 demand view.

500520|2026-09.headline: M&M Q2 FY27 consolidated PAT rose 25% to ₹4,588 crore on revenue of ₹57,553 crore, with full-year tractor industry outlook cut to flattish.

qa_highlights.question: How has demand shaped up after the GST cut, and what changed in powertrain mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Demand stayed robust with no SUV slowdown in rural areas; petrol has lost share to CNG, EV and diesel. Vahan like-for-like festive volumes were roughly flat to minus, and M&M is the fastest-growing brand on Vahan.

qa_highlights.question: Is M&M planning capacity for full utilisation given structural shortages?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity went from 17,000 five years ago to 66,000 now and will be 82,000 at year end and 92,000 next year; a Nagpur plant and a supplier park will double capacity with room to expand quickly.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for EV demand after fuel prices fall, and localisation of batteries?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says EV adoption has passed a tunnelling inflection; pump prices are unlikely to fall soon. Battery packs are already localised; cells will be sourced overseas unless captive supply is needed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the tractor outlook for next year given monsoon normalisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects NOAA's normal monsoon probability above 70% next year and a flat industry even in a strong El Niño year; the Navratri shift will support Q1 FY28.

qa_highlights.question: How much PLI was booked and what is the EV margin path?
qa_highlights.answer: About ₹1,000 crore PLI booked this quarter. EV margins are around 9% helped by PLI; management expects volume, supplier leverage and pricing power to take margins toward ICE levels over time, with depreciation the main drag.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for international Farm subsidiaries after exits?
qa_highlights.answer: Sampo and Erkunt exits are complete; Mitsubishi Mahindra Agricultural Machinery Japan closes by Q4. Exit costs from 3Q and 4Q last year will not recur, helping Farm consolidation in H2.

risks_watch: Tractor industry outlook cut to flattish; monsoon at 87% of LPA with drought in Maharashtra and Karnataka; reservoir levels low.
Commodity inflation: steel up 17% YoY, copper up 42%, rubber up 40%; management flagged possible upticks in steel and rubber in Q3.
International Farm subsidiaries (US -15%, Brazil -18%, Turkey -36%) remain under industry stress.
EV margin depends on PLI support (~₹1,000 crore this quarter) and faces depreciation burden from new investments.
Possible inventory correction in tractor channel in Q4 as industry adjusts to slower demand.
Capacity constraints may limit near-term volume and share gains until NU_IQ, EV and Nagpur capacity comes on stream.
500520|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on the headline quarter and long-term targets, but cautious on tractors and commodities. Management cut the full-year tractor outlook, said the challenges are not yet over, and was reluctant to share order books or product-level capacity.
key_quotes: The keyword for this quarter is resilience.
What we have always said is 15% to 20% EPS growth and 18% RoE.
We've reduced the outlook for the year.
Demand for all our brands at the moment is extremely strong, EV and ICE.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Auto capacity from 66k to 82k units/month (+27%) by end-FY27 and 92k in FY28 against waiting periods of 5-7 months, while tractor industry flat and Farm profit fell 9%.

rows.label: New capex announcement

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: SUV industry guided mid-to-high teens and LCV raised to double-digit growth, with 5-7 month waiting periods on Scorpio-N and XUV 7XO, but tractor offsets limit upside.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade

rows.label: New product launch

rows.label: Aerospace order book and third plant
rows.why: Airbus A320neo tail package and helicopter fuselage won, third plant under construction, and target of $1bn annual orders by FY30.

rows.label: Farm international subsidiary exits
rows.why: Sampo and Erkunt exits complete and Mitsubishi Mahindra Japan closing by Q4, so exit costs from last year's Q3 and Q4 will not recur, supporting H2 Farm consolidation.

rows.label: Mahindra Finance AUM growth
rows.why: AUM above ₹1,30,000 crore against ₹65,000 crore starting point, with PAT up 61% YoY on lower asset quality and tech gains.

tone.note: Management was confident on auto demand, capacity ramp and the PLI-supported quarter, but cautious on tractors, monsoon and commodity inflation; analysts pressed on margins and EV profitability, and management declined to share order book data.

500530|2026-03.headline: Bosch Ltd to acquire related-party Bosch Chassis Systems India (RBIC) for INR9,068.7 crore, ~10.6x FY25 EV/EBITDA, targeted close by end-Q1 FY27.
500530|2026-03.overview: This transcript covers two investor calls on April 13, 2026, about the proposed acquisition of Bosch Chassis Systems India Pvt Ltd (RBIC), a group company, not a quarterly results call; management said it was in silent period and would not discuss quarterly results. RBIC posted FY25 revenue of about INR4,000 crore and a 19.3% EBITDA margin, with 9M FY26 revenue of about INR3,500 crore. Pro forma FY25 revenue for Bosch Ltd rises about 22% to INR22,000 crore and EBITDA margin improves from 12.8% to 13.9%, with about 5% pro forma EPS accretion. The deal is almost all cash, funded from existing funds and internal accruals, with a small preferential allotment to Robert Bosch Netherlands and Robert Bosch US, and shareholder voting runs April 9 to May 8, 2026.

financial_highlights.metric: Bosch Ltd pro forma FY25 revenue
Pro forma FY25 EBITDA margin (Bosch Ltd)

segments.name: RBIC (Bosch Chassis Systems India) - safety and braking
segments.commentary: Covers ABS, ESP, occupant safety sensors and controllers, EV new braking systems (iBooster, integrated power brakes) and conventional actuation; about one-third two-wheeler and the rest passenger and commercial vehicles per management's rough estimate. Three plants (Chakan, Manesar, Sanand) and about 2,000 people including contract workers.

segments.name: Bosch Ltd - power solutions and aftermarket
segments.commentary: Retains powertrain/propulsion and mobility aftermarket. Management said the portfolios are complementary with no overlap. Bosch Automotive Electronics (captive contract manufacturer, low margin, high capex) is excluded from this deal and is under review.

guidance_outlook: Synergies not counted in the business case; post-merger integration of about 6-12 months to follow closing.
Target to complete acquisition by end of Q1 FY27, subject to shareholder approval.
Management expects to hold margins steady for about 5 years and to fund all major OEM projects through their 2031 launches.
Capex for the target guided at about 1.5%-3.5% of net sales in the business case; no firm capex figure given.
Dividend distribution policy of 55%-85% of PAT reiterated.
capex_capacity: Target's main plant is in Chakan; a large plant in Jharkhand; Manesar is an assembly unit and Sanand a warehouse, with management saying the current capacity is near max in its current locations.
Expansion is mostly brownfield, using idle lines from the Bosch global network (second-hand, pre-run lines) for faster ramp-up.
Each e-axle line produces about 150,000 units; the e-axle market is small in India and the 50:50 JV with Tata Autocomp is intended to consolidate volumes.
Management says it will add capacity only against legislation or confirmed OEM programmes.
demand_pricing: Management said the order book is very full, with a project pipeline for 4-5 years, and that no orders have been lost so far.
Two-wheeler ABS: management says Bosch holds a very high, market-leading share; a below-125cc ABS mandate is still under consideration with no new update.
Margins expected to face some pressure from OEMs wanting customized solutions and from cost-down pressure in ABS for the 2-wheeler segment, but management expects to hold margins steady.
Management said it is the market leader in passenger car ABS/ESP and the most advanced ESP is 10th generation.
Localization is over 90% of child parts for some Bosch Ltd products, according to management.

qa_highlights.question: Why was RBIC chosen now, and why not Bosch Automotive Electronics (related-party exposure)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said RBIC is powertrain-agnostic and margin-accretive from day one. The automotive electronics entity is a captive, low-margin, capex-heavy contract manufacturer and is excluded for now but under ongoing review.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue mix and synergies?
qa_highlights.answer: Roughly one-third two-wheeler and the rest cars and commercial vehicles. No synergies counted in the business case; they will be reviewed in post-merger integration.

qa_highlights.question: Reason for the margin jump (gross margin from ~34% to ~40%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited scale, localization of products and child parts, legislation-led volume, modular platforms, and idle lines transferred from the Bosch network, with stable quality and productivity.

qa_highlights.question: Why was a preferential issue of only about INR8.8 crore disclosed and not the acquisition?
qa_highlights.answer: The company secretary said the announcement covered only the preferential issue and that the acquisition details were UPSI before the board meeting. The questioner challenged the disclosure, and management said it would improve governance practice.

qa_highlights.question: Cash, funding and balance sheet after deal?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the cash consideration is covered and both companies will be debt-free post-deal. The company did not disclose the target's H1 cash flow.

qa_highlights.question: Order book at RBIC?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described the order book as very full, with a 4-5 year project pipeline and good market share in all categories.

risks_watch: Related-party transaction exposure is rising: Bosch Automotive Electronics supplies to both entities on a cost-plus transfer price basis, and royalty terms are described as 'very similar'.
Governance: questions were raised on the adequacy of the April 1, 2026 board-meeting intimation, and the company was asked to improve disclosure.
Shareholder approval through the voting window ending May 8, 2026, and completion targeted by end-Q1 FY27.
Management views on the 2-wheeler ABS mandate for sub-125cc bikes remain unconfirmed; the deal business case excludes unlegislated upside.
Margin pressure in ABS for 2-wheelers and from Chinese competitors; the transfer price and cost-based structure will need monitoring post-close.
RBIC cash flow and capex figures were not disclosed; the cash flow figures stated as of 9M FY26 are unconfirmed.
500530|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on strategic rationale and margins, but evasive on segment splits, the target's H1 cash flow, capex figures and disclosure timing; several answers were deferred to post-closing site visits.
key_quotes: So, we are very positive that this will do well for Bosch Limited and thank you for your interest and good questions today.
We believe at Bosch Limited this is a great synergy of integrating this company.
We believe we will hold margins very steady for the next 5 years or so.
And we have a completely captive, the largest captive engineering center of any auto company in India, close to 22,000 people work in that company

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Pro forma FY25 EBITDA margin rises from 12.8% to 13.9% on RBIC's 19.3% margin, and management guides margins steady for ~5 years, though it flags ABS cost-down and OEM customisation pressure.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Brownfield expansion using idle pre-run Bosch lines at Chakan and a large Jharkhand plant is referenced, but no capacity numbers or dates were given and management will add capacity only against legislation or confirmed OEM programmes.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Order book is 'very full' with a 4-5 year project pipeline and no orders lost, and RBIC revenue grew from INR2,900 crore in FY23 to INR4,000 crore in FY25 (17% CAGR) with 9M FY26 at INR3,500 crore.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management says 'our lines are full' and the target's business case assumes capex of 1.5%-3.5% of net sales, but no firm capex figure was given and the target's current capacity is said to be near max at its locations.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Pro forma FY25 revenue rises about 22% to INR22,000 crore and EPS accretion is ~5%, but this is inorganic, synergies are excluded from the business case, and no organic guidance was given.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management flags margin pressure from 2-wheeler ABS cost-down and Chinese competition, and RBIC cash flow and capex figures remain undisclosed, so a downside surprise is possible.

rows.label: RBIC acquisition closing by end-Q1 FY27
rows.why: Shareholder voting runs to May 8, 2026 and management targets completion by end-Q1 FY27 for INR9,068.7 crore at ~10.6x FY25 EV/EBITDA, almost all cash.

rows.label: Both companies debt-free post-deal
rows.why: Management said the cash consideration is covered from existing funds and internal accruals and both companies will be debt-free after the deal.

rows.label: Sub-125cc two-wheeler ABS mandate
rows.why: Still under consideration with no update; management says the deal business case excludes unlegislated upside, so it would be pure upside if mandated.

tone.note: Management was confident on the strategic fit, margin stability and a very full order book, but evasive on RBIC's H1 cash flow, capex figures and disclosure timing; analysts pressed on related-party exposure and the governance of the board-meeting intimation.

500530|2026-06.headline: Bosch Ltd Q1 FY27 revenue rose 22% YoY to INR58,419 million and EBITDA rose 28% to INR8,180 million, with EBITDA margin near 14%.
500530|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations reached INR58,419 million, up 22% YoY and 5% QoQ, led by Power Solutions and 2-wheeler Powersports. EBITDA was INR8,180 million (up 28% YoY, 4.7% QoQ), and management attributed the margin gain to revenue growth and expense optimisation. Reported PAT of INR7,018 million fell 37.1% YoY because the prior year included an exceptional gain on sale of video solutions and access/intrusion businesses; excluding it, PAT grew 9.9%. Management said the Chassis Systems acquisition was completed in July and consolidation starts this quarter.

financial_highlights.change: -37.1% YoY reported (prior year had exceptional gain); +9.9% YoY excluding exceptional; +23.4% QoQ

segments.name: Power Solutions
segments.commentary: Grew 29% YoY, outperforming the broader auto market across passenger cars, commercial vehicles, off-highway and tractors; management attributed this mainly to volume and recent new introductions.

segments.name: Mobility Aftermarket
segments.commentary: Grew 9.6% YoY and 8.7% QoQ, driven by lubricants, batteries, spark plugs and braking systems; independent aftermarket recorded its highest-ever monthly sales in June.

segments.name: 2-wheeler and Powersports
segments.commentary: Grew 41.4% YoY on value-added EMS products and premium motorcycle platforms; management said it gained market share and reported zero production disruptions.

segments.name: Consumer goods (Power Tools)
segments.commentary: Grew 20.9% YoY on tool demand and marketing campaigns, but declined 15.7% QoQ on seasonal factors.

guidance_outlook: Management expects 2-wheeler industry growth of about 8% next quarter, supported by festive demand, rural cash flows and infrastructure activity.
CAFE Phase 3 norms from April 2027 are expected to boost Power Solutions further; CV ADAS regulation starts October 2027.
Management said product mix should stay favourable through FY27 and that margin upward trend will be sustained, though it gave no numeric guidance.
Revenue from the e-axles JV with TACO is expected by late next year; JV order-book details to be shared in about a quarter.
Chassis Systems consolidated results start next quarter; FY26 segment sales breakup promised for the next call.
capex_capacity: Chassis Systems acquisition from a Bosch sister company was completed in July 2026; management sees minimal cost and synergy benefit and treats it as a powertrain-agnostic addition.
Management said no goodwill or amortisation arises from the Chassis acquisition.
JV with TACO (e-axles) to operate out of Nashik; JV with TSF Group (air systems) to operate out of Chennai; both still awaiting merger control clearances.
Investor meet planned at Chassis Systems plant in Chakan, Pune, in November 2026.
Localisation content is rising; management did not quantify the imports-from-parent share, which the annual report shows at about 53% of purchased goods.
demand_pricing: Passenger vehicle demand strong on SUV preference; HCV demand healthy despite a INR7.5 per litre diesel price increase; LCV and 3-wheeler demand robust; tractor demand resilient despite uneven monsoon.
Bosch said it outperformed market volume growth by a few percentage points.
Aftermarket turnaround attributed to strategic price positioning, new schemes, workshop programme expansion and launches such as Tulix LED lights, Prithvi HCV battery, and PC clutches and suspension.
Commodity prices rose sharply over recent quarters and have levelled off; management declined to give outlook.
Margin drivers cited: operational excellence, localisation, volume growth, productivity and favourable mix, with worldwide purchasing helping manage sourcing volatility.

qa_highlights.question: Is the aftermarket's return to high single-digit growth sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the aftermarket recovery follows strategy and go-to-market corrections, and expects sustained growth from a stronger portfolio and expanding workshop programme; no numbers given.

qa_highlights.question: Are the ~14% EBITDA margins sticky, and were there one-offs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited operational excellence, localisation, volume, productivity and favourable mix as sustained drivers; confirmed no one-offs in employee or other expenses.

qa_highlights.question: Will the share of sourcing from parent fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the rise reflects volume surge; localisation plans are on track and will be updated in coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Chassis acquisition accretive and what are the synergies?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said synergies are minimal, it is a profitable company with good projects for several years, and consolidated results start next quarter; FY26 sales breakup to follow.

qa_highlights.question: What share of revenue is from exports?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports are at about 8-8.5% of revenue and the aim is to keep increasing this share over the next couple of years.

qa_highlights.question: Is product mix favourable through FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes, the product mix is quite favourable through the year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the TACO and TSF JVs?
qa_highlights.answer: Both are in final stages of merger control clearance; the e-axles JV is expected to generate revenue by late next year, and order details to follow in about a quarter.

risks_watch: Commodity and currency volatility, geopolitical tensions in West Asia, and supply chain or logistics disruption remain open risks; management declined to guide on commodities.
Monsoon variability, potential El Nino and geopolitical tension are named as 2-wheeler demand downside risks.
Post-GST demand normalisation could arrive in one or two quarters, according to management.
Sourcing from the parent rising to about 53% of purchased goods; localisation progress to be tracked.
Timing of JV merger clearances and of CAFE Phase 3 and CV ADAS content opportunities; the CAFE content value was not disclosed.
Chassis Systems FY26 numbers and segment breakup not yet disclosed; consolidated impact to be assessed from next quarter.

500530|2026-09.headline: Bosch Ltd Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose 28.6% to INR61,641 mn and EBITDA 30.1% to INR8,028 mn, with H2 guided modest.
500530|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue for Jul-Sep 2026 was INR76,551 mn (up 28.2% YoY), with EBITDA of INR10,371 mn (up 23.2%), after including Bosch Chassis Systems India (RBIC) from 1 July 2026. Standalone EBITDA margin was about 13% in Q2 versus about 14% in the prior two quarters, as aluminium prices and a weaker rupee against the euro offset volume absorption. A one-time reversal of long-term service award provision (INR1,240 mn standalone, INR1,304 mn consolidated) sits in exceptional items and lifted reported PAT. Management guided to a more modest H2 on inflation, weak monsoon, tighter rates and a high base, and announced a 3:1 bonus issue and a split of INR10 shares into INR2 face value, subject to shareholder approval.

financial_highlights.change: -13.1% YoY; prior year included INR5,560 mn one-time gain on sale of Building Technologies businesses
-17.6% YoY; Q2 PAT +21.7% YoY incl. INR1,240 mn exceptional credit

segments.name: Mobility (standalone)
segments.commentary: Mobility grew 30.3% YoY in Q2 and 28% in H1, led by Powertrain Solutions, then two-wheeler and aftermarket. Consumer Goods (power tools) grew 17.1% in Q2 and 19% in H1.

segments.name: Powertrain Solutions
segments.commentary: Growth came from passenger cars, commercial vehicles and tractors in Q2. Management cites CAFE Phase 3 (effective April 2027) and CNG/ethanol/hybrid incentives as content-per-vehicle drivers.

segments.name: Two-Wheeler & Powersports
segments.commentary: Growth came from higher motorcycle production and value-added electronic functions. Electronic control modules passed 10 million cumulative units; ABS and engine management launched on a 160 cc motorcycle.

segments.name: Mobility Aftermarket
segments.commentary: Robust growth from OE spares, rotating machines, spark plugs, batteries and filters. Bosch workshop network crossed 5,000.

segments.name: RBIC (Bosch Chassis Systems India)
segments.commentary: Acquired 1 July 2026; FY26 revenue INR48,935 mn, EBITDA INR9,045 mn, PAT INR5,891 mn. Q2 EBITDA margin about 15.5% versus above 18% in FY26, hit by aluminium, ECU and forex costs and one-time ramp costs.

guidance_outlook: H2 FY27 expected to be modest; Q3 FY27 seen as flat to modest growth on a high prior-year base, per management.
Management expects RBIC margins to remain pressured for about one more quarter before recovering toward earlier levels, with some raw-material costs to be recovered.
Management says margins are on an upward track on an aggregated basis, though it declined to give a specific margin target.
Depreciation timing effect of INR77.5 crore in H1 FY26 at RBIC is expected to reverse in later quarters.
CAFE Phase 3 effective April 2027; content-per-vehicle uplift not quantified and deferred to a later call.
TACO joint venture (Nashik) to start production mid-FY28; TSF joint venture (Chennai) towards end-FY28.
capex_capacity: H1 FY27 capex about INR350 crore, against roughly INR300 crore a year over the last three years; spend is seasonal and heaviest in Q3.
Most capex goes to plant and machinery, mainly upgrading existing production lines to meet volume.
RBIC plants at Chakan (Pune), Sanand (Gujarat) and Manesar (Haryana); Chakan has passed 20 million cumulative active safety units.
RBIC added ABS10M capacity for two-wheelers and started production of ESP10 in H1, which carried one-time costs.
Chennai power tools plant passed 20 million cumulative units.
demand_pricing: Passenger vehicle demand strong on low base and SUV preference; HCV, LCV and three-wheeler demand also strong in Q2.
Tractor demand weakened late in Q2 on uneven monsoon, though tractors still grew in Q2 per management.
Raw material inflation (mainly aluminium and ECUs) and INR depreciation against the euro weighed on margins; pass-through is contractual with time lags and some customers push back.
Management says it is trying to recover the full cost increase but cannot yet predict 100% recovery.
FX is passed through under contract for most customers; one customer is negotiation-based.
Standalone exports about 8-9% of sales on average, with Bosch's global network guided at 5-15% export per plant.

qa_highlights.question: Why did RBIC margins fall sharply, and how do pass-through and FX recovery work?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume absorption is the main driver; aluminium and forex on imported parts are the key cost headwinds. Recovery is contractual with a time lag, and full recovery is not assured given customer pushback.

qa_highlights.question: How should H2 demand be expected to trend sequentially, given festive retail and tractor weakness?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed H2 will be modest, citing inflation, weak monsoon, rate tightening and a very high base. Q2 was a record quarter, so cyclicality is expected.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the INR1,240 mn exceptional reversal, and will it recur?
qa_highlights.answer: Bosch decided to stop the long-term service award globally. Eligible staff keep it until 31 December 2026, and the provision made for it is being reversed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the RBIC capex and high ROCE model based on?
qa_highlights.answer: Lines are largely relocated from other Bosch plants and built modularly with heavy reuse, so capex per line is low. Management says current generations will look similar, but new generations may differ.

qa_highlights.question: How much RBIC purchases come from group entities and in foreign currency?
qa_highlights.answer: ECUs come from sister plant Bosch Automotive Electronics and will continue. Localisation of other content is ongoing and expected to rise over time.

qa_highlights.question: Will the parent restructuring or the China-to-India sourcing shift affect Bosch Limited?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the parent's mobility division spin-off has no impact on Bosch Limited. India exports are about 8-9%, and any shift in sourcing is still being assessed with the parent.

risks_watch: Aluminium and ECU prices plus INR/EUR forex, with recovery lagging and not fully assured.
H2 FY27 demand softness in tractors and possibly other segments after a record Q2 and a high base.
Standalone EBITDA margin of about 13% in Q2 versus about 14% in prior quarters; management gave no numerical target.
RBIC EBITDA margin trajectory and whether the one-time ramp costs and depreciation timing reverse next quarter.
Revenue and EBITDA growth of 20-30% has not translated into PAT growth after one-time items.
Share bonus and split need shareholder approval; record date still to be set.
EV revenue salience and order book were not disclosed; the JV is still being set up.

500547|2026-09.headline: BPCL Q2 FY27 standalone PAT rose to INR4,993 crore from a Q1 loss of INR3,962 crore, despite Brent averaging about $116 in September.
500547|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 standalone PAT was INR4,993 crore against a Q1 standalone loss of INR3,962 crore, with revenue from operations of about INR1.5 lakh crore. Management attributed the recovery to agile crude sourcing, a Q2 refining GRM of $32.53/bbl (about $14 after SAED), and lower LPG under-recoveries, which fell to about INR290/cylinder from INR507. Standalone gross borrowings fell to INR15,246 crore and the debt-to-equity ratio improved to 0.16. Marketing under-recoveries on petrol and diesel were still a drag, and management said there was no further discussion on marketing margin improvement at this point.

segments.commentary: Domestic sales 13.47 MMT in Q2 vs 13.62 MMT in Q1. Outlets rose to 25,592 from 25,485. Speed 100 at 162 outlets; BeCafe at 234 locations. Marketing under-recoveries were a drag on Q2 earnings.

qa_highlights.question: Has the crude sourcing mix changed in October, and how is the mix through December?
qa_highlights.answer: Middle East volumes increased, including via Yanbu and ADNOC cargoes; Iraq and Kuwait not yet full. Russian volumes fell in November on freight and premiums, with a few December cargoes possible.

qa_highlights.question: Landed crude cost versus benchmark?

qa_highlights.question: Is any change to marketing margins being considered?
qa_highlights.answer: No further discussion on marketing margin improvement; monthly review of under-recoveries; integrated profitability is near normal levels.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q2 GRM fall vs Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Crude freight costs rose sharply and Russian discounts disappeared on some high-sulphur cargoes; gasoline and gasoil spreads were broadly flat versus Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR150 crore higher transport cost, INR150 crore higher octroi and taxes, and about INR1,200-1,300 crore MTM losses on hedges of forward spreads.

qa_highlights.question: Does FY28-29 capex include the Andhra Pradesh refinery?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Mozambique and Brazil are included; AP refinery will be added once FID is approved, with capex rework to follow.

Bina expansion progress and cost, with 20-25% of work yet to be awarded as of the earlier Q4 call.

500550|2026-03.headline: Siemens Ltd Q4 FY26 (March quarter): orders up 33% to ₹67.3bn and revenue up 14.6% to ₹46.2bn, but EBITDA margin fell 290bp to 9.7% on commodity and FX costs.
500550|2026-03.overview: Management reported strong order intake and revenue growth in the March 2026 quarter, with all three businesses growing revenue double digits. Profitability was hit by material costs rising to 74% of revenue from 69% in Q2, driven by a roughly 18% Euro depreciation against INR and sharp rises in silver and copper. Backlog reached ₹450bn, up 9.3%, including a ₹18bn export bogie order executable over 2029-2039. Management gave no quarterly margin guidance and said two price increases have been taken in DI and SI, with a 3-4 month lag before they flow through.

segments.name: Digital Industries
segments.commentary: Q4 orders ₹9.7bn (+1.4% YoY, book-to-bill 0.84); revenue ₹11.5bn (+14.35%); EBITDA margin 2.6% vs 5% a year ago. 6M orders ₹20.7bn (+17.1%); management said margin ex-FX would be about 6.8%.

segments.name: Smart Infrastructure
segments.commentary: Q4 orders ₹29.6bn (+17.6%, book-to-bill 1.15); revenue ₹25.8bn (+14.5%). 6M orders ₹60.6bn (+22.9%), revenue +11.6%, EBITDA margin 15.1% vs 16.2% (down 120bp) on commodity costs. Volumes grew 17.5% in Q4 and 23% in 6M.

segments.name: Mobility
segments.commentary: Q4 orders ₹28bn (+75%, book-to-bill 3.37) including the ₹18bn bogie export order; revenue ₹8.3bn (+12.7%) on 9K HP loco execution. Q4 EBIT margin 7.6% vs 7.2%; 6M EBITDA margin 6.4% vs 8.2%.

guidance_outlook: No quarterly margin guidance given; management said it cannot predict FX and commodity impact and will report it transparently.
Price increases: one taken before March and one after March, each with a 3-4 month lag; SI short-cycle LV products expected to return to aspired margin levels once price hikes stick.
Locomotive programme: 80 locos a year in FY26 and FY27, 100 a year in 2028-30, 160 a year in 2030-35; 40 delivered and paid by 31 March 2026, with 90%+ localisation.
Low-voltage motors business sale on track for completion in June 2026.
Management expects 0.5-1% GDP uplift over the next couple of years from the India-EU FTA; import costs in some segments to fall.
Locomotive margins are blended (O&M plus delivery) on percentage-of-completion; management said percentage margins on the next 80 locos should be similar, with absolute values scaling with volume.
capex_capacity: Medium-voltage and vacuum interrupter plant in Goa is nearing completion and should reach commercial production soon.
Mobility factories in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (bogies) and Nashik (propulsion and bogie electrics) under review for expansion, given the ₹18bn export order and pipeline; to be updated later.
Bogie order executes over 2029-2039 as product deliveries, not a project.
SI is 70-75% localised; DI localisation not viable at current volumes given PLC minimum volume needs; no capex quantum disclosed for the next 2-3 years.

Material costs rose to 74% of revenue in Q4 from 69% in Q2; silver up 160% and copper up 45% in USD terms between Q2 and Q4.
Cash flow weaker on inventory build due to West Asia crisis and higher receivables and contract assets in Mobility; management said overdues are stable.

qa_highlights.question: Will DI and SI margins hold at current levels for a few quarters, and will they improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no guidance; underlying margins are said to be strong, and DI and SI contracts are short-term with no long-term fixed prices, so impacts are short-term.

qa_highlights.question: Is the bogie order adequately protected against price increases?
qa_highlights.answer: Wolfgang Wrumnig said the locomotive and bogie orders have price variation clauses with an index and the company is adequately covered, with some residual risk. Management would not disclose the value after adjustments.

qa_highlights.question: Why did DI orders decline YoY in Q4 and what is the domestic inflow outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the flat DI orders to a price increase at the start of Q4 that pulled orders into Q3. The CFO said the 6M DI growth of 17% is more representative, and railway orders should be read on a half-yearly basis.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a risk that government ordering softens given fiscal pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no slowdown is visible in power utilities (mainly state government) or railways. The 24,000 km of signalling is already ordered, with the rest expected by end of next year.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar and Nashik factories be expanded?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is examining expansion for both factories given the backlog and pipeline and will update later. Metro rolling stock capacity decisions remain open.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q4 locomotive delivery impact on revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 40 locos were delivered in Q4 only, and that revenue and margin recognition follows percentage-of-completion on cost inflow, not on the delivery count.

500570|2026-03.headline: Tata Motors PV FY26 volumes hit a record 6.42 lakh units (+15% YoY); JLR full-year EBIT only 0.7%, with Rs 4,100 Cr of exceptionals.
500570|2026-03.overview: India PV business recovered strongly in H2 after a muted H1, with Q4 offtake above 2 lakh units (+37% YoY) and the company ranked number two on Vahan with over 14% share. Consolidated revenue for Q4 was about Rs 105,000 Cr (+7% YoY), with PBT before exceptionals of Rs 7,200 Cr, while full-year PBT of Rs 2,500 Cr excluded about Rs 4,100 Cr of exceptionals (cyber, labour code, demerger stamp duty). JLR delivered 95,000 Q4 wholesales and 9.2% EBIT, but full-year EBIT was 0.7% and management called the full-year performance far from intended. Management flagged commodity headwinds of 5-6% of revenue over 9-12 months and a Middle East demand hit in Q1, with guidance deferred to the June investor days.

qa_highlights.question: What is the size of the commodity headwind, and how will it be passed on?

qa_highlights.question: What is the Range Rover EV launch timing and pre-bookings?

qa_highlights.question: How is JLR planning to reduce its breakeven volume to 300,000?

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected FY27 industry growth and TMPV's supply situation?

500570|2026-06.headline: TMPV Q1 FY27: India volumes up 46% to 182,000 units, but 4.5% commodity hit held India EBITDA at about 4%; JLR PBT fell to GBP 109 million.
500570|2026-06.overview: Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles (formerly Tata Motors) posted Q1 FY27 revenue of Rs 95,800 Cr, EBIT margin of 2.4% and PBT of Rs 1,600 Cr, down year on year. JLR wholesales fell about 10% (around 8,000 units) on Jaguar run-out, a supplier fire at Solihull and Middle East disruption, with JLR PBT at GBP 109 million versus GBP 351 million last year. India wholesales rose 46% to about 182,000 units and share rose 200 bps to 14.3%, but a 4.5% commodity hit in Q1 offset fixed-cost leverage and material savings, holding EBITDA margin at about 4%. Management says FY27 guidance for JLR is not changed.

segments.commentary: Wholesales about 182,000 units, up 46% YoY vs industry +24%; market share 14.3%, up 200 bps; firm #2 on registrations. EV volumes over 34,000 units (about 20% of sales), with July EV volume above 15,000 and EV share 43%.

segments.name: JLR
segments.commentary: Wholesales down about 10% YoY (about 8,000 units, around 3,000 below internal plan). Defender up YoY; Range Rover and Range Rover Sport hit by a chassis supplier fire early in the quarter. Retail down 14.5K YoY, with over 5,000 from Jaguar run-out and Middle East. China wholesales down 25%.

TMPV targets higher double-digit volume growth in FY27 and 10% revenue growth per annum at group level.
Group targets $1.7 billion of cost savings across ex-works cost, warranty and fixed costs; detail promised with Q2 results.

India: Q2 commodity hit of about 3% expected; margins expected flattish vs Q1 after 0.5% July price increase, accelerated cost reduction (1.5% in Q1) and 1% IPL benefit; margin step-up expected in H2 as PLI accrues from Q3.
JLR expects about 12,000 EVs in FY27 (tentative); Type 01 and Range Rover GT impact mainly FY28.
India exports targeted at about 2x FY26 levels in FY27.

demand_pricing: India volumes run-rate has consistently exceeded 60,000 a month vs earlier 45,000-50,000; EV mix 19% in Q1, 23% exit June, 24% in July.

EV bookings about 3.5x pre-Middle East crisis (Jan-Feb) levels; supply far below demand.
JLR China wholesales down 25%; management expects China to get worse before stabilising, citing retrospective taxes and luxury tax changes.
JLR VME (variable marketing expense) rose to 7.1%; JLR average transaction price trending up, targeting above GBP 80,000 per car in about 18 months.
JLR aluminium fell from about $3,500/t end-March to about $3,150/t end-June; some contracts reset quarterly, so Q2 may see extra raw material hit.
Industry PV volumes exceeded 1.3 million units, up 24% YoY; industry growth expected to moderate in H2 on higher base.

qa_highlights.question: Are JLR's Q1 temporary issues behind us and what is the volume recovery and Type 01 ramp plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Jaguar wholesales of about 1,500 units lower QoQ are being run out over 3-6 months; Type 01 production starts early next year with impact in FY28, not FY27. The Solihull supplier fire is fully resolved.

qa_highlights.question: Why only 1% price increase despite strong raw material headwinds?
qa_highlights.answer: Pricing is benchmarked against competitors to protect competitiveness; more frequent, progressive increases will follow as cost reductions allow, avoiding a steep single hike.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 volume and margin outlook for India?
qa_highlights.answer: Targeting higher double-digit volume growth in FY27; margins to be neutralised through a mix of price increases and cost reduction.

qa_highlights.question: Will JLR localise production in the US?
qa_highlights.answer: Not localising existing models given volume scale; MoU with Stellantis for new US-specific vehicles (Defender brand), with a definitive agreement targeted by year end.

qa_highlights.question: How does rising EV mix affect JLR margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects BEV Range Rover models to be at least margin neutral and not discounted; the EMA cars replace low-margin models so should be neutral to accretive.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Sierra supply outlook for the festive season?
qa_highlights.answer: Engine casting and sheet-metal constraints are easing over the next two months, with major capacity additions from October.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q2 margin outlook after the 3% commodity hit?
qa_highlights.answer: Net of price increase, cost reduction and the absence of Q1's 1% IPL seasonal impact, Q2 margins are expected to be flattish vs Q1.

qa_highlights.question: What JLR EV volume is expected in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Tentatively about 12,000 EVs in FY27, starting with Range Rover Electric production in September.

Commodity inflation: about 3% further hit in Q2 from quarterly contract resets; PLI certification for most models only from Q3-Q4.

Middle East disruption and Strait of Hormuz routing affecting retail and wholesale; Q1 MENA retail down about 1,400 units.
