500570|2026-09.headline: Tata Motors PV Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue ~₹96,000–97,000 crore (+34% YoY) with EBIT margin 1.1%; JLR cut FY27 EBIT guidance to 2–3%.
500570|2026-09.overview: Consolidated TMPV revenue rose about 34% YoY to roughly ₹96,000–97,000 crore, with EBITDA margin 6.2% and EBIT margin 1.1%, down from 2.4% in Q1 on adverse JLR mix and commodity pressure in India. Exceptional charges of ₹6,700 crore were booked in the quarter for JLR restructuring. Domestic volumes hit a record 67,000 units a month average with 14.3% Vahan share, while EVs reached a record ~16,000 units a month with 43% share. JLR sold 82,000 units at £5.9 billion revenue, flat QoQ, but PBT fell to £6 million on China and MENA weakness and mix; FY27 JLR guidance was lowered.

qa_highlights.question: Why did JLR cut guidance and what is the China plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the cut to China and mix; China plans to be updated next quarter, with JLR staying invested and watching the market closely.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving JLR cash turnaround and investment decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Investment peak from five launches (£11.5 billion spent of £15–18 billion programme) will decline over 18–24 months; EBITDA to rise as new vehicles launch.

qa_highlights.question: Cost savings and voluntary redundancy?
qa_highlights.answer: About 4,000 headcount reduction with ~3,000 leaving this FY; ~£400 million per year of ongoing savings, not all in P&L as some engineering roles are capitalised; £530 million restructuring charge in Q2 (£295 million VRS).

500575|2026-03.headline: Voltas Q4 FY26 consolidated PBT fell to INR 181 crores from INR 343 crores as UCP margins were hit by commodity inflation and rupee depreciation.
500575|2026-03.overview: Consolidated total income rose marginally to INR 4,930 crores in Q4 FY26 from INR 4,847 crores, but PBT fell to INR 181 crores and net profit to INR 113 crores from INR 343 crores and INR 236 crores. For FY26, total income fell to INR 14,483 crores from INR 15,737 crores, PBT to INR 557 crores from INR 1,191 crores, and net profit to INR 377 crores from INR 834 crores. Management said March 2026 was a record sales month and April was close to that level, but margins were compressed by old-cost inventory, FX losses and commodity inflation, with price hikes only partly passed through so far.

segments.name: Segment A - UCP (RAC, CAC, CR, AR, Voltbek)
segments.commentary: FY26 RAC volume was 2.25 million units; Voltas leads the No. 2 player by a 5.1% primary market share gap. Margins were hit in Q1-Q2 by channel overhang and in Q4 by commodity inflation and rupee depreciation. Chennai plant utilisation is ~1.2 lakh units/month against 1.5 million units annual capacity.

segments.name: Voltbek (within Segment A)
segments.commentary: Year-to-date market share of 8.6% in washing machines and 6.2% in refrigerators in a sluggish market. Sanand plant localisation is ongoing and management expects margin expansion over the medium term.

segments.name: Segment B - Electro-Mechanical Projects (MEP)
segments.commentary: Order book close to INR 6,200 crores at 31 March 2026, of which ~INR 4,500 crores is domestic. Management says 40-50% of the India MEP book and some international contracts carry price variation clauses, so commodity and labour inflation is passed through. No client has invoked force majeure; Qatar force majeure was revoked.

segments.name: Segment C - Mining, Construction & Textile Machinery
segments.commentary: Mining and construction equipment showed steady top-line growth, supported by crushing and screening demand and Mozambique operations. Textile machinery was weak amid cautious capex sentiment, with management pinning hopes on Union Budget 2026 and PLI support for spinning recovery.

guidance_outlook: UCP margins: management said the target is a gradual step-up towards FY25 levels (UCP margin ~8.4% in FY25 vs ~3.2% in FY26, per analyst); no firm FY27 margin number given, and no timeline for returning to FY25 levels.
Q4 FY26 margins: management said it is not expecting any sharp downturn in margin profile for the quarter (Q1 FY27), with costs hitting progressively as a mix of pre-war and post-war costs.

Pricing: further price increases are planned, depending on rupee-dollar, war and commodity moves; management said it is watching prices almost weekly and sees double-digit inflation, to be passed through as costs hit. Pass-through expected for most brands.

Demand: industry RAC expected to grow at least 15-20% in FY27 off a weak FY26 base (industry FY26 degrowth ~10-12%, 14.3 million primary units); commercial refrigeration expected to grow upwards of 10%; commercial AC expected to grow 12-15%.
Medium-term: Voltbek expected to steadily improve brand preference, penetration and operating leverage over the medium term; management expects margin expansion at Sanand over time.

Capacity and capex: small capex to lift Chennai from 1.5 million to 2 million units is ready; third investment round deferred 1-2 years until demand is visible. Capex focus remains on Segment A (capacity, R&D, CAC).
capex_capacity: Chennai plant built to 1.5 million units capacity (up from 1 million last year), running at about 1.2 lakh units per month; a small capex to take it to 2 million units is ready, with the third investment round deferred 1-2 years until demand is visible.
Pantnagar and Chennai facilities running at higher utilisation than last year.
Ongoing capex in factory automation, warehouse rationalisation and integrated inventory planning.
Capex is mostly directed at Segment A (capacity and R&D); CAC is a key area for capex deployment.
Sanand plant localisation and scale-up for Voltbek is in progress.
demand_pricing: Price hikes: new BEE table products (from March) carried 5% on 3-star (~75% mix) and 10% on 5-star (~25% mix), a blended ~6-7%, plus a further 1-2% (copper) and another increase in the latest month, linked to rupee depreciation.
GST on RAC cut from 28% to 18% cushions consumer affordability this summer versus last year.
Channel inventory is under 45 days and closer to 30 days, per management.
March 2026 was a record sales month in company history; April was close to that level and May is tracking well. Secondary sales are picking up as the higher-priced stock is absorbed.

500620|2026-06.headline: GE Shipping posted record Q1 FY27 consolidated profit of INR 1,309 crore (standalone INR 1,157 crore), with ~INR 91-92/share EPS and a INR 14.40 interim dividend.
500620|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as the company's most profitable quarter ever by a significant margin, driven by Strait of Hormuz disruption that pushed tanker freight rates and asset prices to record levels. Standalone NAV rose about INR 100/share to ~INR 1,512 and consolidated NAV is just under INR 1,900/share, with the stock trading at about a 25% discount. The company announced its 18th consecutive interim dividend of INR 14.40/share, its highest quarterly payout. Management said it remains predominantly on the spot market (about 25-26% of capacity on time charter), is net cash, and is holding most cash rather than buying ships at peak prices.

segments.name: Dry bulk
segments.commentary: Bulk earnings were marginally better than a year ago. Coal demand rose as LNG disruption pushed power plants to coal, and grain trade was strong. Bulk carrier rates are marginally higher than in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Why not deploy incremental cash into ships given strong freight?

qa_highlights.question: What fuel and earnings savings come from newer ships?

qa_highlights.question: Status of the Hormuz-exposed ships and the idle rig?

500620|2026-09.headline: GE Shipping FY21 standalone reported net profit Rs1,030 crore; normalized Rs842 crore (EPS ~Rs57), dividend Rs9/share.

Standalone NAV rose to Rs489/share from Rs454 a year earlier, while the market-value NAV range moved to Rs514-562 from Rs488-530. Global price positioning: architectural products now at 85-120% of global peers, up from 30-40% earlier.
Architectural: raised prices and added products; EBITDA margin on top SCF products 40-45%, mid-range SCF 30-35%, PPF 20-25%.

Tariff reversal: INR31 crore received to date (INR20 crore refunded to customers, INR11 crore booked); a further ~INR30 crore expected in Q3 (INR16 crore to books, INR14 crore to customers). Reported by reducing COGS and sales.

qa_highlights.question: Peak revenue potential from existing capacity, and the product mix behind it?

qa_highlights.question: Customer concentration (reported as 30%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Concentration exists, with one large EV customer in the US under long-term agreement; management says growth is spread across teams and that this customer does not buy architectural films.

qa_highlights.question: Crude sensitivity and the revenue impact at USD60 crude?
qa_highlights.answer: At USD100-110 crude, management said it passes through costs with a lag. Revenue would have been about INR650-660 crore instead of INR700 crore at USD60, with the lower-crude benefit mainly on the 25% crude-linked IPD business.

qa_highlights.question: Lubrizol tie-up structure and incremental top line?

qa_highlights.question: Dividend policy?

500660|2026-06.headline: GSK Pharma Q1 FY27 standalone sales rose 15% to INR924 crore and PAT 24% to INR253 crore, with growth led by innovation at 7% of sales.
500660|2026-06.overview: Standalone sales grew 15% YoY to INR924 crore, with EBITDA up 17% and EBITDA margin up 50 bps, and PAT up 24% to INR253 crore (27.6% margin). Management said about 4-5 percentage points of headline growth came from a soft base after last year's CMO supply disruption, so underlying growth was about 9-10%. Innovation products (IP-protected) reached 7% of sales versus about 4% a year ago, contributing about 4 points of growth. PAT growth included a one-off dividend from subsidiary Biddle Sawyer; excluding it, PAT growth was about 17%. Spend-to-sales rose about 1 percentage point on front-loaded promotional investment ahead of the September quarter.

financial_highlights.value: improved ~50 bps YoY (management expects ~34% range for year)

financial_highlights.change: driven by pricing and product mix
vs ~4% last year; ~4 pts of headline growth

segments.name: General medicines (Gen Med)
segments.commentary: Grew in double digits and most brands outgrew the market per IQVIA, with EIs of 105-106. About 44-45% of the Gen Med portfolio is under price control. Gen Med is about 2,000 field staff.

segments.name: Vaccines
segments.commentary: Held private-segment leadership in pediatric vaccines. Shingrix grew about 65% in Q1, sells about 45,000-50,000 doses per quarter, and crossed INR100 crore on a MAT basis. A phasing issue in availability for a couple of vaccines is to be corrected in Q2.

segments.name: Specialty (respiratory, oncology)
segments.commentary: Nucala has about 600 active patients, with new patient starts roughly doubling YoY to about 100-120 a month. Trelegy Ellipta holds about 10,000-12,000 units a month despite about 10-12 generic launches of umeclidinium. Zejula and Jemperli together treat about 250-300 patients a quarter.

guidance_outlook: Management does not give formal guidance; the stated objective is sustaining double-digit growth.
Opex/investment ratios expected to moderate in following quarters; S&A ratio to normalise toward historical levels through the year.
EBITDA margin expected to be roughly in the 34% range, similar to last year.
Q2 seasonal acute trends were said to be tracking in line with expectations, with June and July data supportive.
Blenrep (belantamab mafodotin, second-line RRMM) launch expected in Q2 or Q3 FY27 after DCGI approval.
Bepirovirsen (Hibsago) launch in India expected within three to four quarters.
Arexvy launch and upcoming Ojjaara expected within roughly 18-24 months.
Long-term ambition of INR8,000 crore top line in four to five years; established portfolio to grow 8-10%, with new launches providing the rest of the ~13% CAGR.
capex_capacity: Manufacturing is local-for-local: own plant at Nashik (MIDC) plus about 20 contract manufacturers; all Gen Med products are made locally. Management sees no need for further local manufacturing beyond the current portfolio.

Field force of about 2,000 in Gen Med and 200 in established vaccines; about 40-45 people in oncology (medical oncology and hematology), with new hiring focused on areas of little or no presence such as liver disease.
Blended productivity about INR15-16 lakh per rep, up 5-6% this quarter.
demand_pricing: Industry Q1 growth was about 13.5%, with volume growth around 2%; oncology was the fastest-growing Indian pharma segment at about 27%.
GSK Q1 blended volume growth was about 3-3.5%, price about 6%, and the balance from new introductions.
Acute therapies are about 60% of the Indian pharma market; Q2 (July-September) is the seasonal peak.
Supply chain: management said the worst is behind, after the CMO disruption, and that cost hardening on imported inputs from rupee depreciation has not yet hit margins.
Zejula is among the top five PARP inhibitors; Jemperli is the only approved immunotherapy in first-line endometrial cancer, which has about 17,000-19,000 new diagnoses a year.

qa_highlights.question: Does the parent's restructuring focused on specialty hurt growth and India investment, given the Gen Med-heavy portfolio?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Gen Med still grows in double digits and the parent's cost programme is a simplification effort; India was already restructured, and global trials are being brought to India to shorten launch lags.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the CMO-related lost Calpol sales have been recouped?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the worst is behind, the supply chain has been stress-tested, and business continuity plans are being strengthened. It did not quantify recovery.

qa_highlights.question: How is reach into Tier 3/4 and rural areas ensured, given peers' distributor models?
qa_highlights.answer: A super-distributor manages some tail-end brands to reach mofussil interiors; no new operating model details were given beyond this.

qa_highlights.question: What are trends for the seasonal acute Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Trends since June are tracking in line with expectations; management expects Q2 broadly in line with its plan.

qa_highlights.question: Is the opex spike a one-off, and how should EBITDA margins be viewed?
qa_highlights.answer: Spend was deliberately front-loaded ahead of the September quarter (about 3,800 HCP events); ratios should moderate, and EBITDA margins are expected around 34%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook on Blenrep and Bepirovirsen commercialisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Blenrep approved by DCGI for second-line RRMM, launch Q2 or Q3 FY27 (about 7,000-8,000 second-line patients). Bepirovirsen launch in three to four quarters; pricing model still being worked out.

500670|2026-03.headline: GNFC posted FY26 PAT of INR797 crore (up 35%) on PBT of INR1,065 crore, with Q4 revenue up 11% QoQ and 7% YoY on better chemical realisations.
500670|2026-03.overview: Management attributed the quarter's improvement mainly to higher chemical realisations, with Q4 realisations up sequentially across all products except formic acid (range 6% to 28%). Full-year profit was helped by lower raw material prices, while one-time income rose to about INR80 crore in FY26 from about INR38 crore a year earlier. Fertilizer remained loss-making because urea fixed cost and energy norm revisions are still pending. Management declared a dividend of INR21 per share (210%) and guided FY27 capex to about INR2,800 crore.

About INR80 crore (vs about INR38 crore in FY25)

financial_highlights.change: Second highest in company history per management

Net reduction of about INR3,000 per MT QoQ in Q4

segments.name: Chemicals
segments.commentary: Q4 realisations rose sequentially for all products except formic acid, with product-level increases of 6% to 28%. Acetic acid volumes were capped by internal constraints and methanol production was uneconomic at current gas prices. TDI ran at about 80%, and aniline is run mainly as job work because it is not viable standalone.

segments.name: Fertilizer
segments.commentary: Urea is under-recovering because fixed cost and energy norm revisions are pending; management sees almost no chance of urea turning positive until norms are revised. Complex fertilizers are priced on nutrient-based contribution. Urea production exceeded 210,000 MT in FY26 against a 637,000 MT urea reassessed capacity, with TGU making up the balance.

segments.name: Other (IT division)
segments.commentary: Revenue up about 20% and profit doubled from INR17 crore to INR35 crore.

Coal-based CCPP synchronisation revised to third week of June 2026, with performance guarantee test by third week of August 2026. Expected savings of INR10-12 crore per month, with PAT accrual from H2 FY27.

TDI prices remunerative in Q4 and softened but still better in Q1 per management.

qa_highlights.question: Availability and cost roadmap for oil, methanol, benzene and toluene for Q1-Q2 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Oil supply from IOCL has been uninterrupted through the Hormuz disruption; Q4 oil cost fell about INR3,000/MT QoQ. Q1-Q2 outlook is not guided given volatility. Methanol is uneconomic at high gas prices, so GNFC toggles between own methanol/acetic acid and buying acetic acid for ethyl acetate.

qa_highlights.question: What is the TGU situation and capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: TGU was raised sharply after the war started to meet OEM and logistics needs, with production doubled in March. Urea production exceeded 210,000 MT in FY26; the 169,000 MT TGU figure is an average capacity that depends on shutdown timing.

qa_highlights.question: Which products drove the Q3 to Q4 EBITDA improvement of about INR300 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: In order: TDI, ammonium nitrate and technical grade urea.

qa_highlights.question: What is the one-time income breakdown?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 one-timers about INR30 crore; FY26 about INR80 crore vs INR38 crore in FY25. Components include insurance receipts (about INR28 crore), urea freight escalation settlement (about INR15 crore), catalyst dust sale and CCPP delay penalty recovery.

qa_highlights.question: What is the INR2,400 crore loan and advances balance?
qa_highlights.answer: Surplus funds are parked in higher-yield inter-corporate deposits to PSU entities (about 7.25% yield) until the capex cycle completes; management said private sector lending is not permitted under governance policy.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a buyback plan and what is the FY27 capex?
qa_highlights.answer: No buyback is in the pipeline. FY27 capex is about INR2,800 crore; FY28 to be shared in coming quarters.

500670|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 profit described as second highest in company history after Q1 FY22, driven by better realisations despite lower sales volumes.
500670|2026-06.overview: Management said Q1 was shaped by Middle East war escalation and de-escalation, which caused viability-driven shutdowns at acetic acid, ethyl acetate and TDI but lifted realisations. Sales volumes fell well below production, and inventory built up to 30 June was about 15% liquidated by end-July. Fertilizer segment profit rose to about INR85 crores from about INR24 crores, with urea contributing about INR48 crores and ANP about INR12 crores. Management gave no formal quarterly guidance, and several questions on forward realisations and savings went unanswered.

500670|2026-09.headline: GNFC Q2 FY27: management cited a ~INR 200 crore sequential operating profit drop; one-time net impact of ~INR 75 crore; cash and deposits ~INR 3,900 crore.
500670|2026-09.overview: Management described a year-on-year improvement but a sequential margin squeeze in Q2 FY27, driven by realisation erosion in WNA, TGU and AN Melt, higher coal-linked fuel cost, and a wage settlement provision. Net one-time impacts were about INR 75 crore, which management said would have made the quarter INR 75 crore higher without them. H1 capex was about INR 500 crore, the captive coal-based steam plant is operational, and working capital rose on subsidy receivables. Management declined to comment on Q3 trends or current prices, citing price-sensitive information rules, so forward visibility was limited.

500672|2026-06.headline: Novartis India targets doubling revenue in 4-5 years; run-rate ~INR650 crore for FY27, with incremental quarterly costs of INR40-50 crore from next quarter.
500672|2026-06.overview: Management held its first investor meet after the ChrysCapital-led takeover, presenting a commercial reset: bringing promotion in-house, building a ~900-MR field force targeting ~150,000 HCPs, and focusing on six therapy areas. Two bolt-on deals were closed in the first ~45 days: the Minipress XL trademark from Pfizer (cardiology, MAT July 2026 sales INR228 crore) and the in-licensing of ophthalmology brands Pagenax and Accentrix from NHPL. Near-term costs rise sharply, with margin expected to dip before recovering to above 20% in two to three years. Historical revenue was flat over the last four years. Management gave no quantified Dr. Reddy's termination-fee impact and no specifics on fund-raising for the Minipress debt.

500672|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 revenue fell to INR56 crore from INR90 crore as Evonile moved off single-customer model; INR83 crore one-time items booked.
500672|2026-09.overview: Evonile Pharma (formerly Novartis India) reported its first results call after change of control, with Q2 FY27 revenue from operations of INR56 crore versus INR90 crore a year earlier, including INR41 crore from a major customer in the base period. Management attributed the decline to a one-time revenue correction and transition effects, not to weaker underlying demand. Adjusted operating EBITDA was negative INR16 crore for the quarter (INR19 crore for H1), with employee costs up to INR14 crore from INR5 crore as own field force and corporate team were built. Reported results include INR83 crore of one-time items: a INR68 crore exceptional item (INR61 crore from terminating exclusive promotion rights and inventory purchase arrangements with one large customer) and about INR15 crore of transition and Minipress XL acquisition costs within other expenses.

segments.name: Minipress XL (cardiology, acquired from Pfizer)
segments.commentary: Market-leading cardiology brand with more than 50% market share, acquired in the quarter. Market grew about 9% historically versus about 6% for the brand; about 300 of the planned 900 MRs are allocated to it.

segments.name: Ophthalmology (Accentrix and Pagenax, in-licensed)
segments.commentary: Exclusive distribution and promotion agreement signed in the quarter for a retina portfolio, adding ophthalmology to six priority therapies (cardiology, pain management, wellness, transplant, gynecology, neurosciences).

segments.name: Legacy brands (Voveran, Methergene, Calcium Sandoz, myFORTic)
segments.commentary: Management says each brand holds the number one position in its covered market; the brands were under-promoted and sales were largely to a single customer before the change of control.

guidance_outlook: Stable run-rate to be read from Q4 FY27 or Q1 FY28; management said the stabilised base is around INR600 crore organically, to be doubled over 5-6 years, with acquisitions additional.
Management said FY28 revenue would grow on the stabilised base and would be above INR600 crore, though it also cited a base of around INR150 crore as a stabilisation marker.
Gross margin changes expected to be visible only from Q1 FY28, from product mix and new sourcing; bridging stock currently carried.
About INR15-20 crore of further one-time costs expected in Q3 FY27, with a more stable cost structure by Q4.
Incremental run-rate expense of about INR45-50 crore per quarter versus the Q1 base once fully stable (Q4 comparison), per CFO.
Net debt to be significantly reduced by March 31, 2027 via a rights issue; exact finance cost plan to follow once the rights issue plan is finalised.
Industry growth expected within 8-10% long-term (volume 3-4%, price 5-6%, new introductions 1-2%).
capex_capacity: Over 20 CFAs onboarded, giving a nationwide distribution network and direct control of supply chain from October 1.

500690|2026-03.headline: GSFC FY26 standalone sales rose 15% to INR10,827 crore and PAT 14% to INR652 crore; Q4 sales hit a record INR2,622 crore.
500690|2026-03.overview: GSFC reported record Q4 FY26 sales of INR2,622 crore, with fertilizer sales of INR1,985 crore also a Q4 high. The Industrial Products segment posted its highest annual profit in four years (INR200 crore) and its best Q4 EBIT in ten quarters, helped by HX Crystal, traded ammonia and melamine exports, though caprolactam and nylon realisations were under pressure. Management said Q1 FY27 faces unsettled raw material markets, and it is managing the fertilizer mix around sulphur and ammonia supply.

500696|2026-03.headline: HUL Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue grew 8% with 7% USG led by volumes; EBITDA margin 23.7% at top of guidance; FY27 guided better than FY26.
500696|2026-03.overview: March quarter 2026 consolidated revenue rose 8% with 7% underlying sales growth (USG), the company's highest quarterly growth in 12 quarters, driven mainly by volume (UVG 6%). EBITDA grew 6% with margin at 23.7%, the higher end of guidance, while PAT before exceptionals was Rs 2,711 crore (+4%); reported PAT rose 20% helped by the Nutritionalab divestment versus an OZiva fair-value base effect. For FY26, turnover was Rs 63,763 crore with 5% USG and 4% UVG, and the second half outpaced the first; EBITDA grew 2% at a 23.6% margin. Management flagged a sharp March-onward rise in crude-linked input costs (8-10% material cost inflation) from the Middle East crisis and has taken 2-5% price increases, with more pricing possible.

financial_highlights.change: YoY; includes Nutritionalab divestment gain, offset by OZiva fair-value base effect

segments.name: Home Care
segments.commentary: Q4 USG 9% on high-single-digit UVG, strongest in 11 quarters; liquids grew double digit and crossed Rs 4,000 crore turnover. FY26 USG 4%.

segments.name: Beauty & Wellbeing
segments.commentary: Q4 USG 8% on mid-single-digit UVG; hair care grew strong double digit; premium skin care grew double digit while mass skin (Glow & Lovely, talc) was subdued. FY26 USG 6%. Minimalist ARR about Rs 850 crore; Simple ARR above Rs 160 crore.

segments.name: Personal Care
segments.commentary: Q4 USG 5%, pricing-led; skin cleansing grew high single digit (highest in 12 quarters) and premium cleansing bars grew double-digit volume. Oral care grew low single digit. FY26 USG 4%.

segments.name: Foods
segments.commentary: Q4 USG 5% on high-single-digit UVG; coffee grew double digit, tea grew low-single-digit volume, lifestyle nutrition grew double digit. FY26 USG 5% on mid-single-digit UVG.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated top line expected to be better than FY26 (USG basis), despite Middle East and currency volatility.
Mid-term EBITDA margin guidance kept at 22.5% to 23.5%; management expects Q1 FY27 to be at the lower end given cost pressure.

Material cost inflation of 8-10% seen for the June quarter; 2-5% price increases taken so far, with further calibrated price increases in Fabric Wash and Household Care in June quarter and beyond if costs persist.
Full-year FY27 pricing not guided; management said it is too difficult to give a number.
A&P spend stepped up by Rs 270 crore in absolute terms in FY26; non-working media being optimised while core brands stay fully funded.
capex_capacity: Rs 2,000 crore capex signed off for premium formats (liquids in Home Care, Personal Care and Beauty); timeline not specified.
Rs 3,500 crore deployed in FY26 on bolt-on acquisitions including Minimalist and OZiva.
Direct General Trade coverage increased by around 2 lakh outlets in FY26; specialty retail (open format stores, chemists, cosmetic stores) infrastructure being built.
Quick Commerce customer availability up about 1,400 basis points (as shared last quarter); a dedicated Quick Commerce organisation created.
Management said it remains open to bolt-on acquisitions.
demand_pricing: Demand described as stable; rural and urban demand growing at roughly equal rates in FY26.
No pre-buying by trade ahead of March/April price increases; no restocking effect in Q4 per management.
Home Care negative UPG is anniversarising; tea volumes low-single-digit with deflation in pricing cited as the cause.
Bodywash share up about 400 bps (Nielsen-based); body wash and premium skin cleansing growing double digit.

Monsoon forecast at 92% of normal; management cited higher reservoir levels, MSP increases of 5-6%, and record government grain stocks as offsets, and expects no rural demand impact unless rainfall falls below 85%.
E-commerce grew over 25% in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Is growth driven by volume gains after GST cuts, and what are the drivers of UVG?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited three volume buckets: market development (liquids Rs 4,000 crore, mostly volumetric), share gains on core brands, and channel capability build-out; it said elasticity gains are being reinvested.

qa_highlights.question: How confident is management on margins amid input cost volatility, and would volume priority mean margin risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost inflation of 8-10% on material basket versus 2-5% pricing taken so far; savings funnel accelerated; margin band of 22.5-23.5% retained, with lower end likely in the current quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why are Home Care price hikes more modest than in the FY23 cycle?
qa_highlights.answer: Current crude-driven inflation is seen as volatile and geopolitical rather than structural, so price increases are being taken in steps; further hikes will follow if costs persist.

qa_highlights.question: Why is mass skin care dragging Beauty & Wellbeing and what is being done?
qa_highlights.answer: Glow & Lovely and talc were subdued (talc hit by seasonal weakness in March); premium skin care is growing double digit with a premium skin portfolio ARR near Rs 1,400 crore; focus on democratising new formats like sunscreen and light moisturisers.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 pricing outlook and Minimalist size?
qa_highlights.answer: No full-year pricing number given; Minimalist ARR is about Rs 850 crore; cosmetics sub-category growth not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Is there Lifestyle Nutrition sustainability given milk inflation risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Horlicks is consumed in water as well as milk, is focusing on nutrition benefits, and new segments (RTD, protein, Horlicks Superfoods relaunch) are still small with headroom.

risks_watch: Input cost inflation of 8-10% with crude volatility (Brent cited between $85 and $120) and rupee depreciation; pricing lag could pressure margins below the 22.5-23.5% band.
Monsoon and El Nino risk to H2 rural demand; management's threshold is rainfall below 85%.
Mass skin care and Personal Care volume weakness; Personal Care grew only 5% and is pricing-led.
Price elasticity and possible down-trading if further price increases are taken; Home Care rebalancing of price and volume expected in the short term.
Horlicks/Boost recovery still early; Horlicks Superfoods national rollout and protein launch pending.
Foods remains outside the Unilever transaction perimeter; questions on the strategy alignment were addressed.

500696|2026-06.headline: HUL Q1 FY27 underlying sales growth accelerated to 10% (5% volume, 5% price), with EBITDA margin at 23% within guided range.
500696|2026-06.overview: HUL reported Q1 FY27 turnover of INR 17,184 crores with 10% underlying sales growth, the highest in 13 quarters, split equally between volume and price. Growth accelerated from 3% in H1 FY26. EBITDA rose 8% YoY to INR 3,947 crores at a 23% margin, within the guided range. Reported PAT of INR 2,680 crores fell 2% YoY because of a one-off tax credit of about INR 330 crores in the base quarter; adjusted for this, PAT grew 11%. Management reaffirmed that FY27 will be better than FY26 and that the EBITDA margin will stay around the guided range, while flagging monsoon, crude and geopolitical risks.

financial_highlights.change: -2% YoY; base included ~INR 330 crore one-off tax credit
Stepped up sequentially; highest in 11 quarters

segments.name: Home Care
segments.commentary: USG 14% on high-single-digit UVG, the strongest in 3 years. Fabric Wash grew double digits, volume-led; Household Care (Vim Liquid) grew double digits in USG and UVG. Calibrated price increases taken on crude-linked inputs.

segments.name: Beauty & Wellbeing
segments.commentary: USG 12% on high-single-digit UVG. Hair Care grew double digits, volume-led; Skin Care and Colour Cosmetics grew high single digit, with Premium Skin Care at double digit and Minimalist accelerating. Health & Wellbeing (OZiva) was soft as the business transitions toward emerging demand spaces.

segments.name: Personal Care
segments.commentary: USG 4%, driven by price increases taken for palm oil inflation for a second year. Skin Cleansing grew mid single digit (Dove and Pears premium bars double digit; Bodywash double digit); soaps volumes declined mid-single digit per analyst question. Oral Care grew mid single digit.

segments.name: Foods
segments.commentary: USG 7% on mid-single-digit UVG. Coffee grew double digit volume-led; Premium Tea low-single-digit UVG. Lifestyle Nutrition grew double digit (Horlicks, Boost); Boost crossed INR 1,000 crore turnover. Packaged Foods grew high single digit.

guidance_outlook: FY27 expected to be better than FY26; guidance retained, but no quarterly guidance given.
EBITDA margin expected to remain around the current guided range despite elevated commodities and currencies.
Demand environment expected to remain stable; no inflation-led demand impact seen.
Guidance is risk-adjusted for macro and portfolio risks, per management.
Capital Markets Day scheduled for September 2026 for strategy update.
capex_capacity: Haridwar and Sonepat factories recognized in WEF Global Lighthouse Network; HUL now holds 8 designations across 6 sites.
Liquids Lab of the Future in Mumbai, AI-enabled, said to cut formulation timelines by up to 6x.
Unilever Fragrance House launched in India as part of a global fragrance capability programme.
Digital-first distribution centre in Vijayawada with AI-enabled real-time visibility.
demand_pricing: Turnover-weighted market share gains claimed across the portfolio; management does not guide by segment.
Price increases calibrated; cost inflation roughly 10% vs pricing around 5% per analyst citation, not disputed by management.

Tea early-season read shows inflationary trend; pricing decisions to follow buying season.

qa_highlights.question: Has the outlook tone changed versus last quarter given monsoon and geopolitical concerns?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no change; it remains well positioned, and is only cautioning on how the volatile economic scenario pans out.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the mid-single-digit soaps volume decline, and what is market share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to palm oil inflation over two years; it is focusing on premiumization (Dove, Pears double digit, Bodywash double digit) and does not disclose segment share, saying it is winning turnover-weighted share overall.

qa_highlights.question: Is A&P under-investment happening to protect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said A&P is at its highest in 11-12 quarters, with better ROI from AI-enabled programmes and media procurement savings, so like-for-like comparisons are not strictly valid.

qa_highlights.question: Is the El Nino and monsoon risk material to growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a difficult versus good agriculture year moves GDP by 50-60 bps; MSP hikes of 5-6% insulate rural income, and a rainfall deficit of about 15% is seen as not meaningfully impacting the economy.

qa_highlights.question: At what crude level can 23% margin be held without further price increases?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined a precise crude threshold, but said it can maintain margins with about half of inflation passed through and that crude of $75-100/bbl is manageable; $140-160 would be a different discussion.

qa_highlights.question: Is the quick commerce slowdown affecting HUL?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said QCom grew 40-50% and the channel remains structurally attractive, with new entrants and tailored assortments and pack architecture.

risks_watch: Commodity inflation (palm oil, crude-linked derivatives, tea) and the pace of calibrated pricing needed to hold 23% EBITDA margin.
Soaps volume decline under palm oil-led price pressure and value competition in soaps and liquids.
Monsoon progression (rainfall deficit cited at about 15%) and El Nino impact on rural demand.
OZiva growth moderation in Health & Wellbeing and the stated transition of the business.
Management's shift from prior quarter's language on navigating volatility to cautioning on monsoon and geopolitics; watch wording at the September Capital Markets Day.

500696|2026-09.headline: HUL Q2 FY27 underlying sales growth of 15% with 7% volume growth; PAT before exceptionals up 9% to Rs 2,795 crore.
500696|2026-09.overview: HUL reported Q2 FY27 turnover of Rs 18,071 crore, with 15% USG (its highest in 14 quarters) and 7% UVG, despite roughly 8% price growth. EBITDA margin was 22.6%, within the guided 22-24% range, down about 140 bps YoY and 40 bps QoQ as gross margin fell about 400 bps on input cost inflation. EBITDA rose 8% to Rs 4,089 crore and PAT before exceptionals rose 9%; reported PAT was flat because the base quarter had Rs 273 crore of one-off tax gains. Management said it passed through absolute cost increases, protected volumes, and offset gross margin pressure with A&P productivity and overhead leverage.

segments.name: Home Care
segments.commentary: USG 22% on double-digit UVG; Fabric Wash grew double digit across bars, powders and liquids. Management cut Home Care A&P by about Rs 250 crore in the quarter; segment absolute EBIT margin about 16% on revenue near Rs 7,000 crore.

segments.name: Beauty & Wellbeing
segments.commentary: USG 16% on double-digit UVG, with Hair Care accelerating. Health & Wellbeing was subdued; OZiva's 2-year CAGR is beyond strong double digits but growth is non-linear.

segments.name: Personal Care
segments.commentary: USG 9%. Skin Cleansing grew double digit with volume-led growth in Pears and Dove bars; Oral Care grew low single digit with premium innovations up double digit.

segments.name: Foods
segments.commentary: USG 9% on low-single-digit UVG. Coffee grew high single digit; mass tea was soft while Red Label Instant Tea scaled; Lifestyle Nutrition grew double digit.

guidance_outlook: Medium-term EBITDA margin expected within the current guided range of 22% to 24%; management said cyclical dips can take margin to the lower end.
Management expects commodity inflation to remain elevated, but does not expect inflation of the scale seen in June and September quarters to recur.
Calibrated price increases to continue in measured steps if inflation rises.
Structurally, portfolio mix is expected to lift gross margin over a 3 to 5 year horizon; no numeric target given.
About 10% A&P productivity savings expected from non-working media, AI tools and buying efficiency.
Confident of growing ahead of the market under the Winning In New India strategy.
capex_capacity: Added 30,000 general trade outlets in the quarter.
Modern trade category-development asset deployment nearly doubled over the last two quarters.
Horlicks Protein Powder launched in the quarter; early traction encouraging.
Kissan condiments relaunched with new packaging.
demand_pricing: Price growth about 8% in the quarter; volume growth held at 7% despite it.
Management said rural growth rose sequentially and rural is growing alongside urban; growth described as broad-based across categories, channels and geographies.
Mass tea was hit by high tea inflation; price increases in tea largely taken per management.
Quick commerce players are supplied mostly direct; premium channel expansion seen as beneficial.
Market shares improved at company level and in Home Care per management.
SOV:SOM ratio on traditional media moved from 1 to 1.1.

qa_highlights.question: Is volume growth at risk given inflation and price hikes, especially in rural?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited sequential improvement in volume momentum and rising rural demand, with growth broad-based across urban and rural and categories.

qa_highlights.question: Have gross margins bottomed, and will more pricing be needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said pricing covers absolute cost increases; EBITDA margin fell only 40 bps QoQ; structural portfolio mix should support margins in the medium term.

qa_highlights.question: Does the ~8% price increase fully cover cost inflation, and can gross margin return toward 50-51%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said costs are covered; tea pricing largely taken. It declined to give a numeric gross margin target and pointed to a 3 to 5 year structural improvement.

qa_highlights.question: Why has Home Care profit growth lagged strong volume growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to a price-versus-cost lag from petrochemical-linked inputs and said Home Care remains structurally premium; it declined to guide Home Care margin back toward 19-20%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Lifebuoy underperforming, and what is being done?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said soaps cleansing grew double digit sequentially and Lifebuoy faces uptrading within its own portfolio; it cited Lifebuoy Ice Bath launch and further work to stay competitive.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 25% pre-COVID peak margin a reasonable 3 to 5 year aspiration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 22-24% range was widened by 50 bps each side for cyclicality, with a structural shift toward higher-margin categories over 3 to 5 years, but gave no numeric aspiration.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure from elevated commodity inflation, especially petrochemical-linked Home Care inputs and tea.
Home Care EBIT growth has moderated while volumes are strong; margin recovery depends on price catching up with cost.

Lifebuoy and mass soaps competitiveness; mass tea softness.

500710|2026-03.headline: JSW Dulux Q4 FY26 revenue rose 6.2% on 23% blended volume growth, with price and mix cuts holding back realisations and EBITDA margin near 14.4%.
500710|2026-03.overview: Management reported a record 23% blended volume growth across decorative and industrial paints, with revenue up 6.2%, the gap driven mainly by price and mix after premium price corrections from September-October 2025. Like-for-like EBITDA grew about 2% and PBT declined slightly, while the EBITDA margin was stated at around 14.4%. Management said raw material inflation since March 2026 has forced a price increase of about 9.7% through mid-May, with an estimated further 3-4% needed. The company also booked INR64.8 crore from the final real estate sale and proposed a final dividend of INR50 per share.

financial_highlights.change: Record, per management; decorative and industrial both grew strongly
YoY; one of strongest in last 4 quarters
Largely protected vs prior year per CFO
Last of real estate sale, completed March 2026

segments.name: Decorative
segments.commentary: Very strong volume growth amid competition; premium growth good, retail and semi-urban grew faster; Dulux Velvet Touch luxury finishes launched; mass and economy push increasing. segments.name: Industrial (Automotive & Specialty, Marine & Protective, Coil)

Further price increase of about 3-4% needed industry-wide to offset RMC inflation of 24-25% (raw materials about 55% of RMC; implied about 13.5% need), per management estimate.
Price correction drag of about 1.5-2% expected to continue into the coming quarter; mix and price effects expected to neutralise by August-September.
FY27 margins may compress for about a quarter if elevated crude and raw material levels persist, though management sees no structural issue.
Integrated SAP and systems work planned around post-Diwali, towards end of calendar 2026; Mumbai HQ shift ongoing.
Dealer integration: projects business integrated; combined JSW Dulux and JSW Paints sales teams in 7 metros from later in May; retail integration only planned for early FY28 (early calendar 2027).

500710|2026-06.headline: JSW Dulux Q1 FY27 revenue rose 18.8% to ₹965 crore on ~25% volume growth, but EBITDA margin fell to 11.9% with PAT lifted by one-offs.
500710|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 18.8% like-to-like to ₹965 crore, with volume up about 25% (about 18-19% after price). Gross margin was 37.4%, which management says was depressed by roughly 2 points of high-cost inventory and about 2.5 points from reclassifying promotional spends to gross revenue; underlying gross margin was put at 39.5-40%. EBITDA rose 14.7% to ₹115.1 crore but margin diluted about 50 bps to 11.9% after headcount additions (~160 people) and R&D investment. Reported PAT of ₹135.5 crore includes one-offs: ₹55.9 crore dividend from ICICI R&T and ₹108 crore income tax refund (incl. ₹21.5 crore interest) for AY 2013-14.

financial_highlights.change: Management: underlying ~39.5-40% before inventory and reclassification effects
Other income; linked to real estate monetisation

segments.commentary: Grew double digits (management cites ~20% volume growth) and is ~60% of business; premium is ~45% of decorative and led growth, with premium and luxury growing high double digits. Mass and economy grew lower.

segments.name: Industrial
segments.commentary: All sub-segments grew upwards of 25%; automotive grew strongly with premium OEM and refinish wins (Porsche, Mahindra, MG via JSW group, Sikkens body shops).

Management expects Q2 growth in a similar band to Q1 despite a weaker July due to late rains; target is double-digit volume and value growth.

ERP migration from AkzoNobel systems planned by end of calendar year; TSA period is limited.

Headquarters moved from Delhi to JSW Centre, Mumbai during Q1.
demand_pricing: Volume growth ~25%, with price contributing ~6-7 points; growth driven by value per outlet from existing outlets, broadly secular across outlet types.
Gross-to-net reclassification of promotional spends (~2.5% of blended revenue) reduced reported gross margin; management says this aligns with industry presentation.
Management says decorative pricing has stabilised but competition from new entrants, with discounting, will persist for 1-2 years.

Discount ratio includes distributor commission (~4.5-4.7% of revenue), which management says makes dealer commissions otherwise modest; company benchmarks pricing to the market leader, not new entrants.
Benefit expected as high-priced inventory bought at end-March is consumed; lower-cost stock now entering August.

qa_highlights.question: What execution changes are driving better decorative performance, beyond headcount?
qa_highlights.answer: Micro-market segmentation by share tiers; reinforced Velvet Touch and WeatherShield; focus on undercoats such as primers in weak states; digital lead management, AI/analytics and an architect/painter programme. Hybrid direct model being tested in top 20 towns.

qa_highlights.question: How does volume-value gap reconcile with mix improvement?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited three factors: high-cost inventory, ~2.5% gross-to-net reclassification, and faster growth in lower-margin industrial and other businesses.

qa_highlights.question: Target for top-three position and inorganic plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Combined JSW Paints and JSW Dulux revenue is about ₹6,000 crore. Aim is to become number two; industrial to be number one in 1-1.5 years and wider ambition by 2030-31. No explicit M&A mentioned.

qa_highlights.question: Competitive intensity and discounting vs. new entrants?
qa_highlights.answer: Competition to remain intense for 1-2 years; company does not match new entrant discounts and benchmarks against the market leader.

qa_highlights.question: Decorative outperformance vs Asian Paints and Berger (8-9% volume growth)?
qa_highlights.answer: Attributed to premium-led growth, distribution expansion, digital tools and recovery in smaller dealers after new-entrant pressure; no single driver cited.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for July-August?
qa_highlights.answer: July was weaker due to late rains, but management expects Q2 in a similar band and targets double-digit growth in volume and value.

EBITDA margin trajectory versus the 13-15% guidance as headcount and R&D costs continue.
Persistent discounting by new entrants in decorative; mass and economy segment growth lagging.

Execution risk in Project Akshaya, ERP migration and exit from AkzoNobel TSA; related-party governance with JSW Paints.

500710|2026-09.headline: JSW Dulux Q2 FY27 volume rose ~21.8% and revenue ~21.3%, but gross margin fell ~400 bps on industrial price-cost lag, leaving EBITDA margin near 11.5%.
500710|2026-09.overview: Comparable like-to-like revenue grew about 21.3% with volume up about 21.8%, helped by a bounce in undercoats and share gains in decorative and industrial. Price rose about 7.9% but adverse mix of about 8.4% offset it, and industrial price hikes lagged crude-linked raw material inflation. EBITDA was INR110.9 crore (up 4.4% vs like-to-like INR106.3 crore) and PAT before exceptionals was INR71.2 crore (up 2% from INR69.8 crore), with the tax rate near 19% helped by a one-off release. Management kept the ~13-14% EBITDA margin aim as an intent only, since full-year guidance is no longer valid given elevated crude and INR around 94.5-96/USD.

Lower due to one-off release of excess tax provision (AY 2013-14 favourable order)

segments.commentary: Mid-double-digit revenue growth and high-single-digit premium volume growth in H1; ex-putty and texture volume grew about 8-8.5%, with undercoats a seasonal boost. Margin held roughly flat sequentially; cumulative price increases about 3.2-3.5% plus a further ~1% announced for November.

segments.name: Industrial
segments.commentary: Revenue and volume grew about 32% and high-double-digit respectively, with new accounts and share gains in coil coating, packaging and vehicle refinish. Raw material COGS rose about 30-35% in marine, protective, coil and packaging vs price hikes of ~6-7%; industrial EBITDA margin now high single-digit, with a ~4% industrial price increase announced.

guidance_outlook: Management intends to get close to 13% EBITDA margin (earlier 13-14% guidance) but said full-year target is no longer valid; H2 target depends on crude and INR/USD.
Expects industrial margins to recover as price increases flow through; said the margin pressure is temporary, not structural.
Working capital elevated from TiO2 pre-buy and industrial credit delays; expects return to normal levels over 3-5 months.
Project Akshaya targeted to contribute roughly 7-10% of full-year EBITDA; ERP consolidation expected around December 2026.
Expects H2 demand to remain buoyant if crude and dollar do not worsen; monitoring rainfall deficit and price pass-through through November-December.
capex_capacity: Industrial capacity utilisation in some verticals near 75%, leading to higher industrial capex earlier in the year.
Additional decorative capacity being evaluated by segment demand; continued spend on tinting machines and Dulux stores.

No incentives or tax benefits expected from cross-manufacturing; existing plants have largely used available benefits.
demand_pricing: Price hikes staggered in three tranches (30 September, 14 October, 26 October) versus most competitors' 1 November, to help smaller dealers absorb them; blended price exit rate in September 10.4% vs quarterly average 7.9%.
Decorative cumulative price increase about 13.5% by management's count (including the antidumping-related 2%), with a further 1% announced for November.
Competitive intensity in activation and discounting continues, somewhat lower than two years ago; pricing discipline improved as most players took hikes.
Share gains in decorative regained after last year's losses, with growth more broad-based (North and West earlier; South improving; East still a challenge).
Growth split between own stores and new stores moved to about 55%-45% in favour of existing stores (previously ~70-30 towards new stores).
Management said it is not seeing a demand slowdown in retail or projects; October was strong, though it is unclear how much growth is price-led versus demand-led.
Crude fell back to about $105-106/bbl from a peak of ~$114 (~$95 when budget set); INR/USD about 94.5 after touching 96.

qa_highlights.question: How will industrial coatings profitability evolve in FY27, given lower price hikes and higher crude sensitivity?
qa_highlights.answer: Marine, protective, coil and packaging COGS rose ~30-35% vs price hikes of ~6-7%, causing a lag; industrial EBITDA margin is now high single-digit and management is pushing price and pruning low-margin accounts.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20%+ volume growth driven by market share gains, and where?
qa_highlights.answer: Gains in vehicle refinish, coil and packaging; holding in marine. Decorative has regained share lost last year; growth broadening, with the South improving and East still a challenge.

qa_highlights.question: How should capex and incremental spend be viewed given 20%+ volume growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Cross-manufacturing across JSW Dulux and JSW Paints plants has started; industrial capex was stepped up as utilisation approached 75%, and decorative capacity is being assessed by segment.

qa_highlights.question: What is the H2 FY27 outlook given the rainfall deficit?
qa_highlights.answer: Rainfall deficit is within range at the aggregate level; no demand slowdown seen in retail or projects; H2 demand expected to stay buoyant if crude and the dollar do not worsen.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the tax rate about 19% and what is the full-year rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Lower rate due to a one-off release of an excess tax provision after a favourable order for AY 2013-14; full-year rate should return to about 25.6%.

qa_highlights.question: Is competitive intensity easing, and how is JSW Dulux responding?
qa_highlights.answer: Price hikes taken by most players so discipline is better, but activation and discounting remain intense, slightly lower than before; management says execution excellence and integration are the focus.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the working capital build and when will it normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory built from a titanium dioxide pre-buy and market credit stress mainly in industrial; expected to normalise over the next 3-5 months.

qa_highlights.question: What share of gross margin savings and Akshaya contribution is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Akshaya savings are on target, with INR7.3 crore realised in Q2; full-year target is roughly 7-10% of EBITDA, and targets are not being disclosed quarterly.

qa_highlights.question: Where is industrial growth coming from, and what new segments are being considered?
qa_highlights.answer: Automotive is the focus as the vehicle parc grows about 20% CAGR; management is looking at higher-margin segments that can be entered over the next year, provided they are not margin-dilutive.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA margin path to 13-15%?
qa_highlights.answer: Full-year guidance is not valid; intent is to get close to 13%. Further lift is expected from integration across procurement, manufacturing and functions with JSW Paints.

500730|2026-03.headline: NOCIL Q4 FY26 revenue rose 5% QoQ to Rs.330 crore on 7% volume growth, but EBITDA margin fell to 6.4% amid raw material inflation.
500730|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was Rs.330 crore, up 5% QoQ from Rs.316 crore, with volumes up 7% QoQ, driven by domestic demand after GST 2.0 and steady single-digit international growth. Operating EBITDA fell to Rs.21 crore (6.4% margin) from Rs.27 crore in Q3, hit by gas-driven utility costs, shutdown maintenance and a Rs.7-8 crore inventory-related stock change debit. FY26 revenue fell to Rs.1,303 crore from Rs.1,393 crore, with full-year volumes up 3% and PAT down to Rs.56 crore from Rs.103 crore. Management raised prices on non-contractual business in March and on contractual business from Q1 FY27 in response to sharp raw material inflation linked to Middle East disruption.

segments.name: Domestic
segments.commentary: Domestic volumes grew single digits QoQ, aided by GST 2.0 demand; management estimates a 100-150 bps market share gain. Volume split FY26 is 70% domestic, 30% exports.

segments.name: International / Exports
segments.commentary: International volumes grew steady single digits in Q4. Export value share is about 33% (67:33 domestic:export by value). US volumes, hit roughly 50% last quarter by duties, are recovering but management expects traction only in FY27.

segments.name: Specialty rubber chemicals
segments.commentary: Specialty is about 15% of mix today, with management targeting about 20% after the new Rs.130 crore integrated specialty facility ramps up.

guidance_outlook: Management expects H2 FY26 volume momentum (up 12% YoY) to continue into coming quarters, and says Q4 volumes can serve as the base run rate.
Targets double-digit volume growth in coming years.
Targets EBITDA improvement of about 150 bps from the FY26 base going forward.
Price increases on non-contractual business taken in March and on contractual business from Q1 FY27; management sees the current raw material spike as volatility, not structural demand weakness.
Expects 6-8 months from commissioning before material traction from tyre-based customers on new capacity; non-tyre business should start earlier.
Tax rate reverts to normal rates in FY27 with no specific reduction expected.
capex_capacity: TDQ capex at Dahej (announced 26 March 2024) is complete; trial production has started and samples go to customers for approval. Total capex is under Rs.250 crore.

New Rs.130 crore capex announced 16 March 2026 for a comprehensive integrated specialty rubber chemicals facility at Dahej, expected complete by H1 FY28. Mostly growth capex with some intermediates; largely merchant per management, with a part captive.
Installed capacity cited by analysts at about 1,38,000-1,39,000 tons; management declined to give effective capacity, saying utilisation is roughly 65%.
CWIP was about Rs.220 crore at FY26 end; no project debt drawn yet, with bank lines above Rs.100 crore available at repo-linked rates.
Full-year FY26 capex was largely funded from internal working capital release; analysts estimated Rs.170-180 crore working capital saving.
demand_pricing: Realisations were under pressure from low-priced imports through Q4; management says the market corrected finished goods prices after April input price rises.
About 65-70% of volume is under contract, with the rest non-contractual; roughly 40% of revenue is exposed to anti-dumping products.

DGTR gave positive final findings in March 2026 for antioxidant TDQ and Sulphenamides (CBS and NS), subject to central government approval, which management expects around mid-June (about 90 days). Pilflex 13 and 4ADPA findings are pending, with Pilflex 13 expected within a month or two.
Imports rose in Jan-Feb 2026 YoY; management linked this to FTA routes (Thailand, Korea) and year-end advance-licence imports. The company is pressing the government on FTA value-addition norms.
Management assumes 2-2.5% long-term global rubber demand growth, and 7% domestic demand growth per ICRA.
Competitive intensity is rising from Chinese players in latex, and 6PPD alternatives are at trial stage, with the company working on them.

qa_highlights.question: Are customers negotiating on price or prioritising volume security, and what is the contract mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says talks are positive but weighted to supply reliability; contract share is about 65-70%, with the rest non-contract and repriced first.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA not benefit from inflation given inventory on hand?
qa_highlights.answer: Legacy high-cost inventory from the prior year spilled into H1 FY26, and the FTA-driven removal of basic duty on one product compressed spreads. Q4 also had a Rs.7-8 crore stock change debit and March production cuts from gas costs.

qa_highlights.question: Will ADD on TDQ and Sulphenamides lift margins, and what are the timelines?

500730|2026-06.headline: NOCIL Q1 FY27 revenue rose 20% YoY to Rs 403 crore and EBITDA margin hit 11.2%, but volumes fell 3% QoQ on supply constraints.

EBITDA rose to Rs 45 crore (11.2% margin) and PAT to Rs 28 crore, though management described several conversion-cost items as one-offs. Anti-dumping duty on Sulphonamides (CBS and NS) was approved on 20 June 2026, while the Pilflex 13 duty awaits Government approval. FY27 guidance was set at revenue of Rs 1,400-1,600 crore and EBITDA around 10%.

Management says the supply issues are now addressed, expects volumes to recover in H2, and remains confident of FY27 revenue at the upper end of Rs.1,400-1,600 crore with EBITDA margin around 10%. Import dumping and higher utility, coal, gas and freight costs weighed on the quarter.

500770|2026-06.headline: Tata Chemicals Q1 FY27: standalone EBITDA up 35% on volumes and FX-led soda ash pricing, while consolidated EBITDA fell about INR 100 crore on sharply lower realisations.
500770|2026-06.overview: Tata Chemicals reported Q1 FY27 with consolidated revenue up 14% YoY but EBITDA down about INR 100 crore despite lower realisations, mainly from soda ash pressure in the industrial segment. Standalone performed strongly: revenue up 10%, EBITDA up 35%, and PAT from continuing operations up 12%, helped by higher volumes, an INR 2,000/tonne soda ash price increase in India, and fixed-cost control. The company moved to three reporting segments (Living Essentials, Industrial Essentials, Farm Essentials) to highlight non-cyclical revenue, and net debt fell INR 5,692 crore QoQ on asset monetisation (management later cited about INR 300 crore of debt reduction versus March). Management flagged that cost pressures from the Middle East conflict (Kenya HFO, UK gas, India limestone and coal logistics) could intensify after October.

qa_highlights.question: What is the rationale for the segment reclassification, and will it change the P&L?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the aim is to reshape the portfolio toward non-cyclical, sustainability-led products with stickier customers and lower price volatility, with capital allocation following. Geography-wise P&L will still be disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sharp India margin expansion despite lower soda ash and bicarbonate volumes (down about 12% and 19% QoQ)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited plant optimisation that shifted production toward higher salt volumes, lower-cost coal inventory that will unwind next quarter, and some bicarbonate tender contracts forgone for pricing reasons. It said about 18% is a sustainable India EBITDA margin.

qa_highlights.question: What assets were monetised to reduce debt?

qa_highlights.question: What are the status and economics of the sodium-ion battery and recycling businesses?
qa_highlights.answer: The first pack is in testing and the strategy is being reviewed. Management is focused on stationary storage, the drone test was only a proof of flight, and soda ash intensity figures will come later.

qa_highlights.question: What capex and maintenance capex should be assumed for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said annualised capex will be around depreciation and not above it. The CFO confirmed about INR 1,200 crore (FY26 consolidated depreciation) as the FY27 figure.

qa_highlights.question: Why was employee cost higher, and what was IMACID's Q1 performance?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost includes about INR 43 crore of one-off items, with the rest mainly rupee depreciation and Q1 variable pay. IMACID did not run in Q1 due to high sulfur prices and is expected to be profitable for FY27.

500770|2026-09.headline: Tata Chemicals Q2 FY27 consolidated EBITDA fell to INR381 crore (from INR537 crore) and the company posted a loss after tax of INR50 crore.
500770|2026-09.overview: Standalone revenue rose 8% YoY to INR1,303 crore and EBITDA rose 22% to INR292 crore, but standalone PAT fell 31% to INR122 crore. Consolidated results were hit by UK gas and energy cost spikes, lower overseas realisations (US exports to Southeast Asia), logistics costs, and the suspension of Kenya operations. Management described soda ash markets as oversupplied, with prices expected to stay range-bound. Net debt excluding leases stood at INR6,127 crore.

segments.name: Living Essentials (bicarbonate, salt, FOS)
segments.commentary: Standalone India volumes rose on salt, FOS and silica. The UK salt and bicarbonate operations drove the consolidated EBIT loss, from gas and energy costs and higher cost of feedstock soda ash for bicarbonate. Management expects these costs to normalise as energy and logistics costs moderate.

segments.name: Industrial Essentials (soda ash, silica)
segments.commentary: Global soda ash is oversupplied, with China as the key driver. Indian domestic prices softened late in the year, and US export pricing remains under pressure. DGTR has recommended two years of import quantity restrictions after imports rose 89% in FY2024.

segments.name: US (TCNA)
segments.commentary: Revenue rose on volumes from contracts acquired during the year, partly offset by lower export pricing. The company won Searles Valley Minerals Chapter 11 contracts covering half a million tonnes over two years. The US$22 million payment is being amortised as an intangible over five years.

segments.name: UK
segments.commentary: Revenue fell on lower salt realisation. Variable costs rose sharply on gas prices, and this was the main drag on consolidated EBIT.

segments.name: Kenya
segments.commentary: Operations have been suspended since a Ministry of Mining notice. Management says the operation is debt-free and was margin positive. The company is pursuing legal and administrative routes, and a court hearing is expected in November.

segments.name: Farm Essentials (Rallis)
segments.commentary: Monsoon shortfall and delayed sowing hurt agrochemical demand early in the period, but Kharif acreage recovered. Rallis delivered resilient performance, aided by crop care and soil health, while profitability was pressured by input cost inflation.

guidance_outlook: Near-term soda ash market expected to remain range-bound due to Chinese capacity additions and sustained export activity.
Pricing is expected to stay range-bound; sustained improvement depends on supply rationalisation and demand growth in applications and geographies.
Capex of around INR1,000 crore for the current year, including growth projects; next year expected to be roughly the same.
UK energy and logistics costs expected to moderate and return to normal levels.
Focus on cost competitiveness, supply chain resilience, working capital optimisation, debt reduction and disciplined capital allocation.
capex_capacity: Capex of around INR1,000 crore for FY27, including growth projects; FY28 expected at a similar level.
Kenya: the company had been in the midst of doubling capacity and adding a bicarbonate unit, plus seeking a partner for container glass. These plans are now affected by the suspension.
Searles Valley contracts add about half a million tonnes to be served over two years, benefiting from proximity to California and Mexico markets.
Inner Mongolia Berun's 5 million tonne phase one had maintenance outages in October, expected to return to full rates at month end (Chinese supply side).
demand_pricing: Global soda ash: persistent oversupply, weak Chinese real estate and construction demand, and high Chinese export volumes. Chinese producer inventory reached about 1.89 million tonnes by end-September.
India: demand growth remains healthy, supported by solar glass capacity and infrastructure. Imports rose 89% in FY2024 and remain elevated.
Southeast Asia exports are unremunerative; the company is serving only residual contracts and will focus on the Americas and positive-netback markets.
Farm Essentials: uneven rainfall and delayed sowing hit parts of the quarter. Cautious agricultural outlook with weather, crop prices and input costs as near-term risks.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of Kenya operations and the possible course of action?
qa_highlights.answer: Operations remain suspended after a Ministry of Mining notice. The company is pursuing administrative engagement and a legal route, citing the UK-Kenya BIT and a lease running to 2053. The Environment and Land Court is due to hear the matter in November. Management would not give a timeline for restart.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the UK-related EBIT loss in Living Essentials, and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is mainly UK salt and bicarbonate, due to higher gas and energy costs and higher feedstock soda ash logistics cost for bicarbonate. Q2 saw a sharp spike and these costs are expected to normalise.

qa_highlights.question: What contribution margins and accounting apply to the Searles Valley contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: The $22 million paid is recorded as an intangible and amortised over five years. Pricing is substantially above the export option, though exact figures were not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Will other US producers' shutdowns force the company to cut capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Southeast Asia exports are unremunerative and it is serving only residual contracts. Strategy is unchanged and it will focus on the Americas and positive-netback markets.

qa_highlights.question: What is the nature of the INR796 crore proceeds from sale of non-current investments, and what is the capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: The proceeds came from selling listed shares in group companies in July, used to repay US and UK debt. The company holds about INR8,000 crore of group company shares at market value. Capex is about INR1,000 crore this year and similar next year, including growth projects.

qa_highlights.question: Should the company monetise its Tata Sons stake to reward shareholders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to comment on this.

500820|2026-03.headline: Asian Paints Q4 FY26 decorative volume grew 12.4% and standalone PBDIT rose 26%, with management reiterating an 18-20% margin guidance despite roughly 10.5-11% cumulative price hikes.
500820|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was a strong quarter: decorative volume grew 12.4% and value 10.2%, with all three months double-digit and volume-value gap narrowing to about 2.2%. Standalone net sales rose 10.3% and PBDIT 26% to a 21.2% margin, while gross margin reached about 45.6% on deflation of roughly 1.4%. Management has taken about 10.5-11% price increases, flagged further calibrated hikes and expects high single-digit to 8-10% volume growth ahead, while it says competitive discounting remains intense. Full-year FY26 standalone net sales grew 4.3% and consolidated 5.1%, with a 60% dividend payout (total Rs 27.5 per share).

qa_highlights.question: How much of total cost inflation, including rupee depreciation, has been passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 11% has been passed on against a cost impact nearer 20%; the gap will be managed through cost excellence and sourcing, and it plans further calibrated hikes.

qa_highlights.question: Will the pricing and upstocking inflate near-term volumes, and what is the outlook beyond the base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects high single-digit to 8-10% volume growth, with upstocking in Q1 but liquidation of stock limiting it. Q2 and Q3 have a longer festive period, but the geopolitical situation is a risk.

qa_highlights.question: Can margins hold at 18-20% under a high-crude scenario, and how does this compare with FY22?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is hard to predict beyond six months and inflation will not ease quickly. It cited premiumization, backward integration and cost efficiencies as offsets, and called it a tough endeavour.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the mix decline (-2.5%) and gap normalization reflects upstocking or premiumization?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 has higher-value contributions and high-value upstocking, so management expects a 3-4% volume-value gap to persist rather than the 5-6% seen before.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of other expenses growing about 2% in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Parag Rane said cost initiatives and higher revenue scale improved overhead absorption, in line with full-year trends.

risks_watch: Geopolitical situation and crude price path could raise raw material inflation beyond current price hikes.

Q1 and Q2 face higher base and pipeline stock liquidation risk after upstocking in Q4 and Q1.
Price elasticity: management expects a discretionary category with some demand sensitivity to the size of hikes.

500820|2026-06.headline: Asian Paints Q1 FY27: volume up about 9%, standalone top line up about 17%, PBDIT margin about 22%, with weighted price increase about 7%.
500820|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as a good quarter, with volume growth of about 9% spread across all three months and decorative value growth of about 16.6% on a lower base. Standalone top line grew about 17% and PBDIT, PBT and PAT each grew above 30%, with PBDIT margin about 22%. Consolidated top line grew about 18% and PBDIT margin was about 20.6%, up about 240 bps YoY. Management flagged that material inflation of about 25% is being offset only partly by price increases and that Q2 is seasonally lower-margin, while reiterating a PBDIT margin guidance of 18-20% and a full-year volume band of 8-10%.

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 volume growth band of about 8-10%, held for Q2, Q3 and Q4 given festive season and uncertainty in H2 pricing.

Weighted average price increase about 7%; product-mix-driven differential pricing by category.
Input costs: material inflation about 25%, while some input prices (monomers) have eased and TiO2 turned upward at end-June.

Management estimates Asian Paints grew slightly faster than the industry as smaller players lost share due to supply chain volatility.

qa_highlights.question: How is the 17% share of revenue from new products defined, and where do their margins sit?
qa_highlights.answer: New products are those launched within a three-year window and include emulsions, waterproofing, construction chemicals, premium/luxury and new customer propositions. Management said they support healthy overall margins, but gave no quantified margin figure.

qa_highlights.question: Was demand pulled forward by price hikes, and was the Bengal election a drag?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said demand was decent in all three months and some pipeline inventory came in because of pricing action. T1/T2 growth was weaker than rural, but B2B urban growth compensated. Management said double-digit growth was possible, and the 8-10% band was in line with its expectations.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the volume-value gap about 7% and how much is mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Premium mix contributed about 3% in the quarter, with economy products still performing well and newer products helping the mix.

qa_highlights.question: What is the crude level at which current price increases keep margins in the 18-20% band?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to link margins to crude, citing TiO2 and additives not being crude-linked and weighted-average purchasing. It reiterated 18-20% PBDIT margin guidance as the reference point.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin benefit came from low-cost inventory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not quantify it in basis points. It said inventory was about 30-45 days, with older low-cost raw material used for about half the quarter, and most of the finished-goods benefit came through in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Will the VAE project be used only for premium and luxury emulsions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said VAE can be used across categories including economy, adhesives and powders; utilisation depends on product formulation. Ramp-up to near 150,000 MT is expected over about 2-2.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 400-500 bps gross margin benefit from VAE still hold?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said exact bps is hard to pin; the category-level benefit is expected to be in a 300-500 bps band, depending on sourcing advantage and formulation.

500820|2026-09.headline: Asian Paints Q2 FY27: decorative volume grew 6.4% and value 14.5%, while gross margin dipped to 41-43% band guidance and PBT margin fell to ~4.8% on inflation lag.
500820|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 volume growth held at about 6.4% on a high base (~11% like-for-like last year) despite two steep price hikes in Q1 and Q2. Decorative value grew 14.5%, and decorative plus industrial value grew about 16.4% with 6.8% volume. Margins were squeezed: standalone PBDIT margin fell to about 17.1% from 18.5% like-for-like, and the gross margin dipped below the 44-45% range as inflation of about 3% outran price increases of about 7% in Q1 and about 5% in Q2. Management pointed to H1 as the more representative period, with H1 standalone PBDIT margin at 19.6% and consolidated at 18.2%.

segments.commentary: Volume ~6.4% and value ~14.5% in Q2; H1 volume ~8% and value ~16%. Rural outgrowing urban; Bath, Kitchen and Weatherseal grew well, White Teak slower. New products are ~18% of revenue.

segments.commentary: Revenue growth about 34% in Q2; PBT up about 10% but margin fell about 309 bps to about 14.2% on inflation and price-increase lag.

Management prefers calibrated pricing to avoid disrupting demand, and says it will not pass on the full inflation at present.

qa_highlights.answer: A gross margin band of about 41% to 43% is the target range, depending on inflation; a further ~3.5% price increase is announced for November.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said H1 margins at standalone and consolidated levels are within the band and the company expects to maintain 18% to 20% for the year, backed by cost excellence and VAE.

qa_highlights.question: What is the VAE benefit and is it available to competitors?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a differentiated VAE, not generic; benefit of 300 bps to 500 bps on relevant products at full potential, with partial benefit in phase 1.
