500825|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue was INR 4,686 crore (+7.1% YoY) and FY26 revenue was INR 18,858 crore (+7.5%). Q4 PAT of INR 678 crore (+21.1%) was lifted by income tax case closures, so underlying profit growth was weaker. Management attributed the India slowdown in March to dual pricing of INR 5 and INR 10 packs after the GST transition, which hit wholesale and rural channels, plus West Asia disruption to international dispatches. Management guided to price increases from this quarter to offset fuel and laminate inflation.

financial_highlights.change: +21.1% YoY; 14.5% of revenue; boosted by income tax case releases

segments.name: Domestic India
segments.commentary: Growth was about 9% to 9.5% in Q4 before dual-pricing drag; management said it expects a few hundred bps of lost sales to recover. Retail (75% of business) is growing well, while wholesale (25%) was hit.

segments.name: E-commerce
segments.commentary: E-commerce was 6% of domestic sales in FY26 versus 4% in FY25, and management put it above 12% excluding the INR 5 and INR 10 packs. Quick commerce is about 70% of e-commerce, which management expects to reach 85%.

segments.name: International (West Asia)
segments.commentary: Revenue and profitability were hit in Q4 by vessel unavailability through the Strait of Hormuz and weaker demand in West Asia markets. Management said the business was negative for March, and Oman production for North America has moved back to Mundra.

segments.name: Adjacencies and signature brands
segments.commentary: Wafers are growing at healthy double digits and dairy at double digits, led by ghee. Treat, Little Hearts and Jim Jam are growing about 3x company growth, and cake and rusk is growing about 1.4x biscuits.

guidance_outlook: Calibrated price increases start from Q1 FY27, through grammage adjustments and some packs above INR 10.
Management expects the domestic market to stabilize by quarter-end as dual pricing fades, and expects wholesale and rural volumes to recover.
Sourcing optimisation between India and international plants is expected to be fully operational by mid-May 2026.
Management expects biscuit industry sequential growth to resume from June with monsoon and school reopening.
Management is committed to continued cost efficiency programmes (CEP) and plans to step up advertising and brand investment, with no quantified FY27 margin guidance.
No specific FY27 revenue or margin number was given; management said it is confident of a good year.
capex_capacity: Manufacturing for North America was moved from Oman back to Mundra, enabling dispatch to North America.
Management is evaluating alternate fuels and energy sources as long-term hedges against fuel supply shocks.
Renewable electricity share in own plants rose 14%, and specific water consumption fell 7%.
Management did not announce new capacity or capex figures.
demand_pricing: Dual pricing of INR 5 and INR 10 packs (competitor selling at INR 4.5 and INR 9) hit rural and wholesale channels from January through March; the 60-65% of biscuits sold at these price points are most exposed.
Management said the gap is about 200 to 400 bps in sales, but it cannot precisely quantify the impact.
Price realisation on the INR 5 and INR 10 segment is lower than the competitor's, so management believes value share is unaffected.

Raw material view: wheat is deflationary but has risen over the past month on rains and quality; palm oil is covered for 5 months; sugar stable; cocoa lower; laminate and fuel (LPG, CNG) are inflationary.
Wheat inventory is covered for about 5.5 to 6 months at attractive prices; palm oil is covered for 5 months.
Other expenses rose 18% on 7% revenue growth, driven by higher advertising and brand investment.

qa_highlights.question: Why was standalone growth lower in Q4 when Nov-Dec ran at about 12% and Jan-Feb at about 9%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the first two months of Q4 were reasonable, with dual pricing in rural and wholesale channels hitting throughout the quarter, and West Asia pulling March down. Domestic growth was about 9% to 9.5% before the dual-pricing drag.

qa_highlights.question: How much did dual pricing dampen sales growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was hypothetical to quantify, but the impact was roughly 200 to 400 bps. Growth in general trade key accounts is high-single to double digit, modern trade is about 15% to 16%, and e-commerce is above 50%.

qa_highlights.question: What pricing action is needed given competitors are vacating INR 4.5 and INR 9 packs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will take selective price increases through grammage adjustments and some packs above INR 10. Other biscuit companies are moving gradually to full price points.

qa_highlights.question: Is Britannia under-indexed on INR 5 and INR 10 packs in e-commerce?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not actively promote these packs online because premium packs drive more value and channel conflict is a concern. The packs remain available through search and in baskets.

qa_highlights.question: Will GST cut benefits reach biscuits, and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the GST benefit is less visible on INR 5 and INR 10 packs than on higher price points. It expects benefits to show more in medium to long term, with the growth recovery in June.

qa_highlights.question: What is Q4 volume growth and how do pack counts look?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume growth was about 5.5% by grammage. It acknowledged that transactions fell in wholesale and rural channels and expects this to correct over the next few months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin outlook for FY27 given cost pressures and higher investment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will be selective on marketing spend, targeting the marketing mix for better returns, and expects to manage margins within a certain band. No quantified FY27 margin guidance was given.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company pursue inorganic growth and new platforms?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is actively scanning acquisitions that add new capabilities or address unmet needs, and that more platforms will be added, including health.

risks_watch: Recovery of dual-pricing-hit wholesale and rural channels and whether the INR 5 and INR 10 price points normalise.
Q4 PAT includes income tax case releases, so the reported 21.1% PAT growth is not recurring.
Fuel and laminate inflation, plus West Asia shipping and LPG constraints, could pressure margins and international operations.
Competitor (number 2 player) reported double-digit volume growth, which may signal share loss in INR 5 and INR 10 channels.
Rising other expenses (+18% YoY) from brand investment could weigh on margins in FY27.
Price increases could affect volumes, which management argues will remain resilient.
500825|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on medium-term recovery and cost discipline, but cautious and sometimes vague on near-term numbers. Management avoided quantifying the dual-pricing impact and FY27 guidance, and said the outcome depends on execution.
key_quotes: So, there will be calibrated price increases starting from this quarter.
And we are very confident that in very short period of time, these channels will also come back to normalcy.
So we had a volume growth of close to 5.5% upwards.
I think we have to keep going stronger on market share, but like we said that we are also adept at managing margins.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Operating profit grew only 6% on 7.1% revenue growth in Q4, FY26 margin was 17.0%, and management plans to step up advertising while facing fuel and laminate inflation; calibrated price increases from Q1 FY27 are the offset but are unquantified.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q4 volume grew about 5.5% by grammage, domestic ex-West Asia grew 9-9.5% before dual pricing, and management expects biscuit sequential growth to resume from June, but price increases could dent volumes.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management did not announce new capacity or capex figures, and no utilisation level was disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No FY27 revenue or margin number was given, and management's cost and marketing plans point to margin pressure rather than upside.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Dual pricing cost an estimated 200-400 bps of sales in Jan-Mar, West Asia was negative in March, and other expenses rose 18% on 7% revenue growth, so near-term numbers could slip.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management is adding platforms including health and is growing Treat, Little Hearts and Jim Jam at about 3x company growth, though no specific launch date was named.

rows.label: Calibrated price increases from Q1 FY27
rows.why: Management guided to grammage adjustments and some packs above INR 10 to offset fuel and laminate inflation, with competitors vacating INR 4.5 and INR 9 price points.

rows.label: Domestic channel recovery by quarter-end
rows.why: Dual pricing hit wholesale (25% of business) and rural channels, and management expects stabilisation by quarter-end, but the 200-400 bps drag is not precisely quantified.

rows.label: North America supply restored via Mundra
rows.why: Manufacturing moved from Oman back to Mundra and India-international sourcing optimisation is due by mid-May 2026, but West Asia was negative in March and vessel access through Hormuz remains constrained.

tone.note: Management was confident on medium-term recovery, pricing and cost discipline, but vague on near-term numbers, avoiding quantifying dual-pricing impact and FY27 guidance; analysts pushed on the INR 5/10 pack dynamics, margin outlook amid higher marketing spend, and e-commerce under-indexing.

500825|2026-06.headline: Britannia Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 9.5% to INR 4,964 crore, with ~9% tonnage volume growth and PAT margin at 11.9%.
500825|2026-06.overview: Management said revenue from operations on a consolidated basis was about INR 4,964 crore, up 9.5% YoY, with standalone growth at 10%. PAT was 11.9% of revenue and grew 13.6% YoY. Management said the quarter exited in mid-teens growth after dual-pricing disruption in rural and wholesale channels faded in June. Input cost inflation from LPG/PNG, palm oil, sugar and milk is a headwind, and management said only about half of it has been offset through price increases so far.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 52 crore last year, as stated by an analyst
none booked in FY26 or Q1 FY27

segments.name: General Trade (GT)
segments.commentary: Management said GT demand picked up, with the recent run-rate about 1.5x the full-year FY26 growth rate. Key states are growing and other states are growing about 1.3x faster.

segments.name: E-commerce / Quick commerce
segments.commentary: E-commerce grew at strong double digits. Quick commerce is about 80-85% of e-commerce and is growing at healthy double digits.

segments.name: Other channels
segments.commentary: Newer channels were growing at about 2.5x the GT rate overall.

segments.name: Dairy and adjacencies
segments.commentary: Dairy grew at double digits. Cake, rusk and wafers grew at double digits led by portfolio innovation. Croissant lines were growing above 30% and Croissant run-rate was about INR 200 crore annualised (INR 100 crore ARR doubled).

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Mixed quarter: pressure in Middle East and Saudi Arabia and headwinds in North America, offset by growth in Africa led by Kenya. Management expects a return to growth from this quarter.

segments.name: Eastern India
segments.commentary: Growing in double digits per management.

guidance_outlook: Management did not give explicit FY27 guidance. It said the team is confident of a good year, defined as balanced growth across volume, value and profitability.
Management expects roughly 1.5-2% more price realisation from shrinkflation changes to come through in the coming quarters, after about 1% in Q1.
Management said it is watching sugar, palm oil, milk and LPG/PNG costs ahead of the festive season and said the current cost level is higher than in February 2026.
Management said Q2 faces a base effect in September from the GST price transition last year, and July and August were normal months.
Brand-building spend is running ahead of sales growth, with no percentage given.
capex_capacity: Management said it is working to reduce LPG/PNG dependence through biomass and alternate fuels, but no timelines were given.
Renewable energy share in plant power rose 16%, and management is working to expand it under state rules.
A new Chief Business Officer for Dairy was appointed and a Strategy and Corporate Development head joined, with management saying the leadership team is now complete.
demand_pricing: Q1 volume growth was about 9% in tonnage terms; pricing contributed about 1% and was mainly shrinkflation in INR 5 and INR 10 packs.
Management said dual pricing disruption in rural and wholesale was felt in April and early May and ended in June. Demand was described as holding up.
Industrial fuel inflation was steep: LPG and PNG roughly 2.5x in April-May, now about 1.5x February levels. Palm oil is near INR 140 per kg, up more than 20%.
Management said it could mitigate about half of input inflation through price increases so far.
Sugar rose more than INR 7 per kg in the last 2-3 weeks. Flour has held up, but El Nino and rainfall are a watch item for wheat prices.
Management said it has regained market share on a sequential basis across many biscuit categories, following the end of dual pricing.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the mid-teens exit growth in June, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company sells in based on sell-out, so no loading. The dual-pricing impact ended in June, which brought back some buyers, and organic demand held up. It gave no forward indication.

qa_highlights.question: How will ad spend and input inflation affect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said LPG prices are about 1.5x February levels and sugar and palm oil are also up. Brand spend is ahead of sales growth, with no percentage given. Management said half of inflation has been offset by price increases.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 EBITDA margin hold at or above FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the input cost base is higher than in February. It did not commit to full-year margins, but said it is confident of managing levers across value, volume and margin.

qa_highlights.question: Are there PLI benefits in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said no PLI incentive was booked in FY26 or Q1 FY27, because the threshold growth was not achieved.

qa_highlights.question: How is Britannia responding to GT competition in Eastern India and other areas?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited regional empowerment, targeted media and influencer spend, and local product innovation such as Milk Bikis Thirukkural packs in Tamil Nadu. Sub-distributors are being converted to direct distributors.

qa_highlights.question: How big is the GST impact on volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said over 60% of sales are at INR 5 and INR 10 price points, so GST-cut elasticity will be gradual and smaller than for higher-priced packs.

risks_watch: Input cost inflation: LPG/PNG, palm oil, sugar and milk, with festive-season sugar pressure and monsoon/El Nino risk to wheat and flour.
Margin pressure from higher brand spend and only partial pass-through of input costs (about half so far).
International business: Middle East, Saudi Arabia and North America remain weak, and geopolitical developments are uncertain.
Whether the mid-teens exit growth and 9% volume growth can be sustained after dual-pricing normalisation.
Competitive intensity in GT, plus a September GST base effect in Q2.
Health and regulatory shift toward healthy snacking; management is building a health and protein platform, with no timelines given.
500825|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on demand and the GT recovery, but cautious on input costs and margins. Management gave no numerical FY27 margin or volume guidance and declined to forecast beyond Q1.
key_quotes: So we have exited the quarter on a very positive note.
At best, we have been able to mitigate half of the inflation through price increases.
So you should not hold it on to the P&L like a permanent phenomenon.
So the wholesale channel and the rural channel, where the dual pricing had an impact is now over, and we see that the throughput, both in terms of selling in and selling out is very good.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Input costs are higher than February 2026 (LPG/PNG about 1.5x February, palm oil up more than 20%, sugar up more than INR 7/kg in 2-3 weeks) and only about half of inflation is offset by price, while brand spend runs ahead of sales growth.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new plant, line or capacity addition was discussed; only renewable power share rose 16% and LPG/PNG dependence reduction has no timeline.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q1 tonnage grew close to 9%, the quarter exited in mid-teens growth after dual pricing ended in June, and GT run-rate is about 1.5x FY26 growth, though Q2 faces a September GST base effect.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management discussed no new capex; the only capacity-related item is a renewable energy push under state rules, with no capex size or timing given.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No numeric FY27 guidance was given and management declined to forecast beyond Q1, with cost headwinds rising into the festive season.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management is watching sugar, palm oil, milk and LPG/PNG costs ahead of the festive season, only about half of input inflation is priced in, and the Q2 September GST base effect is a headwind.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Croissant lines are growing above 30% with an annualised run-rate of about INR 200 crore, dairy grew at double digits, and a health and protein platform is being built with no timeline.

rows.label: Shrinkflation price realisation of 1.5-2% to come through
rows.why: Pricing contributed about 1% in Q1 mainly from shrinkflation in INR 5 and INR 10 packs, and management expects roughly 1.5-2% more in coming quarters.

rows.label: International recovery from Africa offset by Middle East and North America weakn
rows.why: Management expects a return to growth from this quarter, but Middle East, Saudi Arabia and North America are under pressure and Kenya is driving Africa growth, with no figures given.

rows.label: PLI incentive not booked
rows.why: No PLI incentive was booked in FY26 or Q1 FY27 because the threshold growth was not achieved, so no upside is assumed.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand recovery, exit-rate mid-teens growth and GT momentum, but cautious on input cost inflation and margins and gave no FY27 numeric guidance; analysts probed sustainability of June growth, ad spend versus margin, and FY27 margin versus FY26.

500825|2026-09.headline: Britannia Q2 FY27 revenue rose 16.6% YoY to INR 5,542 crore, with PAT at 13% of revenue and H1 revenue crossing INR 10,000 crore.
500825|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR 5,542 crore, up 16.6% YoY and 11.6% QoQ, with PAT up 10.2% YoY and 13% margin on revenue. H1 revenue was INR 10,506 crore (up 13.1%), the first time H1 crossed INR 10,000 crore. Volume growth was 13% on a low base of minus 3%, and General Trade (GT) accelerated, with management attributing part of this to a GST transition base effect worth 1.5-2%. Input costs (wheat flour, palm oil, sugar, milk, laminate, fuel) rose sharply YoY, and a 3.5% price increase was implemented in the quarter with more in the pipeline.

financial_highlights.value: Growth as stated 8.5% YoY; management cited operating profit margin around 17%

segments.name: General Trade (GT)
segments.commentary: GT growth in Q2 FY27 is 2.6x the full-year FY26 growth rate, per management; GT is the largest part of the business. Growth described as uniform across opportunity and mature states, with rural and semi-urban strong.

segments.name: E-commerce
segments.commentary: E-commerce is trending at close to 7% of overall sales (FY26 about 6%); management says it would be in double digits excluding INR 5 pack sales, and the company is treating it as a separate business unit.

segments.name: Other channels (modern trade, alternate, e-commerce)
segments.commentary: Growing at a rate significantly above GT, per management.

segments.name: Adjacency bakery business
segments.commentary: Grew more than 20%, led by croissant and cake; rusk growing slower. Dairy: cheese performing better (flavoured slices launched about 1.5 months earlier); Sattvam Ghee and Winkin' Cow milk drink trending well.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Recovered after Q1 disruption from Middle East war; Middle East Africa and rest of International both grew in good double digits, though Middle East costs remain high due to freight premiums.

segments.name: Biscuits share of portfolio
segments.commentary: Biscuits about 78-80% of total sales, with non-biscuit portfolio expected to grow faster.

guidance_outlook: Further price increases (activation/shrinkflation-led) are in the works; the 3.5% taken in the quarter covers only part of cost inflation, and management aims to close the gap with subsequent increases; implementation takes about 1.5-2 months.
Management declined to guide on future gross margin trajectory, saying inflation is expected to persist and events are hard to predict.
Grammage reduction is expected to weigh on volumes going ahead, though management remains confident in the volume growth story.
Future health and protein platforms are in development; no launch timelines given to protect competitive position.
Cost optimisation programmes to continue this year to limit pass-through to consumers.
capex_capacity: No capacity, capex or commissioning figures were discussed in the call.
Renewable electricity share in own plants at 48%, constrained by state government caps on renewable usage.
Women make up 45% of factory workforce; Britannia Nutrition Foundation reached about 5.73 lakh beneficiaries in H1.
demand_pricing: Input costs YoY: wheat flour marginally down; refined palm oil up 17%; sugar up 6%; milk up 16%; laminate up 18%; fuel up 45%. QoQ: wheat flour up 9%, palm oil up 11%, sugar up 4%, milk up 2%, laminate up 7%.
Price increase of 3.5% implemented in Q2; further increases planned. Industry migrated from INR 4.5 fractional pricing to INR 5 and INR 10 price points around May-June 2026.
Management says shelf space has been regained versus Malkist and others after odd-pricing period; NutriChoice Zero growing in strong double digits.

Competition: Malkist (cracker segment, Cheeze Dipped launched by Britannia to compete), and Reliance entering biscuits starting in Tamil Nadu; management says INR 5 and INR 10 price points are harder to disrupt than in cola.
GST-related transition in September last year contributed a base effect of at most 1.5-2% at quarter level.

qa_highlights.question: Are there further price increases beyond the 3.5% taken, and how should gross margins evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 3.5% came through, more price increases are in the works, and the 3.5% covers only part of inflation; it declined to predict gross margin direction.

qa_highlights.question: Is the GT pickup a base effect or sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Partly base effect (September transition month, impact up to 1.5-2% of quarter), but management also cited resilient GT consumption in semi-urban and rural areas and better own execution; Vipin Kataria said growth is uniform and sustainable.

qa_highlights.question: Are you back to pre-odd-pricing market share?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; management said Britannia has regained shelf space and share, and the INR 4.5 price point has disappeared from the market.

qa_highlights.question: What is the e-commerce potential and is it a major growth driver?
qa_highlights.answer: E-commerce at about 7% of sales; management is treating it as a business unit with channel-specific products and sees premiumisation as the key lever; urban e-commerce already in double digits.

qa_highlights.question: How do you see wheat coverage and the next crop?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Britannia is an efficient wheat buyer, has historically beaten the market with mark-to-market gains, and is watching a challenging monsoon for the next wheat season; no specific coverage percentage given.

qa_highlights.question: Biscuit vs non-biscuit mix and medium-term growth shape?
qa_highlights.answer: Biscuits are about 78-80% of sales; growth to come from core innovation, higher-margin adjacencies, healthier and Gen Z-targeted products, e-commerce and premiumisation.

risks_watch: Sustained input inflation (palm oil, milk, laminate, sugar, fuel) with only 3.5% price increase so far; gross margin pressure likely to persist.
Volume impact from planned grammage reduction as price increases are taken.
Reliance entry into biscuits starting in Tamil Nadu and fierce competition with Malkist in the cracker segment.
Middle East freight and cost headwinds in International business.
Wheat crop outlook given challenging monsoon; next season's wheat cost.
500825|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on top-line and volume momentum, but cautious and deliberately non-committal on gross margins, input cost trajectory and future launch timelines, which management withheld citing competition and uncertainty.
key_quotes: Yes, it is a scenario where you are seeing a high level of inflation, and inflation is there to stay.
Obviously, the cost inflation is more than what, and this has only covered part of it.
We have regained our shelf space. We have regained and done better on the share.
Britannia as an organization is extremely bullish on e-commerce.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Input costs up sharply YoY (palm oil +17%, milk +16%, laminate +18%, fuel +45%) against only a 3.5% price increase, and management declined to guide on gross margin direction.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No capacity, capex or commissioning figures were discussed in the call.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q2 volume grew 13% on a -3% base, but a 1.5-2% GST base effect flatters the quarter and planned grammage cuts and further price hikes are expected to weigh on volumes ahead.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed and no utilisation figure was given.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No formal guidance was given, management declined to guide on gross margins, and cost inflation exceeds the 3.5% price increase taken so far.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Sustained input inflation with only 3.5% pricing so far, Middle East freight costs and Reliance's Tamil Nadu entry create margin and volume risk, though no formal guidance exists to cut.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Health and protein platforms are in development with no launch timeline, while Cheeze Dipped and flavoured cheese slices are already launched and bakery adjacencies grew more than 20%.

rows.label: Further price increases to close inflation gap
rows.why: Management said more activation/shrinkflation-led price hikes are in the works, with a 1.5-2 month implementation lag, because the 3.5% taken covers only part of cost inflation.

rows.label: Cost optimisation programmes continue
rows.why: Management said cost optimisation will continue this year to limit pass-through to consumers, though no savings quantum was given.

rows.label: E-commerce as separate business unit
rows.why: E-commerce is about 7% of sales (FY26 about 6%) and runs in double digits excluding INR 5 packs, with premiumisation as the stated lever.

tone.note: Management was confident on volume momentum, GT growth and share regain, but cautious and non-committal on gross margins, input cost trajectory and launch timelines; analysts pushed on whether GT growth is base-driven and on margin direction.

500830|2026-03.headline: Colgate India Q4 FY26 revenue rose 9% to Rs 1,583 crore, with domestic growth at 9.2% and gross margin at 69.6%.
500830|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 net sales were Rs 1,583 crore, up 9% YoY, with domestic growth of 9.2% and growth broad-based across Core, Premium, toothpaste, toothbrush and personal care. Full-year FY26 sales were flat at Rs 5,984 crore, and full-year EBITDA margin was 31.2% including an 80 bps GST input-credit (IDS) impact. Q4 NPAT was Rs 353 crore, and excluding one-offs (restructuring, GST, prior-period tax refunds, labour code) management said profit grew about 9%. Management declared an interim dividend of Rs 48 per share and said it is still paying out virtually 100% of NPAT.

financial_highlights.change: excluding one-offs, management says profit grew about 9%
absolute spend up 10%; FY26 13.7% of sales
stated as improved on prior years despite GST-blocked capital

segments.name: Toothpaste (Core: Colgate Strong Teeth, Max Fresh)
segments.commentary: Max Fresh is described as the fastest-growing franchise in the portfolio, with a blue variant in testing and new Sensorials variants (berry added). Management said consideration for all sub-brands is flat or rising versus original levels.

segments.name: Premium (Colgate Total, Visible White, PerioGard)
segments.commentary: Premium mix is up 35% over the past two years per management. Visible White Purple was launched 18 months ago and is described as the most successful launch in Colgate's history; PerioGard franchise is said to be doubling YoY. Management did not disclose the premium share of sales; e-commerce is about 10% of business.

segments.name: Toothbrush
segments.commentary: Management says Colgate is 1.7x its nearest competitor in the entry tier. New launches include a Rs 10 brush with 16g to 20g of toothpaste offered in the pack and a PerioGuard brush.

segments.name: Personal care (Palmolive)
segments.commentary: Palmolive focus is hand wash and body wash. Management said foaming hand wash is the leader in the category and growing at double digits in key channels; body wash is a partnership-led watch item.

guidance_outlook: Gross margin is expected to stay in the range seen in recent quarters over the next two quarters despite commodity and currency headwinds, offset by the Funding the Growth programme.
EBITDA is not guided to a specific level or expansion; it will be calibrated to advertising investment, with top-line growth and absolute profit as the stated priorities.
A price increase to offset the post-West Asia inflation is expected to be taken within a few weeks; category price increases are expected to be in the low single digits.
Management targets balanced volume and price-led growth but gave no numerical growth target.
Management is pursuing GST input-credit mitigation through supplier duty representations, refunds in non-manufacturing states, and transporter rate changes.
Brand investment is expected to rise further from the Q4 level of 12.6% of sales; FY26 was 13.7%.
capex_capacity: No capacity, utilisation or capex figures were disclosed in the call.
Direct outlets reach is 1.7 lakh; 2 lakh stores were added to reach in 2025.
Plant sustainability: recyclable tubes now fully adopted, renewable energy share moved from 40% to 60%, plastic neutrality at 101%, recyclable/reusable/compostable packaging at 95%.
demand_pricing: Q4 growth was balanced between price and volume, and management said Q4 volume was flat.
Post-GST price cuts have been lapped after the Q1 calendar 2026 anniversary, so the price increase is now needed for input-cost inflation.
Rural demand is recovering and is beginning to converge with urban growth, though rural is growing more slowly than in 2025.
Promotional intensity has not eased; management is using AI tools to cull promotions and redeploying the spend.
Premium portfolio is growing faster than the core; management cited the 130-140 index to the core as the premium threshold.
Quick commerce share is ahead of total e-commerce, which is ahead of the offline business.

qa_highlights.question: How has the QR-linked dentist recommendation programme helped premiumisation, and how is B2B sales to dentists growing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 4.5 million people were scanned, with around 20% of scans going to a dentist; the programme is being repeated and expanded to a virtual format via QR codes on 500 packs. B2B sales to the profession grew at about a 50-60% two-year CAGR, with a field force of about 150 people.

qa_highlights.question: Competitors have launched similar products (for example Purple); is the market expanding and what is the D2C threat?

For FY26, consolidated revenue grew 8% and EBITDA 3%; reported PAT fell on a one-time Rs 30 Cr wage code impact and the Mashobra fair-value charge from the prior year, and management said excluding these profit grew 2%. Management said April and May trends were better than expected, led by domestic demand.

qa_highlights.question: Will large events like BRICS and the Aviation show boost RevPAR?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, large events have a ripple effect across cities, with Delhi and Mumbai benefiting from overseas visitors to Bengaluru's air show.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Kolkata Oberoi delayed and how firm is the new timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Heritage building restoration uncovered fire and structural safety work, plus a Kolkata construction halt after a fatal incident about two months ago; halt still in place pending building-by-building approvals.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a cost overrun on the Oberoi Grand from delays?
qa_highlights.answer: Delays add cost, the size depending on reasons, and the bigger impact is deferred revenue and profit from delayed market entry.

qa_highlights.question: Can the Mumbai outperformance continue, and what is foreign tourist trend in recent months?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Bombay market was strong and EIH beat it, but would not forecast 20% outperformance; Q2 foreign trend expected to stay weak.

qa_highlights.question: Rajgarh stabilisation timeline and winter outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: About 3 years to stabilise for a leisure hotel, with winter months from October expected to do considerably better.

qa_highlights.question: How much did the base business margin fall after adjusting for Rajgarh and one-offs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ex-Rajgarh margin was about 30.6% vs last year, with roughly Rs 9 crore YoY impact from power and fuel, Rs 4 crore marketing, IT and renovation costs. Management declined to disclose management fee income.

risks_watch: Margin recovery depends on Oberoi Rajgarh ramp-up; management guides about 3 years to stabilise and expects winter months from October to be considerably better.
Foreign arrivals were about 10% below last year in Q1 and management expects Q2 foreign trend to stay weak; normalisation in Q3-Q4 depends on West Asia stabilising.
Power and fuel costs rose due to the West Asia/Hormuz crisis; ex-Rajgarh impact about Rs 9 crore YoY, with cost pressure expected to persist.

Kolkata Oberoi timeline pushed to 2029 with construction halt still in place pending building-by-building approvals; Oberoi Grand opening Sept 2028 with management declining to give percentage completion.
Employee cost pressure from headcount, increments, labour code impact and working-hour reduction commitment; management declined to quantify Rajgarh revenue or management fee income.
key_quotes: What has stood out for us is strong domestic demand.
If we exclude Rajgarh, our RevPAR growth was 11.4%.
So, due to all those reasons, our EBITDA was not in line with the revenue.
I really don't want to comment on whether it's going to be 20% going forward but our endeavor is always to do the best we can.
500840|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on domestic demand, brand share and the Mumbai and Trident performance, but guarded on forward numbers: management declined to give full-year guidance or quantify Rajgarh revenue, flight catering margin and management fees. Explanations for the EBITDA gap were given in detail, while delays at Kolkata and Oberoi Grand were attributed to external factors and timelines were presented with limited firmness.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Ex-Rajgarh margin was about 30.6% but consolidated margin fell (EBITDA Rs 207 crore on Rs 698 crore, roughly 29-30%); recovery depends on Rajgarh winter months from October and on power and fuel costs (about Rs 9 crore YoY ex-Rajgarh) which management expects to persist.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Oberoi Grand (197 keys) is expected to open September 2028 and Oberoi London in 2028, with about 30 new properties by 2031; the near-term additions are mostly beyond the window, and Kolkata slipped to 2029.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q2 business on books versus last year was described as very positive, occupancy was up 2-4% and ARR up 6-8% in the industry, and EIH RGI rose to 125 from 121; foreign arrivals were about 10% below last year and Q2 foreign trend is expected to stay weak.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Q1 capex was Rs 148 crore on already planned projects, and the Hebbal development (over 1.3 million sq ft) and Wildflower auction (qualifying date 10 September 2026) are pending, but no new capex plan was stated and management gave no utilisation figure.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management gave no full-year guidance and declined to forecast the full year, and foreign arrivals were about 10% below last year with Q2 expected to stay weak.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Kolkata Oberoi slipped to 2029 with the construction halt still in place, Oberoi Grand delay costs are unquantified, and the Rajgarh ramp-up is about 3 years to stabilise.

rows.label: Oberoi Rajgarh ramp-up and winter season
rows.why: Management expects winter months from October to be considerably better, but stabilisation takes about 3 years for a leisure hotel, so margin drag from Rajgarh persists in the window.

rows.label: Kolkata construction halt and Oberoi Kolkata delay to 2029
rows.why: A construction halt after a fatal incident about two months ago is still in place pending building-by-building approvals, and the opening has been pushed to 2029.

rows.label: Industry event demand (BRICS, Aviation show)
rows.why: Management said large events have a ripple effect across cities and industry ARR gains are expected from limited supply and MICE events later in the year.

tone.note: Management was confident on domestic demand, Trident and Mumbai share gains and Q2 bookings, but guarded on forward numbers, declining full-year guidance, Rajgarh revenue, flight catering margin and management fees; analysts pressed on margin drag, Kolkata delay and Oberoi Grand cost overrun.

500850|2026-03.headline: IHCL Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 14% to INR2,845 crores with EBITDA margin of 37%; FY27 guidance is double-digit (12-14%) revenue growth.
500850|2026-03.overview: IHCL reported its 16th consecutive quarter of record performance, with Q4 consolidated revenue up 14% YoY to INR2,845 crores and EBITDA up 15% to INR1,052 crores. Standalone Q4 RevPAR grew 12%, the company said, with standalone EBITDA margin up 160 bps to 49.5%. For FY26, consolidated revenue grew 16% to INR9,971 crores and consolidated PAT crossed INR2,000 crores for the first time. Management said March and early April were weak due to the West Asia conflict, with recovery from mid-April, and guided FY27 revenue growth of 12-14%, with Q1 FY27 growth expected above 12%.

segments.name: Standalone hotels
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR1,721 crores with 12% RevPAR growth and 49.5% EBITDA margin; FY26 revenue INR5,640 crores (+10%) and EBITDA margin 45.1% (+120 bps).

segments.name: New businesses (Ginger, Qmin, Ama, Stays & Trails, Tree of Life)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR753 crores, up 25%, with a 31% four-year CAGR. Ginger Mumbai Airport crossed INR100 crores revenue at a 56% EBITDA margin; Qmin has 100-plus outlets and GMV near INR200 crores.

segments.name: TajSATS (catering)
segments.commentary: Revenue growth of 16% was flattered by an airport levy accounting change; management said growth would have been about 11-12% on a like-for-like basis.

segments.name: Ginger consolidated (Roots and Ginger Mumbai Airport)
segments.commentary: Combined revenue about INR700-709 crores with a very high EBITDA margin; management now reports Ginger on a consolidated basis rather than Roots standalone.

guidance_outlook: FY27 double-digit revenue growth guided at 12-14%, with management confident of delivering it.
Like-for-like RevPAR planned at high-single-digit growth (about 7-9%) on a one- to two-year view; ARR is the main lever.
Non-like-for-like growth of about 4-5% expected in FY27 from around 60 hotel openings, and acquisitions expected to add over INR250 crores incremental revenue.
Q1 FY27 revenue growth expected to be above 12%, with domestic demand stronger than international.
Capex of INR1,000-1,200 crores annually; Ginger portfolio target of 250 hotels under development or operating by end-FY27.
Next Capital Market Day to be announced within weeks; capital-light share guided at 63% on the prior framework, with ANK & Pride amendments pointing toward about 70%.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex over INR1,000 crores: about INR650 crores on renovations, routine maintenance and digital, and the rest on greenfield projects.
Over the last three years, more than INR2,500 crores invested in capex; more than INR500 crores deployed across four acquisitions.
Portfolio of over 630 hotels and 64,000-plus keys; pipeline of 31,000-plus keys, 93% capital-light; 68% of operating portfolio under managed or asset-light formats.
FY27 openings of about 60 hotels (around 5,000 keys, give or take 5%); Frankfurt delayed to around June 2026; 15 ANK & Pride conversions expected to open in Q1 FY27.
Atmantan and ANK & Pride integration on track, with benefits expected in H2 FY27; President Mumbai renovation completed.
demand_pricing: Goa grew about 25% in April (some hotels 30%+); Mumbai and Delhi face high bases after strong prior years; Dubai and Maldives are down, London is okay, and domestic is strong.
West Asia conflict cost about INR40-50 crores of consolidated revenue and close to INR100 crores on an enterprise basis from last-minute event cancellations and rescheduling.

Foreign tourists are about 30% of standalone guests and this share has not moved much; management says foreign business arrivals are rising while leisure tourist arrivals remain below pre-COVID levels.
Rupee-denominated portal pricing; domestic drive vacations and MICE consolidation into domestic resorts are supporting demand.

Management says supply is tight for the foreseeable future, so RevPAR should grow at least at inflation; revenue management and a website channel shift added about 2 percentage points to distribution mix.
Lands End Mumbai runs at 90%+ occupancy, so growth there is rate-led.

qa_highlights.question: How are April and current trading, and what drives FY27 growth of 12-14%?
qa_highlights.answer: March and early April were difficult, with stability from mid-April and strong growth since. Management built the guide from key account rates, wedding bookings on the books, about 4-5% non-like-for-like growth from openings, and renovated inventory; ARR is the swing factor.

qa_highlights.question: Did the company cut the FY27 openings count?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the figure is roughly 5,000 keys on average per year, give or take 5%. Platform partnerships could add 300-400 keys, and most openings are management contracts, so the P&L impact is small.

qa_highlights.question: Does the ANK & Pride portfolio change the long-term capital-light mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the mix moved toward 70% capital-light from the 63% target at the Analyst Day, because ANK & Pride is largely capital-light with only a few owned hotels. The change is additive and does not reflect any sale of capital-heavy assets.

qa_highlights.question: How will margins evolve and is there operating leverage left?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is still room for margin improvement because the newer brands are still scaling and acquisition costs were high. It is comfortable with the 35% consolidated margin provided new brands are not built with upfront capex.

qa_highlights.question: What is Q1 FY27 trading and the MICE cancellation impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects Q1 revenue growth above 12%, with domestic outpacing international. Some MICE business was deferred rather than lost, such as the company's own hospitality conference; some nights are permanently lost.

risks_watch: West Asia conflict and its effect on international travel, Dubai transit traffic and London hotels.
Aviation cost and capacity cuts by domestic carriers, which could hit travel demand and pricing.
Frankfurt opening slipping to around June 2026 and the pace of the 60-hotel opening plan.
Mumbai and Delhi high bases, which could slow like-for-like growth.
Clarity of the new Capital Market Day guidance on ROCE and the capital-light mix.
500850|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on the medium term, with guidance tempered by explicit caution on West Asia impacts in March-April. Management was candid on the weak start to Q1 and deflected some questions on specific numbers, e.g. the segment breakdown and the 7-9% ARR bridge, saying they are an art rather than a science.
key_quotes: We remain fairly confident that we will again deliver double-digit growth between 12%, let's say, and 14% in the FY '27 fiscal.
The business was a bit sluggish. I would say March was a difficult month. Beginning of April was difficult.
This time, we have none, and we have a lot of cash. So, it might throw other opportunities.

rows.why: About 60 hotel openings (~5,000 keys, +/-5%) guided for FY27, 15 ANK & Pride conversions due to open in Q1 FY27, and Frankfurt slipping to around June 2026; non-like-for-like growth of 4-5% is built in.

rows.why: Management expects Q1 growth above 12% with domestic outpacing international, and Goa grew about 25% in April; but March-April was weak and Mumbai and Delhi face high bases.

500850|2026-06.headline: IHCL Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 15% to INR2,419 crores and PAT 21% to INR358 crores, with EBITDA margin at 31.1%.
500850|2026-06.overview: IHCL reported its 17th consecutive quarter of record performance, with consolidated revenue up 15% YoY to INR2,419 crores, EBITDA up 18% to INR753 crores and PAT up 21% to INR358 crores. Domestic RevPAR grew 14% and hotel segment revenue 17%, driven by leisure markets like Rajasthan and Goa while international properties, especially Dubai, lagged due to West Asia disruption. Standalone revenue grew 18% to INR1,298 crores with EBITDA up 30% to INR542 crores and margin of 41.8%. Management reiterated double-digit revenue growth for the year and said July and early Q2 trends were strong.

financial_highlights.change: c.+6 pts YoY (analyst cited 35% to 39%ish; mgmt said margin up 0.5%)

segments.name: Hotels
segments.commentary: Hotel segment revenue grew 17% and makes up about 87% of business; domestic RevPAR grew 14%, with double-digit RevPAR growth across all brands. Margin held at 32.6% despite about INR15 crores of Frankfurt ramp-up and TajSATS Noida kitchen costs.

segments.name: Growth brands (Ginger, Qmin, ama, Tree of Life)
segments.commentary: Ginger consolidated revenue INR183 crores, up 20% YoY with 39% EBITDA margin. Ama has 380+ bungalows, 196 operational; Tree of Life has 40+ resorts, 23 operational; Qmin at 100+ outlets.

segments.name: Acquisitions (Brij, Atmantan)
segments.commentary: Brij's 11 operational hotels generated INR11 crores revenue, up 42% YoY. Atmantan delivered INR19 crores consolidated revenue, up 19% YoY.

segments.name: TajSATS / air catering
segments.commentary: Air catering revenue rose 3% while EBITDA fell 1%, as second-largest airline capacity cuts hit flight catering volumes; non-flight catering grew mid-20s% at lower margin.

capex_capacity: Operational hotels at 382 with about 265 in pipeline; 20 hotels signed and 11 opened in Q1, 17 of signings under Gateway, Ginger and Tree of Life.
Frankfurt new asset ramping up, with pre-opening and start-up costs weighing on Q1 and July-August.
Taj Ganges Varanasi new 100-room wing commissioned March 2026, PBT-positive in first quarter, revenue up 44% and EBITDA margin 40%.
Taj Bandstand (Mumbai) targeted for 2030-2031 with about 450 keys and INR1,000 crores revenue; excavation 95% complete.
Ginger Bangalore Airport and a 350-room Ginger/Vivanta combo in 12-14 months; 300-room Ginger at Mopa Airport Goa under construction; Kolkata Airport Ginger under construction.
First of three lodges opened in Kruger National Park; two more to follow in about 12 months.
demand_pricing: Leisure markets strong: Rajasthan RevPAR up high 20s to 27-29%, Goa ARRs up double digit; big city hotels up low to mid-teens.
Standalone occupancy 82% vs 76% in the previous quarter; occupancy up about 6% on comparable domestic base.
Taj Palace room revenue up 32% and Fort Aguada room revenue up 45% after renovations.
International: Dubai business at about 80% of prior revenue in total (JLT 60%), Taj Exotica Palm below 50%; San Francisco recovering; New York pipe-burst cut 49 rooms.
Wedding and banqueting subdued; Africa Summit cancelled a week before start in May, hitting Delhi F&B and conference; government MICE slowed.

qa_highlights.question: Are MICE and domestic demand shifts from international travel accelerating into H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said trends continue into Q2 with no softening; leisure markets outperforming, and foreign arrivals still needed in Q3-Q4 for the sector.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone employee cost rise only 0.6% YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed it to a reversal from labour code benefits; normal payroll increases are 7-8%.

qa_highlights.question: Will full-year growth reach the upper end of 12-14% guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 is tracking ahead, with July stronger than Q1; it hopes to beat, but gave no explicit guidance raise.

qa_highlights.question: How will Frankfurt be accounted for?
qa_highlights.answer: Full revenue is booked; the asset's impact turns positive from September, after pre-opening costs in July and August.

qa_highlights.question: What is the international strategy and capital intent?
qa_highlights.answer: Capital-light model only, with no hotel purchases; leases on institutional-style returns of 5-7% and brand-led renovations in Singapore, Switzerland and London.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the like-for-like growth is affected by renovated assets?
qa_highlights.answer: Slide 9 excludes Taj Palace, Fort Aguada, Blue Diamond and Calicut, which were under renovation last year, to give an apples-to-apples comparison.

risks_watch: Air catering margin pressure as Air India and IndiGo capacity cuts persist; management does not expect a quick rebound in Q2.
Dubai and Maldives/Sri Lanka exposure, with Palm leisure and Emirates connectivity still impaired.
Muted Q3-Q4 foreign arrivals and wedding and MICE recovery dependent on government events.
Frankfurt ramp-up in July-August, and New York rooms returning in 2-3 months.
Ginger conversion pace (15 in Q1, targets of 40 in Q4) and quality of rebranding.
500850|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on domestic demand and the Q2 outlook, while candid about international and air catering headwinds. Management was somewhat evasive on M&A scale and quantified little on margin guidance.
key_quotes: And definitely, the way Q2 has started, it makes us optimistic about doing similar or even better performance on the top line in this quarter.
We are at a 645 figure and we remain confident of crossing this milestone during the current month itself.
Our continuous focus on operating efficiencies enabled us to sustain hotel segment margins at 32.6%.
guidance_outlook: Management reiterated double-digit revenue growth for FY27 and said it expects to sustain margins, strong cash generation and improved quality of earnings.
Q2 expected to deliver similar or better top-line performance than Q1 (Q1 consolidated revenue growth 15%); July pacing ahead of Q1 per CFO, with Q1 momentum expected to spill into Q2.
Management fee income expected to sustain high-teens CAGR, supported by hotel openings pipeline.

Air catering: Q2 expected to be similar or somewhat similar in margin pressure; no quick rebound expected; full-year view to be updated around September-October once Air India and IndiGo capacity returns.
Q3-Q4 foreign arrivals still needed; management said it would know more around September-October; Frankfurt impact turns positive from September.

Ginger conversions targeted at 15 in Q1, 20 in Q2, 25 in Q3 and 40 in Q4; management does not give specific margin guidance and said margins are directionally upward if top-line follows Q1 trajectory.

rows.when: Q3-Q4 FY27, to be clearer around September-October
rows.why: Dubai is at about 80% of prior revenue and Taj Exotica Palm is below 50%, and management says Q3-Q4 foreign arrivals are still needed with more clarity in September-October.

tone.note: Management was confident on domestic leisure demand, Q2 tracking ahead and double-digit FY27 growth, but cautious on international (Dubai, Palm), air catering margins and Q3-Q4 foreign arrivals; analysts pressed on upper-end guidance and the margin outlook.

500850|2026-09.headline: IHCL raised FY27 consolidated revenue growth guidance to 15%-17% after Q2 revenue rose 22% to INR2,484 crores and standalone EBITDA margin hit 38.9%.
500850|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 was strong: consolidated operating revenue grew 22% YoY to INR2,484 crores, operating EBITDA grew 24% to INR706 crores (28.4% margin, up 50 bps), and PAT rose 23% to INR349 crores. Standalone operating revenue grew 26% to INR1,336 crores and standalone EBITDA grew 40% to INR520 crores, with margin up 400 bps to 38.9%. Management raised FY27 consolidated revenue growth guidance to 15%-17% from 12%-14%, with Hotel segment growth of 17%-19%. Occupancy rose to 82% from 75%, and TajSATS remained a drag on margins.

financial_highlights.value: Revenue and EBITDA growth of 25% and 30%

segments.name: Hotels (consolidated)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 25% and EBITDA up 30% YoY; domestic hotel RevPAR up 25% and standalone RevPAR up 28%, with double-digit RevPAR growth across all brands.

segments.name: Management fees
segments.commentary: Income up 25% to INR156 crores, driven by 25% growth in managed room inventory, higher RevPAR, technical fees and new brand fees from branded residences and villas; management targets high-teens fee CAGR.

segments.name: Select service (Ginger, Qmin, Ama, Tree of Life)
segments.commentary: Ginger revenue INR193 crores (+25%) at 40% EBITDA margin; Ginger reached 100 operational hotels and targets 150 by March 31, 2027. Qmin has over 130 outlets, Ama over 400 villas and bungalows, Tree of Life over 50 resorts.

segments.name: TajSATS (air catering)
segments.commentary: EBITDA declined sequentially in Q2 due to airline schedule curtailments after West Asia fuel-price pressure; non-aviation institutional catering partly offset the decline. Management expects improvement in H2.

segments.name: International subsidiaries
segments.commentary: St. James' Court margins fell 360 bps YoY in H1 FY27 due to delayed renovation works and cost pressure; management expects London recovery with double-digit growth in October. Pierre (New York) is EBITDA-positive but not at target margins.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth raised to 15%-17% (from 12%-14%), i.e. 300 bps above prior guidance; Hotel segment revenue growth 17%-19%.
Implied H2 growth is well above the 14% midpoint arithmetic, per CFO, as TajSATS is a drag and H2 is seasonally strong; the guidance excludes OHL.
Plan to open 50 hotels in FY27; 30 expected in H2 (possibly 32-34). Standalone hotel count was 392 operational as of Oct 27, 2026, with 4 more openings in October.

Management to publish a revised portfolio target (700-hotel Accelerate 2030 target expected to be crossed early) by mid-November 2026; separate management-fee guidance expected by end of next quarter.
OHL merger: 25 IHCL shares for every 117 OHL shares; appointed date April 1, 2027; expected to add 6%-7% to standalone operating revenue in FY28, not in FY27 guidance.
Management expects more than INR1,000 crores of management fee income in roughly two years and about 5,000 keys opened per year.
capex_capacity: Portfolio at 670 hotels with over 69,000 keys (operational or under development) at end-H1 FY27; 47 hotels signed and 20 opened in H1 FY27.
Pipeline of over 34,800 keys, 94% capital-light (81% management contracts, 13% leases).
H1 FY27 capex is 20%-30% above the annual average of the preceding 7-8 years, per management.

Asset upgrades at Taj Palace New Delhi, President Mumbai, Taj West End Bengaluru, Taj Fort Aguada and Taj Lake Palace; Taj Palace New Delhi room revenue up 132% YoY and crossed INR100 crores monthly revenue in September.
Expected upcoming Frankfurt ramp-up after start-up challenges; London and San Francisco expected to improve in Q3.
demand_pricing: Occupancy rose to 82% from 75% in Q2 last year; standalone and domestic consolidated occupancy each up roughly 6%-7%, so growth was balanced between occupancy and ARR.
Demand supported by MICE events (BRICS Summit, Bloomberg event, fintech event); management said Q2 ex-BRICS would still have been a comfortable double-digit RevPAR number.
Wedding nights next year are expected at about 95 versus 60-65 normally, a tailwind for social MICE.
Domestic demand is the main pillar; foreign tourist arrivals have a 3.9% 10-year CAGR, and management sees upside if this reaches 5%-6%. Room nights were flat YoY in Q2 per management.

Tier 2/3 supply: management says demand growth of 15%-20% in these markets is largely met by unorganised players, and that the 12% capacity CAGR headline should be viewed with caution given project delays.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the H2 guidance implied by the revised numbers, and is occupancy at 82% sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth will be mostly rate-led plus new hotels and international recovery (London, Pierre, San Francisco, Frankfurt), with occupancy gains also in the mix; H2 guidance is conservative given the 30-34 hotel openings.

qa_highlights.question: Why did TajSATS EBITDA fall sequentially?
qa_highlights.answer: Airline schedule curtailments after West Asia fuel-price pressure, mainly from June; Q2 had the full impact. Non-flight catering grew, but at lower margin. FY27 is a consolidation year.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 14% implied H2 growth conservative and what are the uplift drivers?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said H2 growth would have to be higher than the 14% arithmetic to hit guidance, given TajSATS drag, a high Q4 base and seasonally strong MICE and weddings.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 25% growth in Q2 driven by renovation base effects?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said renovations are routine for iconic assets; H1 capex is 20%-30% above normal and the growth reflects structural demand shifts, not only a low base.

qa_highlights.question: Why keep international assets, given lower margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited strategic value of the global Taj brand; international consolidated margin of about 35% is stated as industry-leading, with London profitable and Pierre EBITDA-positive but not at 20%-25% margins.

qa_highlights.question: What can standalone RevPAR be without BRICS, and how sustainable is the 400 bps margin expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: No one-offs in Q2; margin gain from operating leverage, MICE, and management fee mix (booked standalone). Management did not give specific margin guidance but expects a positive margin trend despite new payroll and regulatory costs.

risks_watch: West Asia geopolitics: higher fuel prices and airline capacity cuts hit TajSATS and international travel; Dubai and Ras Al Khaimah fees affected.
TajSATS margin recovery in H2 depends on airline schedules and West Asia developments.
International subsidiaries: St. James' Court margin decline (360 bps in H1); London renovation and property-tax effects; Pierre profitability target still unresolved.
Depreciation up about 20% YoY on consolidated basis (34% on the non-standalone line) from acquisitions and new assets; watch for margin dilution.
Pending OHL merger (close expected before April 1, 2027) and revised portfolio and management-fee guidance due mid-November 2026 and end of next quarter.
Chennai and Kolkata lag other metros on FTA-dependent demand; management expects recovery in next one or two quarters.
500850|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, guidance and pipeline, with frank acknowledgement of TajSATS, international margins and West Asia headwinds. Management was somewhat defensive on the international portfolio and evasive on the exact H2 growth math and the Q2 ex-event RevPAR figure.
key_quotes: Accordingly, we are revising our full year growth guidance upwards to 15% to 17%.
So international is what makes Taj the world's strongest hotel brand.
I would say, optimistic on TajSATS going back to where it was and actually even improving upon it in the second half.
I think we are getting very close to finding a more sustainable solution, but this is not the one which will do 20% 25% EBITDA margin.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Standalone EBITDA margin rose 400 bps to 38.9% on operating leverage and fee mix, but TajSATS is a drag, international margins fell 360 bps in H1 and depreciation is up about 20%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: H2 FY27 (30 openings expected), FY27 total 50
rows.why: 20 hotels opened in H1 FY27 and 4 more in October; 30 more planned in H2 against a 670-hotel portfolio with over 69,000 keys and a 34,800-key pipeline, 94% capital-light.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Occupancy rose to 82% from 75% (about 6-7 points in standalone and domestic) and 30 hotels are due to open in H2; however, room nights were flat YoY in Q2.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: H1 FY27 capex is 20%-30% above the 7-8 year annual average and a revised portfolio target is due mid-November 2026, but no new capex programme or figure was announced.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management said H2 needs growth above the 14% arithmetic midpoint and calls the guidance conservative given 30-34 H2 openings, but it has only just raised guidance.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: FY27 consolidated revenue growth was raised to 15%-17% from 12%-14%, and Q2 revenue grew 22% to INR2,484 crores; the main risks are TajSATS and West Asia fuel and airline pressure.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Ginger has 100 operational hotels with a target of 150 by March 31, 2027, and new brand fees from branded residences and villas are already flowing into management fees.

rows.label: Management fee income growth to high-teens CAGR; over INR1,000 crores in about t
rows.why: Fee income rose 25% to INR156 crores (from INR125 crores) on 25% managed-room growth, and management reaffirmed a high-teens CAGR.

rows.label: OHL merger (25 IHCL shares per 117 OHL shares), appointed date April 1, 2027
rows.when: close before April 1, 2027; contributes in FY28
rows.why: Expected to add 6%-7% to standalone operating revenue in FY28, excluded from FY27 guidance.
