502090|2026-03.headline: Sagar Cements guides FY27 volumes to about 7 million tonnes (FY26: 6.1 Mt) and Q4 EBITDA/tonne rose to ₹445 from ₹218.
502090|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 volumes grew 8% YoY and full-year volumes grew 11% to 6.1 million tonnes, with revenue up 20% in the quarter helped by non-trade pricing. Q4 EBITDA per tonne was ₹445 against ₹218 a year earlier, and quarterly PAT was ₹100 crore. Management flagged a fuel cost shock from the West Asia conflict (pet coke at $136-140 CIF versus about $120 earlier), with impact expected from mid-Q2 if prices do not ease. Management also announced a Superfine Building Materials division and in-principle approval for merging Andhra Cements into the parent.

segments.name: Plants (Q4 utilisation)
segments.commentary: Mattampally 59%, Gudipadu 84%, Bayyavaram 69%, Jeerabad 95%, Jajpur 44%, Dachepalli 38%. Jeerabad is cited as consistently running around 90%.

segments.name: Superfine Building Materials (new division)
segments.commentary: Approved by the board on 13 May 2026. It will use GGBS and fly ash to make superfine products (Blaine target 10,000-20,000) for UHPC, repairs and cladding. Management guides a minimum 30% margin; revenue and EBITDA numbers are deferred to next quarter.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume target of about 7 million tonnes, relying on about 0.5 Mt from Jeerabad upgrade (expected by end-Q1), about 0.9 Mt from Andhra ramp-up and the balance from market growth of 12-15%.
FY27 EBITDA per tonne expected to be close to ₹600 if prices stay flat, with about ₹150/tonne from internal cost savings (WHRS, Andhra preheater, grinding units).

Pet coke and coal cost pressure: about ₹200/tonne at clinker and ₹100-150/tonne at cement on current blend, with impact from mid-Q2 if prices stay high. Management also pencilled in about ₹225-250/tonne in total fuel and miscellaneous cost increases, assumed to be passed through.
FY27 budget: ₹580 crore cost, about ₹100 crore lower than the prior year's cost base according to management's comments.

Capex: ₹190 crore pending on three ongoing projects (Andhra ₹140 crore, Gudipadu ₹17 crore, Jeerabad ₹33 crore). Maintenance capex about ₹50 crore per year. Some projects to be funded through lease or equipment finance.
Vizag land monetisation (about 100 acres, net about ₹3.5 crore per acre): ₹350 crore pencilled over 18-24 months, with ₹150 crore in year 1 after the government GO, and ₹150 crore assumed in FY27.
Net debt guidance for FY27 is to pay debt down from operating cash flow; year-end net debt was about ₹1,550 crore versus the earlier guidance of about ₹1,300 crore.
capex_capacity: WHRS: 2.8 MW of 4.35 MW (AQC boiler) commissioned on 12 May 2026; remaining 1.55 MW (preheater boiler) due by end-June 2026.
Jeerabad grinding expansion and Dachepalli expansion in progress; Jeerabad due before end of Q1 FY27.
Andhra Cements grinding expansion due by September 2026; new VRM for cement grinding due by September 2026.
Andhra clinker kcal consumption about 700 kcal/tonne of clinker versus about 775-780 earlier.
Madhya Pradesh incentives of about ₹171 crore over seven years; about ₹65 crore received so far, about ₹110 crore remaining over four years.
demand_pricing: Industry demand held up in the first two months of Q4 but slowed in late Q4 due to labour shortages, the festive season and unseasonal rains. Q4 volume growth was 8%, and Q1 FY27 to date is up about 7% YoY.
Price hike of about ₹25-30 per bag in second week of April (non-trade led) across regions; Hyderabad retail about ₹295 and wholesale about ₹268 after the hike.
Prices have been flat since mid-April, with some pressure in central and eastern markets (₹5 hike in Indore not sustained) and a slight negative bias there; south has held the April hike.
Demand outlook: AP and Telangana strong; Tamil Nadu 5-10%, Karnataka 5%, Odisha 5%, Madhya Pradesh 5-7.5%.
Management said bags cost fell about ₹2/bag, but the war impact on explosives and diesel (₹23.75/litre hike in commercial diesel) is expected to add about ₹100/tonne.
Superfine products priced around ₹30,000/tonne versus ₹2,500-3,000/tonne for low-Blaine GGBS, with low volumes expected initially.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected cost impact from the West Asia crisis?
qa_highlights.answer: Pet coke has risen from around $120 to $136-140 CIF, adding about ₹200/tonne at clinker and ₹100-150/tonne at cement. Inventory cover runs to mid-Q2, and imported coal is being partly switched to domestic coal, with the outcome known by end-Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise 28% QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Around ₹11.5 crore was one-offs: about ₹7.5 crore mine bearing land (MBL) cess and about ₹3.24 crore DMF expense at a subsidiary, covering roughly 3-3.5 years of accrual. Promotional spend also rose. Excluding one-offs, growth is about 26%.

qa_highlights.question: Can FY27 volume of 7 Mt be achieved given past misses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the target relies on Jeerabad (+0.5 Mt), Andhra ramp-up (+0.9 Mt) and market growth; it chooses not to chase share at the expense of cash.

qa_highlights.question: Will Jeerabad clinker sales continue in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Some clinker sales are expected during the phased ramp-up, subject to clinker prices, with margin held at that location's level.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any cost reduction left after Andhra stabilised?
qa_highlights.answer: Andhra clinker cost is now in line; the new VRM (by September) should deliver the planned savings. Margins are expected to be better in FY27 than FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Why did net debt rise above guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Promoter unsecured debt for the Andhra project was drawn after the planned rights issue became an OFS, and solar capex was accelerated for short payback. Debt is expected to fall from operating cash flow.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital days rose sharply: why?
qa_highlights.answer: Credit days were extended in a difficult market, fuel prices were higher, and volumes grew. About ₹80 crore of US coal was bought in March on 180-day LC credit. Moderation is expected.

qa_highlights.question: Vizag land GO status and sale timing?
qa_highlights.answer: GVMC and UDA approvals are in place; the state GO is awaited, expected within six months. Management is assuming ₹350 crore over 18-24 months at the old reckoner rate of ₹4 crore per acre.

qa_highlights.question: Operating cost gap between standalone and Andhra?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the gap is mainly logistics and market spread, with the Andhra cost gap closing after investments; detail to be discussed offline.

risks_watch: Fuel cost inflation: pet coke and coal may add ₹100-150/tonne at cement from mid-Q2 if prices do not ease; a ₹225-250/tonne total cost pass-through is assumed.
Pricing: the April hike is holding in the south, but central and eastern prices are flat to slightly negative.
Execution: Jeerabad upgrade (0.5 Mt), Andhra ramp-up (0.9 Mt), WHRS completion by end-June and VRM by September; past volume guidance has been missed.
Debt and working capital: year-end net debt about ₹1,550 crore, above prior guidance; working capital elevated; funding of ₹190 crore capex needs lease finance.
Vizag land monetisation depends on the state GO, which is still awaited; ₹150 crore is pencilled into FY27.
Incentive receipts: about ₹23 crore outstanding at March 2026, expected mid-July 2026.

I think in the current year itself, we should be very close to ₹600 because the significant improvement for us has come from the cost itself

rows.why: Superfine Building Materials division approved by the board on 13 May 2026 with a minimum 30% EBITDA margin, priced ~₹30,000/tonne versus ₹2,500-3,000/tonne for low-Blaine GGBS, though revenue and EBITDA numbers are deferred and volumes are expected to be low initially.

502090|2026-06.headline: Sagar Cements Q1 FY27: volumes up ~13% YoY but loss after tax of ₹28 crore and EBITDA of ₹451/tonne on West Asia-driven cost inflation.
502090|2026-06.overview: Volumes grew about 13% YoY and revenue rose 5% YoY, with realisations broadly stable. Profitability moderated as energy, fuel and packaging costs rose amid West Asia tensions, leaving EBITDA at ₹451 per tonne and a loss after tax of ₹28 crore. Management maintained a 7 million tonne volume target for FY27 (excluding clinker) and reiterated FY27 EBITDA guidance of ₹500–550 per tonne, down from the earlier ~₹600 reference raised by an analyst. Capex completed in the quarter includes Jeerabad 0.5 million tonne expansion and the remaining 1.55 MW of Gudipadu waste heat recovery; the 0.75 million tonne Andhra Cements expansion is expected by quarter-end.

Madhya Pradesh demand grew ~9–10%; Maharashtra and Odisha described as healthy.
July demand expected to track Q1 trend, with labour availability back.

Tamil Nadu ban on transport of rough stones and aggregates to other states: management sees no impact.
Heat waves and election-related labour shortages in Eastern and Southern India disrupted Q1 execution.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 7 million tonne FY27 volume target ex-clinker, and how much clinker will be sold in Q2 and beyond?
qa_highlights.answer: The 7 mt target excludes clinker. Clinker is still sold to Andhra Cements' sister unit Bayyavaram and some outside, and some at Jeerabad until ramp-up; management would not quantify volumes.

qa_highlights.question: Is double-digit volume growth possible in FY28, and what is the Q2 cost inflation and is the ~₹600/t EBITDA guidance intact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says FY27 and FY28 both see double-digit volume growth. Full-year cost pressure is about ₹100/t across fuel, raw material and miscellaneous, offset by savings; Q2 gets extra inventory and maintenance cost at three plants. Guidance is ₹500–550/t, assuming flat prices, not ~₹600.

qa_highlights.question: Are prices stable versus Q1 averages?
qa_highlights.answer: Prices have been flat from March exit to July and June to July; realisation was up about ₹50–60/t, with the cause unclear (mix or price hikes).

qa_highlights.question: Status of Vizag land sale and FY27 realisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Awaiting a generic Government GO after the government signalled it would replace a case-specific order; the ₹150 crore for FY27 is still seen as doable. Management said buyer engagement exists but timelines were the issue.

qa_highlights.question: Which regions drive incremental H2 FY27 demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Almost all incremental volume comes from the South (~80% of footprint). Madpradesh is also expected to rise after the 0.5 mt Jeerabad expansion, supporting the ~15% growth projected for the year.

qa_highlights.question: How does Andhra Cements' cost structure compare with Mattampally, and how should the three units be modelled?
qa_highlights.answer: Variable cost at Andhra is ₹100–125/t higher than Mattampally because it buys grid power without waste heat recovery; management says the kcal and unit metrics are at par. Andhra carries most of the debt, and management offered to share modelling details offline.

qa_highlights.question: Can Q1 EBITDA of ~₹425/t reach ₹600/t for full year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ₹550/t is 'definitely doable', citing Gudipadu WHR savings, Jeerabad expansion and the Andhra cement mill due end-September, assuming stable prices.

qa_highlights.question: Is capex going to rise, and what is the debt reduction path?
qa_highlights.answer: No new capex beyond ₹30–40 crore annual maintenance through 2028. About ₹240 crore of ongoing capex spreads over FY27 and FY28; operating cash flow is not yet reflected in the gross debt path.

qa_highlights.question: What are the levers to manage power and fuel costs if the West Asia crisis escalates?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has no control over prices and can only manage consumption, which it says is efficient. Inventory covers operations to mid-October; ₹100/t inflation is pencilled in (₹50 fuel, ₹50 other), and clinker is at its peak.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the Tamil Nadu ban on rough stone and aggregate transport, and what limestone auction premiums are seen?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees no impact. Recent Telangana limestone auctions, about a year or 18 months old, went at 50–75% premiums; other auctions are pending in TN, AP and Telangana.

qa_highlights.question: Will the land sale and volume ramp support the net debt projection?
qa_highlights.answer: Parth Bhavsar asked about net debt trajectory. Management said the ₹150 crore land sale is in FY27 and about ₹200 crore in FY28.

502090|2026-09.headline: Sagar Cements Q2 FY27 volumes rose 26% YoY, but loss after tax of ₹52 crore; management guides FY27 EBITDA of ₹350-375 crore.

Management said the company has hit its margin bottom and expects H2 recovery driven by South price hikes of about ₹25 per bag on average (roughly ₹500 per ton realisation uplift). FY27 EBITDA guidance was revised to ₹350-375 crore (about ₹525 per ton) from the earlier ~₹410 crore projection. Net debt has peaked with CapEx largely complete and is expected to decline from Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: When will Andhra break even?

qa_highlights.question: What is the revised full-year EBITDA?

qa_highlights.question: What fuel cost increase is assumed, and what if the company moves to spot prices?

qa_highlights.question: Is the net debt going to fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt is expected to stay flat in Q3 FY27 and decline sharply from Q4, with around ₹250 crore reduction from FY28 plus Vizag land proceeds.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY28 EBITDA per ton and volume outlook?

502219|2026-03.headline: Borosil Renewables FY26 standalone sales rose 38% to INR1,534.83 crore and EBITDA margin hit 32% on higher solar glass realisations.
502219|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 standalone sales were INR437.62 crore (up ~34% YoY, a record quarter) with EBITDA of INR144.61 crore at 33% of sales, helped by average ex-factory realisation of INR150.2/mm and about 15% higher volumes. Management attributed roughly half the quarterly sales jump to Ind AS revenue recognition timing (about 6% of Q4 sales), and said the run-rate is nearer INR400-410 crore a quarter. Fuel surcharges passed to customers during the West Asia-driven gas price spike had negligible net impact on realisation (under INR1/mm). The company wrote off its German exposure (Geosphere and GMB) with no additional P&L loss, as a provision was already made in Q1 FY26. Management also announced a rooftop solar branded-products venture, a 600 TPD furnace expansion targeted for Q4 FY27, and an enabling resolution to raise up to INR750 crore in equity.

segments.commentary: FY26 sales INR1,534.83 crore with EBITDA margin 32%; Q4 volumes up 15% YoY and 14% QoQ, with production run at full capacity and no curtailment during the West Asia disruption.

segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 overseas net revenue INR2.3 crore and EBITDA INR0.82 crore, versus INR3.96 crore and INR1.90 crore in the prior quarter; German production shut from July 2025 and exposure to Geosphere and GMB written off.

Management cited INR950 crore of capitalisation planned in the current financial year.

Domestic solar glass capacity is about 2,600 TPD (about 18 GW); about 33 GW of further capacity is expected by March 2027, mostly captive, taking the domestic total to about 51 GW against demand of about 65 GW.
Rooftop business: no capex for 1-1.5 years; the company may consider inverter assembly after 6-8 months to a year, but not module manufacturing.
Board approved an enabling resolution to raise equity up to INR750 crore, subject to shareholder approval; management said there are no current plans to raise capital.
demand_pricing: Realisation held near INR150/mm; management said pass-through of gas and fuel cost added less than INR1/mm, and that the price is tied to the landed cost of Chinese imports and near peak levels, with rupee depreciation providing only limited headroom.
Domestic solar installations were 44.6 GW in FY26 versus 23.8 GW in FY25, implying about 60-62 GW of glass consumption; imports still supply about 70% of demand.
ALMM-II (domestic solar cells) effective June 2026; solar cell capacity at 30 GW, expected to reach 75 GW by FY-end; ALMM-III for ingots and wafers from June 2028.

Indonesian Chinese-owned plant (about 1,500 TPD) has entered the market but has made limited impact so far; the Turkish producer's exports face high freight costs; the UAE plant is blocked by Strait of Hormuz conditions.
Export demand is low in major markets; the US may grow as customers seek non-Chinese origin glass, and Europe has niche demand for greenhouses and flat-plate collectors.

Cost pressure from oil-linked inputs is so far modest; vendors are seeking pass-through and the company is negotiating; gas quantities are secured under medium- and short-term contracts, but spot prices are high.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the INR150/mm realisation comes from fuel pass-through, and what would it be without it?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashok Jain said the pass-through contributed less than INR1/mm, about INR0.70-0.75, and a similar increase is visible in net realisation between Q3 and Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Will realisation or margins come under pressure as new domestic capacity arrives?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees no pressure for domestic producers; most upcoming capacity is captive, demand exceeds the 51 GW expected capacity, and Indonesian imports are not yet a price threat.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 13-15% sequential sales growth with flat realisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Roughly half was production gain (about 7%) and half was Ind AS timing: in-transit sales were lower at the end of Q3 and so were recognised in Q4, with the sales base reset to about INR400-410 crore a quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is gas supply secure given the West Asia crisis?
qa_highlights.answer: Quantities are broadly secured under medium- and short-term contracts; the government gas cut is based on the past six-month average, and the rest is bought at market-related prices, so price rather than volume is the constraint.

qa_highlights.question: What is the rooftop solar roadmap, capex and margin profile?
qa_highlights.answer: No capex for 1-1.5 years; modules, inverters and batteries will be outsourced; first-year target is about INR75 crore, with margins expected below 10% initially and little or no profit in year one; working capital is kept low by negotiating terms.

qa_highlights.question: Will the furnace expansion commissioning timeline hold, and what does it do to margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said timing is as currently planned (first furnace around January 2027), with sales from Q1 FY28; operating leverage and higher yield are expected, but management did not commit to a specific margin uplift.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for depreciation and tax?
qa_highlights.answer: Depreciation has fallen because older SG1 and SG2 assets are fully depreciated; current charge mainly reflects the 2023 expansion. Tax is around 21% of PBT, with deferred tax at a similar rate.

Fuel surcharge and gas price volatility from the West Asia conflict; management said the Q1 FY27 reset depends on the 30 June stock-take.

Indonesian Chinese-owned capacity could pressure prices; management suggested BIS and quality-control measures as a mitigant.
Rooftop business faces competition from Tata Power, Havells and Luminous, and early margins are guided below 10%.
Furnace commissioning slippage (first furnace January 2027 target) and the planned INR100 crore SG1/SG2 rebuild capex.
Export demand remains weak in Europe; freight costs are high because of Red Sea and Hormuz disruptions.

rows.why: Rooftop solar branded products launched with first sales in March 2026 and a first-year target of ~INR75 crore, sourcing modules, inverters and batteries externally; inverter assembly may follow in 6-8 months to a year.

rows.label: Realisation held near INR150/mm with demand above domestic capacity
rows.why: Average ex-factory realisation was INR150.2/mm in Q4 FY26 versus INR127.6 in Q4 FY25, and management sees ~60-62 GW glass demand against 51 GW domestic capacity by March 2027, but imports still supply ~70% of demand and Indonesian capacity has entered.

rows.label: Customs continuation of CVD on Malaysian solar glass
rows.why: Management expects the notification before the current duty expires on 6-8 June 2026, and a delayed or diluted notification would weigh on pricing against imports that make up ~70% of demand.

rows.label: Enabling resolution to raise up to INR750 crore equity
rows.why: Board approved an enabling resolution subject to shareholder approval, but management said there are no current plans to raise capital, so dilution is not expected in the window.

tone.note: Management was confident on domestic demand-supply gap and pricing and the 600 TPD build, but cautious on Q4 sequential sustainability (Ind AS timing) and evasive on expansion beyond 600 TPD; analysts pushed on realisation durability, fuel pass-through and the Q4 sales base.

502219|2026-06.headline: Borosil Renewables Q1 FY27 standalone sales rose 53% YoY to INR405.69 crore and EBITDA to INR142 crore (35% margin), helped by a fuel surcharge.
502219|2026-06.overview: Standalone sales were INR405.69 crore, up 53% YoY from INR332.26 crore, while EBITDA rose to INR142 crore at 35% of sales versus 27.9% a year ago. Average ex-factory realisation rose to INR160.30 per sq m from INR150.20 in Q4 FY26, including a INR9.50 fuel surcharge introduced from 10 March 2026 after the West Asia war raised fuel costs. Management said the surcharge is now being cut as fuel prices ease, and that the 600 TPD furnace expansion is on track for commissioning in Q1 FY27-end (January to March 2027). Reported PAT of about INR169 crore in Q4 FY26 was inflated by a INR75 crore tax write-back, so the sequential PAT comparison is not like-for-like.

segments.name: Solar glass (core, standalone)
segments.commentary: Plants run at full capacity of 1,000 TPD; realisation INR160.30 per sq m, with EBITDA margin above 33% for the fourth straight quarter. Top 10 customers are about 65-68% of volume.

segments.name: Overseas subsidiaries (German step-downs)
segments.commentary: No revenue in Q1 FY27 and an EBITDA loss of INR0.84 crore, against INR14.32 crore revenue and INR23.24 crore loss a year earlier. Investment written off in the books after the court administrator indicated no recovery.

segments.name: Rooftop solar (new)
segments.commentary: Early-stage on-grid residential kit (module, inverter, battery) sold as a system. Q1 revenue about INR1.3 crore against an internal FY27 target of about INR36 crore; EBITDA margin expected in single digits, versus 30-35% for glass.

guidance_outlook: 600 TPD expansion at the existing site: construction targeted by December 2026, commissioning January to March 2027 (SG4 and SG5, about one month apart). Management says revenue should be modelled from 1 April 2027, though the internal target is 1 March.
Once the 600 TPD is commissioned, sales are expected to rise about 60%, adding about INR80-85 crore of quarterly EBITDA at current run-rate and prices.
Realisation to fall as the INR9.50 fuel surcharge is passed back to customers; management says cost declines should offset this, so profit is not expected to be affected.

Management declined to give a formal guidance but said it expects to continue at similar revenue and EBITDA levels if conditions hold; expects extra profitability this year because prices were at full levels all year.
Ambition to grow from about INR2,500 crore to at least INR4,000 crore revenue in 3-4 years after March 2027; next expansion decision expected within about 6 months.
capex_capacity: Current capacity 1,000 TPD; expansion of 600 TPD at existing location takes it to 1,600 TPD, with the expansion fully funded per management.

Furnace SG1 and SG2 refurbishment: timing not fixed, possibly Q4 FY27 to Q2 FY28, likely after SG4/SG5 are commissioned. A rebuild needs about 75 days of shutdown plus 15 days to restart, so about 90 days with no output from the furnace being rebuilt.
Any further capacity beyond the 600 TPD expansion would be a new building and facility, sized at 600 or 1,200 TPD, and not an add-on to the current layout.
Domestic solar glass capacity expected to reach 7,700 TPD by March 2027 (about 51 GW), against about 2,600 TPD (18 GW) today and about 11,000 TPD demand for 62 GW of module requirement.

Module capacity in India is 203 GW; solar cell capacity is 30 GW, expected to rise to 75 GW by 2027 under ALMM-2 (effective 1 June 2026). ALMM-3 for ingot and wafer starts 28 June, with about 50 GW expected by 2029.
demand_pricing: Management says domestic industry supplies only about 25% of demand; even at 7,700 TPD, supply would cover only 75%, so pricing is expected to hold, with import-parity pricing as the reference.
Exports to the US are very small and in niche applications; the company is focused on the domestic market.
A significant portion of new domestic capacity is captive, so the open-market supply gain is limited, according to management.
Management expects module makers to consolidate over the next 1-1.5 years because module capacity far exceeds requirement; Mono PERC players and those without cell supply may drop volumes.
CVD of 9.71% on solar glass imports from Malaysia extended for five more years from 2 June 2026, on top of anti-dumping duties on China and Vietnam since December 2024.

qa_highlights.question: Why did PAT fall from INR169 crore in Q4 to INR87 crore in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 FY26 PAT included a INR75 crore tax write-back tied to the write-off of the German subsidiary investment (INR325 crore provision). Excluding it, performance was not inferior.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital days rose from 34 to 152; is that right?
qa_highlights.answer: Management disputed the 152-day figure, saying working capital is about 60 days, with a slight rise from stores inventory.

qa_highlights.question: Will domestic prices fall as capacity grows to 7,700 TPD?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said demand is robust, with domestic supply covering only about 25% now, and that pricing is anchored to import parity, so no pricing challenge is foreseen.

qa_highlights.question: What is the rooftop solar business worth?
qa_highlights.answer: Internal FY27 revenue target is about INR36 crore, Q1 revenue about INR1.3 crore, with single-digit EBITDA margins because it is a trading-style solution business.

qa_highlights.question: Any equity raise or debt plan?
qa_highlights.answer: The current expansion is fully funded. Future projects will be funded from internal cash, with some debt if the project is large. No near-term equity raise is planned.

qa_highlights.question: How is the gross margin around 80% calculated?
qa_highlights.answer: Management put gross margin at about 78% on a manufacturing-cost basis, with raw material at about 23-24% of sales, and said margin volatility is not expected.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost of the SG1 patch repair and the volume effect of furnace rebuilds?
qa_highlights.answer: A four-day patch on one furnace cost about INR3 crore in lost output. A full rebuild would shut the furnace for about 90 days, causing a volume loss in the year it happens.

qa_highlights.question: What is the tax rate for the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 25.2% should be assumed for the full year.

risks_watch: Fuel-surcharge unwind: the INR9.50 per sq m surcharge is being reduced as fuel prices ease, so realisation could fall from INR160.30 even with stable costs. Management says the cost decline offsets it.
Commissioning risk: the 600 TPD expansion (SG4, SG5) must be commissioned by March 2027, with revenue only from April 2027. Any delay pushes the 60% volume uplift later.
Furnace SG1/SG2 rebuild: about 90 days of lost output per furnace, timing not fixed (Q4 FY27 to Q2 FY28); this could reduce FY28 volumes against the 1,600 TPD capacity.
Customer concentration: top 10 customers are about 65-68% of volume, and module consolidation could affect volumes.
Capacity additions in domestic glass (to 7,700 TPD by March 2027) could pressure prices, though management expects supply to stay short.
Rooftop solar and the overseas subsidiaries are small and early, with unclear profitability; the call gave no segment-level data.
Management declined to comment on press reports of a strategic investment. Next-phase project choice (glass furnace or adjacent business) is due in about 5-6 months.
502219|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on operations and demand, with management stressing full plant utilisation and a robust domestic market. It was evasive on guidance, declining to give formal numbers, and on the strategic investment press reports. Defensive on the PAT comparison, which it attributed to a one-off tax write-back.
key_quotes: I'm happy to inform that we were able to operate the plants at full capacity despite disruption in fuel supplies and the prices led by war in West Asia.
So if you really remove that INR75 crores, the performance is not inferior.
So our expansion is exactly 60% of the current capacity. And we are assuming the prices to remain same way.

502219|2026-09.headline: Borosil Renewables Q2 FY27 solar glass sales were INR382.1 crore with EBITDA margin down to 30.4% on furnace maintenance and a 2.8% price cut, with October output reported higher.
502219|2026-09.overview: Standalone H1 FY27 sales rose 12.8% to INR801.8 crore and EBITDA rose 18.5% to INR258.3 crore, but Q2 alone showed softer numbers. Q2 solar glass sales were flat YoY at INR382.1 crore, with EBITDA of INR116.34 crore at 30.4% margin versus 33% a year earlier, because of furnace maintenance (production down about 4.5-5%) and a reduced fuel surcharge after gas prices eased in July. Management said the fuel surcharge was restored in October as gas prices rebounded, and that October production was strong and above prior levels. The 600 tpd expansion (about 60% capacity addition, project cost raised by INR150 crore to about INR1,100 crore) is on track for commissioning toward end-Q4 FY27, funded internally without extra bank debt.

segments.name: Solar glass (core)
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 sales INR382.1 crore at 30.4% EBITDA margin; volume dip from furnace maintenance and a 2.8% price decline from reduced fuel surcharge. Management expects margins to return to higher levels by end of Q2/Q3.

segments.name: Solar kits (trading)
segments.commentary: Revenue of INR14.1 crore in Q2 FY27 (INR15.4 crore in H1) with negligible EBITDA. Sales are being made in batches, with module and inverter purchases of about INR14 crore shown as purchase stocking credit.

segments.name: Rooftop solar (new)
segments.commentary: Early-stage B2C/C&I rooftop business launched in four states with distributors appointed and some projects executed. Management said margins are low as the business is largely trading, and it is not yet profitable at scale.

segments.name: Overseas subsidiaries
segments.commentary: No net revenue in Q2 FY27 and negative EBITDA of INR0.11 crore, versus INR5.08 crore loss in Q2 FY26.

guidance_outlook: Management expects October output to continue at high levels and to make good the Q2 shortfall within FY27; the production dip was about 4.5-5%, with output now said to be 8-10% above earlier levels (early, not yet sustained).
Management expects EBITDA margins of at least 30% going forward and 31-32% in FY27 and FY28 (based on current parameters), with fuel surcharge restored in October.
600 tpd capacity addition (about 60% increase) is expected to be commissioned toward end-Q4 FY27; furnace 1 and furnace 2 firing planned in February and March 2027.
Furnaces SG1 and SG2 may each need a 75-day rebuild, most likely in H1 FY28; management says no production loss is expected in FY27 and expects the new capacity to offset the outage.

Project cost raised by INR150 crore to about INR1,100 crore, funded internally (INR800 crore internal, INR300 crore debt already sanctioned but not drawn); management says no further dilution foreseen.
Company expects to be net cash positive by end-March 2027; a decision on new growth areas is expected by end of FY27.
Expansion of 60% expected to add 2-3% EBITDA margin via operating leverage from the new facility.
capex_capacity: 600 tpd new capacity at existing site, about 60% increase; total project cost about INR1,100 crore after an INR150 crore revision (about 20% from exchange rate, balance from fuel-cost-saving equipment and power redundancy of about INR25 crore).

Capital work-in-progress rose to INR349 crore at September 2026 from INR107 crore at March 2026; LCs of about INR150 crore plus advances outstanding; building nearly complete and machine deliveries under way.
Installation to start by end of Q3 FY27; furnaces to be fired in February and March 2027.
Existing furnaces run at full capacity; SG1 and SG2 (operating about 7 years) to be rebuilt, 75 days each, likely H1 FY28.
Domestic solar glass supply of about 18 GW versus demand of about 62 GW DC; module capacity 233 GW; cell capacity about 38 GW rising to about 75 GW by 2027.
demand_pricing: Average ex-factory realisation INR155.9 per square metre in Q2 FY27, down from INR160.3 in Q1 FY27; the INR4.4 drop was due to the reduced fuel surcharge. Management expects a return to about INR160 by quarter end.

Fuel surcharge was partly rolled back in July after gas prices eased, then raised again in October as Brent and gas prices rose to about USD115 (versus about USD100 when first passed on and USD75-80 at the rollback).

Soda ash (about 30-32% of raw material cost) price up about 10% from June to September quarter; imported dolomite and limestone costs and China freight rates also rose. Management plans to shift dolomite sourcing from 30-40% domestic toward more domestic supply.
Anti-dumping duty on China and Vietnam in place until December 2029; management sees domestic supply shortfall supporting pricing.
Management says there is no cost-plus or pass-through for raw materials; the fuel surcharge was a one-off force majeure recovery, so productivity gains are needed to offset other cost increases.

qa_highlights.question: What was the revenue and EBITDA loss from the Q2 production disruption?
qa_highlights.answer: Management put the revenue loss at about INR15 crore, with production down about 4.5% due to furnace maintenance; output has since recovered and exceeded earlier levels.

qa_highlights.question: Why did raw material costs rise and can margins return to 30%+?
qa_highlights.answer: Soda ash prices rose about 10%, imported dolomite and freight costs increased, and the fuel surcharge was reduced; management expects margins to recover through restored surcharge, higher volumes, and domestic sourcing savings.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 600 tpd expansion fully funded and what is the debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR800 crore is internal funds (from preferential issues already received) and INR300 crore is previously signed debt not yet drawn; no further dilution is foreseen.

qa_highlights.question: How will SG1 and SG2 rebuilds affect FY28 volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 75-day shutdowns are planned for H1 FY28, expected to be offset by the new line; it also said this is speculative and volume recovery cannot be guaranteed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the rooftop solar strategy and margin profile?
qa_highlights.answer: Rooftop is at an early stage in four states, using the Borosil brand and distributors; management said margins will be low as it is largely trading and that scale is needed before profit improves.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue contribution expected from the new capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects turnover to rise about 60% in line with capacity, with 2-3% EBITDA margin gain from operating leverage.

risks_watch: Gas and crude price volatility (Brent cited at about USD115): fuel surcharge pass-through has lagged cost moves in both directions, and management has not yet restored the Q1 realisation level.
Commissioning and ramp-up of the 600 tpd line by end-Q4 FY27; the INR150 crore cost overrun and the power-redundancy and exchange-rate items.
Demand and sell-through of about 1,600 tpd of new capacity; management did not commit to specific customer contracts beyond discussions.
Planned 75-day rebuilds of SG1 and SG2 in H1 FY28, and management's refusal to guarantee recovery of lost volume.
Soda ash, dolomite and freight cost inflation with no contractual pass-through; progress on domestic sourcing shift to be monitored.
Rooftop and solar kit ventures are low margin and small; the management target for their revenue was not quantified.
Overseas subsidiaries are loss-making, though loss narrowed sharply in Q2 FY27.
502219|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on recovery and demand, with management repeatedly saying October output was strong and the shortfall would be made up. Cautious and evasive on specifics: Chairman called volume make-up "speculative", would not commit to exact margins beyond "at least 30%", and deferred the tax and cash-flow queries to Investor Relations.
key_quotes: Our company is making glass at a higher rate than anywhere else in the world per square meter.
We cannot guarantee that we make up the volume loss.
As a company in corporate philosophy, we do not believe in overstretching ourselves to the point that management suffers.

502355|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 standalone EBITDA was INR663 crore at 22.9% margin on record OHT volumes of 85,820 MT, while management flagged raw material inflation of 7-8% in Q1 FY27.
502355|2026-03.overview: Balkrishna posted its highest-ever quarterly and annual OHT volumes, with Q4 volume up 5% YoY to 85,820 MT and FY26 volume at 317,356 MT. Standalone Q4 revenue rose 2% YoY to INR2,894 crore, but EBITDA margin was hit late in the quarter by geopolitical supply-chain headwinds, and FY26 EBITDA fell 10% YoY to INR2,423 crore. The company has stopped giving volume guidance, is starting its on-highway push (TBR, 2-wheeler, PCR), and has approved an additional INR2,000 crore capex. Management signalled raw material and margin pressure into FY27 with only partial price pass-through so far.

segments.name: Off-highway tyres (OHT)
segments.commentary: Q4 volume of 85,820 MT (+5% YoY) was a record; H2 clearly stronger than H1 with Europe recovering on easing channel inventories and Americas improving. US was just under 10% of FY26 volume, with a target of about 10% in FY27.

segments.name: Carbon black
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue grew marginally; third-party sales were about 9% of the business. Capacity is 265,000 MTPA after the December 2025 line, with the new lines fully utilised; about 30% of output is consumed internally and about 70% sold externally at industry-average margins.

segments.name: On-highway tyres (OHT-on-road)
segments.commentary: Entered truck-bus radial with launches in February 2026 and re-launched 2-wheeler tyres (capacity about 100,000 tyres a month). Phase 1 CV radial capex of INR750 crore added 800 tyres a day of fungible CVR/OHT capacity; PCR launch is targeted by end of calendar 2026 with first-phase capacity of 6,700 tyres a day. Long-term vision is INR5,000 crore revenue by 2030.

guidance_outlook: No volume guidance for FY27 given the geopolitical uncertainty; management expects growth but declined to quantify it.
Raw material prices rose about 4-5% in Q4 FY26 and are expected to rise a further 7-8% in the June 2026 quarter.
Price hikes of 3-5% already taken across geographies, with a further roughly 2% targeted by end of May 2026; more hikes possible.
Freight was about 4.5-5% of revenue in Q4 and is expected to rise marginally absent further disruption.
FY27 total capex guided at INR1,500-1,800 crore; maintenance capex about INR200 crore a year on top of projects.
Management aims to sustain EBITDA margins of 23-25% at company level even as on-highway scales up; 5-year revenue growth vision of about 17% CAGR, with the jump back-ended as capacity comes on line.
EUR/INR realization about INR99 in Q4; FY27 hedge rate expected to be higher than this year, not yet quantified.
Final dividend of INR4 per share recommended, on top of INR12 paid over the previous three quarters.
risks_watch: Raw material inflation of 7-8% in the June 2026 quarter, with only partial pass-through through price hikes; management flagged likely near-term margin pressure in FY27.
Geopolitical supply-chain disruption affecting freight (about 4.5-5% of revenue) and margins.
Execution risk on the on-highway ramp (TBR, PCR, 2-wheeler) with no disclosed revenue targets for FY27 and PCR launch slated for end-2026.
Funding of the INR3,800 crore remaining capex is not finalised; the possible peak debt level was not confirmed (gross debt INR4,049 crore at March 2026).
Realisation of the US reciprocal tariff refund and how much will be passed to distributors.
Balance carbon black capacity (to 360,000 MTPA) and CV Phase 2 are due in Q1 FY27 and during FY27; any slippage would affect the ramp.

key_quotes: So we stopped giving guidance due to the geopolitical scenarios and uncertainties.
At this moment, we may have some price pressures, margin pressures.
This was our highest ever quarter and best number.
We have positioned ourselves as a premium player in that category.

qa_highlights.question: Volume guidance for OHT in FY27 and CV radial sales expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management stopped volume guidance due to geopolitical uncertainty; expects growth but will not quantify. CV radial business has just begun, with the 2030 vision still the target.

qa_highlights.question: Total FY27 capex and the INR2,000 crore additional capex: what it covers and whether it is incremental to the INR6,800 crore plan?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex guided at INR1,500-1,800 crore. The INR2,000 crore covers capacity expansion, infrastructure, AI automation and sustainability, staggered over several years. INR6,800 crore includes about INR3,000 crore already spent; maintenance capex about INR200 crore a year is extra.

qa_highlights.question: Raw material and price pass-through outlook; near-term margin pressure in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Raw material rose about 4-5% in Q4 and may rise 7-8% in June quarter. Price hikes of 3-5% taken with about 2% more by end-May. Management said 'we may have some price pressures, margin pressures' and is evaluating pass-through.

qa_highlights.question: Can company EBITDA margin of 23-25% be sustained with on-highway scale-up?

Standalone EBITDA was INR703 crores at a 20.61% margin, pressured by raw-material costs linked to geopolitical disruption, partly offset by a ~5% price hike. PAT was INR432 crores. The On-Highway business (truck-bus radial and 2-wheeler) went live in Q1 and is being seeded, with a ramp expected from Q2; management declined to disclose its revenue or volume.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a US tariff refund claim in process?

qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR1,500-2,000 crores more will be spent in FY27 on top of INR1,000 crores already spent, and the balance of the INR6,800 crore plan will decline thereafter.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee costs rise 18% YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO-side answer cited a Gujarat minimum-wage increase, staff increments, and hiring for new businesses; management expects this to normalise as new-business turnover builds.

qa_highlights.question: Will OHT margins and FY28 free cash flow improve?

502355|2026-09.headline: BKT signs Pirelli offtake deal to produce 800,000 Pirelli-branded premium car tires per year by 2030 at Bhuj PCR plant, starting CY2027.
502355|2026-09.overview: This was a short business update call on the Pirelli-BKT strategic offtake agreement, held at short notice, with Q2 FY27 performance explicitly off-limits under the silent-period policy. BKT will manufacture Pirelli-branded car tires (17-inch and above) at its newly built Bhuj PCR plant, ramping gradually from CY2027 to 800,000 tires per year by CY2030. A second phase contemplates a 50:50 JV and a dedicated plant for high-value passenger car tires, subject to preset conditions, with management saying the JV work must be announced by 2030. Management said the offtake fits within the existing expansion programme, with no additional capex for the offtake, and pricing is raw material at actuals plus conversion cost.

financial_highlights.change: Ramp from CY2027 start, gradual year-on-year
Roughly 350-355 operating days per year assumed

financial_highlights.metric: Share of Phase 1 capacity for BKT brand
Company blended EBITDA margin cited by analyst
financial_highlights.change: Analyst reference; management declined to comment on Pirelli margin

segments.name: Passenger car tires (PCR) - Pirelli offtake
segments.commentary: Contract manufacturing of Pirelli-branded 17-inch and above car tires at Bhuj, using Pirelli-specific specs; pricing on raw material actuals plus conversion cost, so BKT earns conversion margin. Majority of volume expected for India, with some for Pirelli's global markets.

segments.name: Passenger car tires (PCR) - BKT brand
segments.commentary: Bulk of Phase 1 capacity (about 80% of 6,700 tires/day) stays on BKT brand, addressing the full Indian market from 13-inch upward. BKT is at an early stage of its on-highway journey.

segments.name: Carbon black
segments.commentary: Management said BKT's carbon black business benefits because Pirelli tires made at BKT will use BKT-branded carbon black.

guidance_outlook: Offtake to commence in CY2027, scaling to 800,000 Pirelli-branded tires per year by CY2030.
Offtake investment is part of the existing expansion programme; no additional capex for the offtake, but JV plant would need additional investment.
Pirelli volumes count toward the existing FY30 target of about 20% of revenue from non-OHT (new on-road) categories.
Margin policy unchanged per management: the company's stated policy is to maintain margins despite the 20% non-OHT target.
Vision 2030 reiterated; management said the partnership gives more confidence in achieving it.
JV timing not disclosed; the JV is to be announced by 2030, subject to preset Phase 1 conditions.
capex_capacity: Bhuj PCR plant is newly constructed with equipment management said is nearly identical to Pirelli's own plants; no further capex needed for the offtake per management.
Phase 1 capacity is 6,700 tires per day, with infrastructure that can expand multifold modularly based on demand traction.
Management declined to give a percentage of 2030 capacity that the 800,000 tires would occupy, citing modular expansion.
JV plant: timeline and capex not disclosed; management said it is too early to comment and declined to say whether the JV will be completed by CY29 or CY30.
demand_pricing: Pirelli targets the very high-end Indian car market, which management described as about 10% of the total market; Indian passenger car market growing at 6% to 7% annually.
Pricing is raw material at actuals plus conversion cost on domestic supplies; BKT's earnings are the conversion margin.
Management declined to share Pirelli's market share in India or the minimum offtake volumes, calling them confidential.

Management said there is no royalty payable in the JV; a separate service agreement covers testing and simulation use of Pirelli infrastructure for BKT-branded products, for a consideration not disclosed.
Management said BKT would not get access to Pirelli's technology or designs; each company keeps its own IP, with a clear partition between Pirelli-branded and BKT-branded production.

qa_highlights.question: What investment is needed for the Bhuj capacity and the Pirelli ramp-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the offtake is part of the ongoing expansion programme already announced last year; the JV would need additional investment, but no timeline or amount was given.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Pirelli deal be part of the 20% non-OHT revenue target for FY30?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, Pirelli revenue counts within the existing 20% non-OHT target; management said conviction in the Vision 2030 target has increased.

qa_highlights.question: Does BKT get access to Pirelli's technology, designs or SKUs?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said BKT will use its own technology and designs for its own products, and there will be a clear partition between Pirelli and BKT production.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a royalty payable to Pirelli?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no royalty and none was discussed. A separate service agreement covers Pirelli testing and simulation infrastructure for BKT products, for consideration.

qa_highlights.question: Will Pirelli's distribution network be available to BKT?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said distribution stays with each brand's own team; the tie-up is expected to ease channel acceptance for BKT car tires, not to share distribution.

qa_highlights.question: How many operating days should be assumed for 6,700 tires per day?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said roughly 350 to 355 days per year.

JV terms, timing, capex and the preset conditions are undisclosed; management declined to say whether the JV will be done by 2030.
Margin impact of the Pirelli conversion-based pricing has not been quantified; management declined to give revenue or margin potential by 2030.
Dilution risk to BKT's own car-tire positioning in the premium segment, since both brands share the same facility, though management said the brands differ in technology and price points.
Export mix and use of Bhuj output for Pirelli's global markets remain unclear.

502986|2026-03.headline: Vardhman sees industry spinning spreads near $0.90–0.95/kg versus ~$0.60–0.65 four months ago, but Q4 hit by ~INR57–58 crore forex mark-to-market loss.
502986|2026-03.overview: Management described a sharp turnaround in the Indian textile value chain over the past six months: US tariffs eased, cotton and yarn prices rose, and Chinese yarn demand lifted Indian exports. Q4 gross margin rose about 300 bps QoQ, but EBITDA was held back by an other-expense charge of about INR57–58 crore from mark-to-market on rupee forward cover after the rupee hit INR94.80 on 31 March. Management said fabric price increases lag yarn by 2–3 months, so Q4 did not fully reflect the improvement and Q1 FY27 should be better. The call gave no formal numeric guidance; most outlook comments were qualitative and tied to cotton, the dollar-rupee rate and the FTA pipeline.

financial_highlights.change: QoQ, as stated by analyst; management did not dispute

financial_highlights.metric: Forex mark-to-market loss charged to other expenses
financial_highlights.change: Q4 one-time hit; rupee at ~INR94.80 on 31 March
Up from ~$0.60–0.65 four months earlier; management cited 40–50% improvement

segments.name: Spinning (yarn)
segments.commentary: 30s combed yarn rose from ~$2.65–2.70/kg in Nov–Dec to ~$3.30–3.35/kg now. Management said yarn prices are set by international cotton and demand is strong, and that spinners are sold about 2–3 months forward in exports.

segments.name: Fabric
segments.commentary: Management said fabric price hikes are being pushed selectively, with a 2–3 month lag to yarn. The new performance (100% synthetic) fabric plant, commissioned last fiscal year, is expected to reach full use in 6–9 months.

segments.name: Garments
segments.commentary: Small existing garment capacity is being expanded to improve viability. Management said there is no decision on a large-scale garment expansion. Average realisation per shirt was stated as $7.5 after an initial misstatement of $5.

guidance_outlook: Management expects most textile companies, including Vardhman, to do far better in Q1 FY27 given the spread improvement, and said Q2 and Q3 should beat last year if current yarn prices, rupee and cotton levels hold.
Remaining ~10% of spinning modernisation to finish in the next 6–8 months; biomass boilers and other green power projects to commission in 1–2 months, with cost benefits from June or July.
Forex mark-to-market will reverse or add depending on where the dollar-rupee closes; no forecast was given.
Cotton: Vardhman normally holds 6–8 months of cotton cover; new Indian crop arrives around October, so stocks must be run down by September.
Management expects FTA-driven demand to build over roughly 12–15 months and is finalising capacity plans over the next 2–3 months.
capex_capacity: Spinning modernisation about 90% complete; remaining work to finish within the current financial year (next 6–8 months).

Performance fabric plant commissioned last fiscal year; 6–9 months needed to build order book. A fourth cotton and normal fabric line was also commissioned in FY26 but could not be fully used because of US tariffs; utilisation is expected in 6–9 months.
Open-end spinning project on hold to restart. New land in PM MITRA Park, Madhya Pradesh is expected by December or January, with plans to be finalised in 2–3 months.

Industry spindles: about 53 million rated; 11–12 million permanently stopped, leaving about 41–42 million working (industry estimate, not government data). Normal additions of 2–2.5 million per year were missed for three years.
Garment capacity expansion approved as a first step to viability; no decision on broader expansion.
demand_pricing: Chinese buying of Indian yarn rose to ~30 million kg per month over the last 4–5 months, against 7–8 million kg earlier. India's monthly yarn exports reached ~120 million kg-plus against a 100 million kg average.

Cotton: New York futures rose from ~$0.62–0.63/lb to ~$0.82–0.83/lb. Indian cotton moved from INR52,000–53,000/candy to INR67,000–68,000/candy; CCI selling price was INR67,000/candy after a ~INR5,000 rise in the last week.
Indian cotton is now priced around New York plus $0.05–0.08, close to the long-run relationship. Management said this removes the earlier disadvantage for spinners.

Pricing: fabric and garment price increases are being pushed across the chain. Brands are granting only small increases so far, with management expecting more clarity in 1–2 months. Yarn cost pass-through was described as comfortable given stronger demand.

Management noted US garment and home textile utilisation has recovered to roughly 90–100% after tariffs eased, from 50–60% earlier. Earlier, US tariffs reached 50%, which had forced discounting and loss-making orders.

qa_highlights.question: How has the cotton price move to parity with US cotton affected yarn demand and realisations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yarn prices follow international cotton and that higher Indian cotton cost is absorbed by Indian producers. Demand and higher cotton costs have been passed on comfortably so far.

qa_highlights.question: Can the spread gains be quantified and are they sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management put the spread at ~$0.90–0.95/kg against ~$0.60–0.65 four months earlier, about 40–50% higher. Sustainability depends on New York futures and China demand, which management could not predict.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 EBITDA margin expansion limited despite gross margin gains?
qa_highlights.answer: A ~INR57–58 crore forex mark-to-market charge at INR94.80/USD on export hedges was booked in other expenses. Management said the reversal depends on the year-end rupee rate.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q4 fabric lag mean stronger Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes: fabric price increases lag yarn by 2–3 months, and Q1 should be better, with Q2 and Q3 also better than last year if spreads hold.

qa_highlights.question: How long will spindle capacity take to return?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects expansion decisions in 6–9 months if margins hold for 3–6 months. About 1,000 small mills have closed, so consolidation is structural.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for garments and realisation per shirt?
qa_highlights.answer: Garment capacity expansion is an early viability step with no decision on broader expansion. Realisation was given as $7.5 per shirt.

risks_watch: Forex: Q4 carried a ~INR57–58 crore mark-to-market loss; Q1 reversal depends on where the dollar-rupee closes.
Cotton price durability: a fall in New York futures would compress the current spread. Hedge and speculative flows were cited as a source of volatility.
Policy: the government has not decided on duty-free cotton imports. Ministry support was described as aligned but unconfirmed.
Fabric pass-through lag and brand resistance to price increases.
Geopolitics: the Iran–US conflict has raised crude and logistics costs and affects polyester pricing; China's demand for Indian yarn may not last.
Spread and capacity figures are industry estimates (not government data) and could be revised.

502986|2026-06.headline: Vardhman Q1 FY27 margins rose on spinning yarn-size gains and raw-material trading gains; fabric utilisation remains weak as US orders slipped.
502986|2026-06.overview: Management said Q1 FY27 numbers improved in both percentage and absolute terms, driven mainly by the spinning business through better yarn sizes and a partial trading gain on raw material bought before the cotton price rise. The fabric business lagged: absolute volumes were roughly flat YoY and 3-4% below Q4 FY26, because US orders were lost after a missed sampling season tied to US tariffs. Management expects the spinning margin to moderate as cheap inventory runs out, but sees a 13-14% margin as a reasonable direction. Capex is mostly complete, with biomass boilers starting and the Dhar (PM MITRA) site dependent on land and power by around December 2026 and June 2027.

segments.name: Spinning (yarn)
segments.commentary: Utilisation full, margins good and demand strong; gains came from yarn-size mix and partial raw-material trading gains. Yarn export rose to about 110 million kg/month from 95-100 million kg, mostly from China (about 7-8% of production).

segments.name: Fabric (cotton and synthetic)
segments.commentary: Weak utilisation after losing US season orders; management says prices pass-through on yarn is only 60-70%, leaving 20-30% unrecovered. New synthetic fabric line has 15 lakh meters/month capacity at 15-20% utilisation, with two brand approvals and production starting in August 2026.

segments.name: Garments
segments.commentary: Current capacity about 7,000 shirts/day; plan to double to 4.5 million (units as stated) with peak revenue of about INR300 crore at full utilisation, targeted around Q1 FY28 (about one year from now). Mix is about 30% export and 70% domestic brands.

guidance_outlook: Management expects Q2 to show the benefit of higher yarn prices realised in April-May 2026, given the 3-month export and 45-day domestic order cover.

Indian cotton (CCI) rose from about INR55,000 to about INR64,000 per candy, now aligned with international prices; MSP up 6-7% implies cotton not below INR65,000-66,000 next season.

Spinning capacity: 12-13 million spindles closed in India over three years; only about 0.7-0.8 million spindles of expansion announced this year.

Export share of garments about 30%; domestic brands about 70%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the spinning order book and does the price rise show up in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Export orders cover about 90-95 days and domestic about 45-50 days historically, with the same cover today. Management confirmed the April-May price gains should show in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Margin sustainability after Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins will moderate as cheap inventory runs out, though not to the 2-3 year trough; trading margins may not persist at market cotton prices unless yarn rises further.

qa_highlights.question: Garment expansion economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Doubling capacity to 4.5 million (stated) could reach about INR300 crore revenue at 100%, with full operations about one year away due to worker training; the aim is stand-alone viability.

qa_highlights.question: Dhar capex and timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Dhar capex is not included in the INR3,600 crore plan. Construction starts only once land is given (expected December 2026) and power is assured (not before June 2027).

qa_highlights.question: Cotton yarn spread and where margins settle?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 spot spread was about USD0.90/kg. Management said historical range is USD0.85-1.00, with 13-14% margins reasonable.

qa_highlights.question: Will China keep buying Indian yarn?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects Chinese yarn imports to continue because of high Chinese cotton prices (over USD1 per lb) and Xinjiang-cotton risk, though this is not confirmed beyond current months.

Fabric utilisation and US order recovery, which management expects to improve over the next 2-3 months.

502986|2026-09.headline: Vardhman Q2 FY27: yarn business improved on demand and cotton-driven price hikes, while fabric remained weak with input costs up about 20% YoY.
502986|2026-09.overview: Management described Q2 FY27 as better than Q1 and the prior-year period, driven mainly by the yarn business, where demand from exports (including China-linked garment demand) and cotton-cost pass-through lifted yarn prices. Fabric was weaker: top line and bottom line fell versus both last year and Q1, hurt by lower export volumes amid US tariff uncertainty, domestic pricing pressure, and input costs up about 20% YoY. Management said order pipeline is improving, and it expects fabric utilisation and the synthetics business to improve in H2. Specific financial figures (revenue, EBITDA, PAT) were not read out on the call.

financial_highlights.value: Lower than prior-year quarter and Q1 (no absolute figures stated)
About 7,000 shirts per day; top line about INR150 crores

segments.commentary: Improved on stronger export demand and cotton-cost pass-through; management said part of the gain came from trading gains on cotton bought at INR54,000-55,000 per candy, which may not recur. Spinning utilisation is near 100%.

segments.name: Fabric (naturals and processing)
segments.commentary: Weak in Q2: export volumes down on US tariff uncertainty, domestic price pressure, and new processing capacity underutilised. Utilisation was about 70-75% in Q2 and about 80% currently.

segments.name: Synthetics / performance fabrics
segments.commentary: Commissioned in March; still in sampling and stabilisation. Two customers approved and placing orders at about 35-40% utilisation; break-even expected at about 50%; management expects operating-positive in H2 FY27.

segments.commentary: Around 7,000 shirts per day and about INR150 crores revenue; capacity being doubled at the existing location, with EBITDA targeted to rise from 7-8% to 13-14%.

qa_highlights.answer: Only one announced project (about 50 TPD open-end, about INR500 crores, operational in 6-7 months). A 100,000-spindle plant would cost at least INR1,000 crores; no new spinning capex approved yet.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for cotton prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Indian cotton tracks New York futures, which it sees at USD0.75-0.85 as a normal range; converted cost INR64,000-66,000 per candy. Analyst views on a tighter Indian crop suggest prices could stay firm unless duty-free imports arrive.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Bangladesh situation and how much yarn does Vardhman export there?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said wage unrest is cyclical and expected to settle around BDT17,000-18,000; India supplies about 30-35% of its yarn exports to Bangladesh and demand is unchanged. Vardhman-specific export figures were not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the fabric utilisation and peak revenue potential?
qa_highlights.answer: Fabric utilisation about 70-75% in Q2 and about 80% now, rising to 90-95% over a few quarters. Management declined to give absolute revenue potential but said at least about 15%, and an analyst's 25% math was not confirmed.

qa_highlights.question: Is M&A being considered to gain market share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is open to deals but said smaller targets are in poor condition; organic growth remains preferred. It cited uncertainty over government cotton import policy as the main constraint on large spinning expansion.

qa_highlights.question: What are the long-term growth, margin and ROE/ROCE expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Long-term EBITDA margin guidance 16%-20%; revenue CAGR 5%-8%; ROCE to improve as debt-equity moves from near zero and capital is deployed. An analyst noted ROE has fallen from 15-20% to 11-12%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cotton yarn spread today compared with Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Spread broadly comparable to Q2 on current cotton and yarn prices; differences can arise from inventory cost mix.

qa_highlights.question: What margin benefit is expected from renewable power and modernisation?
qa_highlights.answer: About 40-50% of renewable projects complete; remaining 50% expected in 3-4 months. Expected saving of about INR1-1.5 per unit on power cost, with biomass boilers replacing coal.

503100|2026-03.headline: Phoenix Mills FY26 consolidated revenue rose 16% to Rs 4,423 crore and EBITDA 22% to Rs 2,637 crore, with no new retail capacity added.
503100|2026-03.overview: FY26 showed strong broad-based growth: consolidated revenue Rs 4,423 crore (+16%), EBITDA Rs 2,637 crore (+22%), and PAT Rs 1,557 crore (+20%), achieved without adding retail area. Retail consumption hit a record Rs 16,587 crore (+21%), with Q4 up 31%, though retail rentals grew only 10% to Rs 2,157 crore, which management attributes to the MG-plus-revenue-share lease structure and ramp-up of newer malls. Offices expanded to 4.8 million sq ft with occupancy at 70%, and management expects a meaningful step-up in office income from FY27. Net debt to EBITDA improved to 1.19x despite the ISMDPL (CPP stake) buyout and peak construction capex.

qa_highlights.question: What is Q4 consumption growth excluding jewellery and electronics, and how will the rent-consumption gap move in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Ex-jewellery and electronics, Q4 consumption growth was about 17-18%. Management expects the gap to narrow as revenue share kicks in, and says rental growth should hold even if jewellery and electronics moderate.

qa_highlights.question: Will the PMC Pune and Bangalore consumption gains reflect in rentals, and when?
qa_highlights.answer: About 9% of area in both malls is leased but not yet trading, so rental upside lands in FY27; Pune is seen at 14-15% rental upside and Bangalore about 20%.

qa_highlights.question: What rental upside is expected from the roughly 50% of portfolio area expiring in the next 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims for rental uplift similar to FY26's roughly 20% blended new and renewal growth, supported by brand repositioning and F&B concepts like Gourmet Village; market conditions must remain supportive.

qa_highlights.question: When will office rental income start and how fast will it ramp?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue from newer office assets expected from Q2 FY27, growing quarter on quarter, with quarterly office income seen doubling by Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the consumption trend in April 2026?
qa_highlights.answer: April is very strong, with close to 30% growth including Akshay Tritiya; excluding jewellery and electronics, growth would be about 17-18%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the land strategy beyond 2030 and for new cities?
qa_highlights.answer: Scouting Hyderabad, Jaipur and Navi Mumbai; one or two new-city transactions targeted in FY27, plus conversion of existing assets such as Palladium and PMC Bangalore into super campuses.

risks_watch: Retail rental growth (10%) lagging consumption growth (21%); convergence depends on revenue share kicking in and jewellery/electronics mix.
Reliance on jewellery and electronics for consumption momentum, which carry low revenue share ratios.
Trading occupancy ramp-up at PMC Pune and Bangalore to 90% by end Q1 FY27 and 95-96% by end FY27.
Office occupancy at 70% overall, with Bangalore leased in the late 30s; RISE Commercial pre-leasing yet to be disclosed.
Kolkata residential launch timeline still pending; Kolkata and Surat malls in H2 FY28.
Macro volatility noted by analysts; management described hotel backdrop as challenging.
503100|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on retail and office leasing momentum, with specific numeric guidance for FY27 rental uplift. More measured on timelines for Kolkata residential and RISE pre-leasing, and declined to split minimum guarantee from revenue share income.
key_quotes: Importantly, we delivered this performance without adding any new retail capacity during the year.
Even as Q4 consumption moderated sequentially, retail rentals remained largely stable and retail EBITDA was essentially flat quarter-on-quarter.

We typically don't provide that breakup, Parikshit but you may consider 90% of the rental income to be fixed in nature and the rest is incremental revenue share over and above the fixed rent that we generate from retailers.
We will come back and make those disclosures, Mohit, the minute we start signing LOIs.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Office income expected to double by Q4 FY27 from Q2 FY27 onwards, and retail rental growth of 14-15% at Pune and about 20% at Bangalore should lift EBITDA faster than costs, after FY26 EBITDA grew 22% on revenue up 16%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new retail area was added in FY26 and the Kolkata and Surat malls only open in H2 FY28, so no new retail capacity lands in the window; office growth comes from leasing up existing 4.8 mn sq ft.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Retail consumption grew 21% to Rs 16,587 crore in FY26 with Q4 at +31% and April near 30%, and trading occupancy at PMC Pune and Bangalore is targeted at 90% by end Q1 FY27 and 95-96% by end FY27.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is only 70% on the 4.8 mn sq ft office portfolio and retail area is not being expanded, but management plans one or two new-city transactions (Hyderabad, Jaipur, Navi Mumbai) in FY27, and Rs 1,035 crore of construction capex was spent in FY26.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guides mid-to-high double-digit retail rental growth in FY27, and April consumption near 30% (17-18% ex jewellery and electronics) could push rentals above that if the revenue share kicks in faster than expected.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Rental growth of 10% trails consumption growth of 21%, and reliance on jewellery and electronics, which have low revenue-share ratios, could hold rentals back if those categories moderate.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Over 400 new stores opened in FY26 including Apple, Ikea and Uniqlo, and F&B concepts like Gourmet Village are being used to reposition brands at expiring leases covering about 50% of area over 2-3 years.

rows.label: Office leasing pipeline and RISE Commercial pre-leasing
rows.why: FY26 gross leasing was over 2.2 mn sq ft and several deals have commercials closed with documentation under way, though RISE Commercial pre-leasing is not yet disclosed and Bangalore is only in the late 30s % leased.

rows.label: New city transactions (Hyderabad, Jaipur, Navi Mumbai)
rows.why: Management targets one or two new-city announcements in FY27 after scouting, and the pipeline has been extended through 2030 to about 18 mn sq ft.

rows.label: Net debt/EBITDA below 1.2x despite ISMDPL buyout
rows.why: Net debt/EBITDA improved to 1.19x from 1.24x last year, with net debt at Rs 3,160 crore after the ISMDPL buyout and peak construction capex.

tone.note: Management was confident on retail consumption, April trading near 30%, and specific FY27 rental uplift numbers (Pune 14-15%, Bangalore ~20%), but measured on Kolkata residential timing, RISE pre-leasing, and declined to split minimum guarantee from revenue share; analysts pushed on the rent-consump

503100|2026-06.headline: Phoenix Mills Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 13% to Rs 1,075 crore and operating EBITDA 14% to Rs 642 crore, with retail consumption up 32%.
503100|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 13% YoY to Rs 1,075 crore and operating EBITDA grew 14% to Rs 642 crore at a 60% margin, with net profit up 23% to Rs 297 crore. Core annuity revenue rose 17% to Rs 1,033 crore and core EBITDA rose 19% to Rs 649 crore. Retail consumption grew 32% to Rs 4,730 crore, though jewelry and electronics drove much of that growth; ex-jewelry and electronics consumption grew 24% while rental grew 17%. Capex was Rs 1,085 crore, including Rs 716 crore paid to GAMADA for Chandigarh land, and net debt stood at Rs 3,658 crore (1.3x net debt/EBITDA).

financial_highlights.metric: Operating free cash flow (net of interest and tax)
financial_highlights.value: Rs 602 crore; core businesses Rs 584 crore
Rs 5,658 crore / Rs 3,658 crore; net debt/EBITDA 1.3x

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Rental income Rs 594 crore (+17%) and EBITDA Rs 625 crore (+17%); consumption Rs 4,730 crore (+32%), ex-jewelry and electronics +24%. Apparel and accessories (60% of trading area) +24%, jewelry +55%, electronics +61%, F&B and entertainment combined above 20%.

segments.name: Offices
segments.commentary: Income Rs 75 crore (+44% YoY) and EBITDA Rs 42 crore (+31% YoY). Leased occupancy 72% (June 2026) vs 70% a year earlier; rent-paying occupancy 42%, targeted to converge with leased occupancy by March 2027.

segments.name: Hospitality
segments.commentary: Income Rs 145 crore (+18% YoY) and EBITDA Rs 62 crore (+19% YoY); St. Regis Mumbai income +19% and EBITDA +20%.

segments.name: Residential
segments.commentary: Q1 booking Rs 64 crore and collection Rs 51 crore; about 1.5 lakh sq ft completed inventory unsold at OBW and Kessaku. About Rs 84 crore of sales (incl. Rs 20 crore carried over) expected to reflect in Q2.

guidance_outlook: Retail rental income guided to mid-teens growth for both FY27 and FY28, reiterated on the call.
Consumption: July 2026 trending above 20% growth; management expects healthy double-digit consumption growth going forward; September is seasonally the weakest month.
Retail rent-to-consumption ratio to be maintained in a 12% to 14% range (currently about 12.5%).

New openings in FY27-FY28: Phoenix Grand Victoria (Kolkata, about 1 million sq ft), Phoenix Surat (about 1 million sq ft, now end-2027 or early 2028), Phoenix Palladium expansion (about 4.5 lakh sq ft, FY27/FY28, about 50% leased), Phoenix MarketCity Bangalore Phase-2 (about 170,000 sq ft F&B floor, early 2027), Whitefield offices (about 0.4 million sq ft) and 400-key Grand Hyatt.
Offices: leased occupancy targeted at 90% by end FY27 for Phoenix Asia Towers and One National Park Chennai.
Residential launches in Kolkata and Bengaluru by end 2026 or early 2027; Kolkata about 1.2 million sq ft at a launch price around Rs 30,000 per sq ft (approximate).

Surat and Kolkata openings slipping into end-2027 or early 2028, and Palladium expansion timing (FY27/FY28), are execution items.
Office rent-paying occupancy at 42% must converge toward 72% leased occupancy by March 2027.
