September consumption seasonally weakest; Q2 consumption outcome is the next checkpoint.
503100|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on operating momentum and leasing, with cautious qualifiers on the timing of new openings and on gold-linked consumption. Management was evasive on the anchor-level split of expiries and avoided giving a firm launch date for Surat, Kolkata residential and Lower Parel plans.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the Bengaluru residential and Kolkata launch now pushed to early 2027, and what product and price for Kolkata?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said timelines are indicative, driven by approvals and RERA rather than delay; Bengaluru sold at about Rs 36,000 per sq ft in Q1. Kolkata is about 1.2 million sq ft at around Rs 30,000 per sq ft, a premium gated community.

qa_highlights.question: Will fashion rental growth catch up to the 24% consumption growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to 50% of the portfolio expiring over three years and said rental growth will come from renewals, new assets and revenue share; partnership model means no maximisation of short-term rent. Non-gold consumption +24% vs rent +17%.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 8.7 million sq ft expiry is anchors and what is the mark-to-market upside?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not provide the anchor breakup and avoided guidance on mark-to-market; past expiries have driven rental growth of 20% to 30%. Mall of Asia reached Rs 3,000 per sq ft trading density within three years.

qa_highlights.question: Lower Parel: pre-leasing status, rates, and timing of development plan for the extra FSI?
qa_highlights.answer: Pre-leasing has started with some area committed at Rs 350 to 400 per sq ft on leasable area. Development plans for the additional FSI to be shared after Rise Retail opens; approvals partly secured.

qa_highlights.question: Jewelry and electronics contribution to rental income, and gold price exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Jewelry and electronics are about 5% of trading area, 28% of consumption and about 7.5% of rental income; management acknowledged jewelry growth partly reflects higher gold prices that may reverse.

qa_highlights.question: Surat timing and rental contribution from FY28 openings?
qa_highlights.answer: Surat expected by end-2027 or early 2028, launch date to be fixed by mid-next year. Fixed rent starts from first month of tenant trading; malls take about 12 months to reach 85% to 90% occupancy.

qa_highlights.question: Consumption outlook after July and rent-to-consumption trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: July trending above 20%; September weakest month. Rent-to-consumption expected in 12% to 14% range, currently about 12.5%; mid-teens rental growth guided for FY27 and FY28.

capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 capex Rs 1,085 crore: Rs 314 crore construction and Rs 771 crore land acquisition and development rights, mainly Rs 716 crore balance payment to GAMADA for Chandigarh land; Chandigarh now wholly owned by PML and excavation has started.

Retail pipeline: Phoenix Grand Victoria (Kolkata, about 1 million sq ft) and Phoenix Surat (about 1 million sq ft, end-2027 or early 2028), Phoenix Palladium expansion (about 4.5 lakh sq ft, FY27/FY28, about 50% leased), Phoenix MarketCity Bangalore Phase-2 (F&B floor about 170,000 sq ft, early 2027, 30-plus restaurants).

Offices: Whitefield Bengaluru about 0.4 million sq ft and 400-key Grand Hyatt in Whitefield; Whitefield Phase-3 approvals secured, civil work to start shortly. Lower Parel Project Rise plus adjacent tower 1.5 to 1.6 million sq ft; pre-leasing started at Rs 350 to 400 per sq ft on leasable area.

Residential: Kolkata about 1.2 million sq ft, launch price around Rs 30,000 per sq ft (indicative); Bengaluru launch by end-2026 or early 2027, Q1 average realisation about Rs 36,000 per sq ft. Thane total potential over 4 million sq ft (1.3 million sq ft mall, about 400-key hotel, 1.2 million sq ft office); Chandigarh mall 1.5 to 1.7 million sq ft.

Capacity: retail platform targeted at 18 million sq ft by 2030; Thane, Chandigarh and Coimbatore completions targeted by 2030. Office platform about 5 million sq ft across Mumbai, Pune, Bengaluru and Chennai versus about 2 million sq ft in 2024.
demand_pricing: Consumption Rs 4,730 crore, +32% YoY; ex-jewelry and electronics +24%; trading density +26%. Apparel and accessories (60% of trading area) +24%, jewelry +55%, electronics +61%, F&B and entertainment combined above 20%, F&B alone +26% in the rest-of-portfolio view.

Jewelry and electronics occupy about 5% of trading area, contribute 28% of consumption and about 7.5% of rental income; productivity about 5 times portfolio average. Rest of portfolio (~70%) consumption +24%, rental +17%.
July 2026 consumption trending above 20% growth; management expects healthy double-digit consumption growth going forward; September seasonally weakest month.
Rental income Rs 594 crore (+17%); rent-to-consumption about 12.5%, down from about 14% three years ago; management guides 12% to 14%. Mid-teens rental growth guided for FY27 and FY28.

Leasing: over 300 transactions covering nearly 1 million sq ft in Q1; about 390 new stores in last 12 months; malls leased at 97% to 98%; Phoenix MarketCity Pune (Avenue of Stars) consumption +29%, Bengaluru consumption +22%, both at 89% trading occupancy. About 50% of portfolio up for lease expiry over next three years (8.7 million sq ft over five years cited by analyst); anchor split not disclosed.

key_quotes: So, total Rs. 84 crore sales is likely to reflect in Q2 which has already been done till 30th June.
And how you do in that month actually makes or breaks your consumption numbers for the quarter.

503100|2026-09.headline: Phoenix Mills Q2 FY27 annuity EBITDA rose 21% to Rs 669 crore, with retail consumption up 25% and rental income up 15%.
503100|2026-09.overview: Annuity revenue (retail, offices, hotel, asset management) grew 16% YoY to Rs 1,055 crore in Q2, with annuity EBITDA up 21% to Rs 669 crore and PAT before minority interest up 31% to Rs 391 crore. Consolidated revenue of Rs 1,153 crore was held back by lower residential handovers (Rs 62 crore recognised in H1), with Rs 120 crore of sold units slated for H2. Office occupancy rose to about 79% in September 2026 from 70% in March 2026, and consumption grew 25% with no new retail area added. Management reaffirmed double-digit rental growth for FY28, stated retail rental guidance of 15% for FY27 could be exceeded, and disclosed progress on the ISMDPL stake step-up to 68.1%.

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Rental income up 15% to Rs 605 crore in Q2 and 16% to Rs 1,200 crore in H1; retail EBITDA up 18% to Rs 639 crore in Q2. Consumption Rs 4,685 crore (+25%); excluding jewellery and electronics +22%.

segments.name: Offices
segments.commentary: Office income up 64% YoY to Rs 89 crore and EBITDA up similarly to Rs 56 crore in Q2; 54% of the new office portfolio is rent generating against 79% leased.

segments.name: Hospitality
segments.commentary: The St. Regis Mumbai income and EBITDA up 13% in Q2, with average room rate up 20% and EBITDA margin at 44%.

segments.name: Residential
segments.commentary: Revenue recognised on handover; only Rs 62 crore in H1 versus a significantly higher prior-year period. Rs 120 crore of sold units to be booked in H2 FY27.

guidance_outlook: Retail rental growth guidance of 14-15% for FY27 (given in April) expected to be exceeded by 1-2 percentage points, per management.
Rental growth of 14-15% factored for FY28 as the more tangible metric; double-digit rental growth expected in FY28 from existing assets.
Phoenix Mall of Asia expected to sustain healthy double-digit consumption growth in FY28.
October 2026 consumption expected at least 20% YoY on a normalised basis, with upside toward 25%; full-month figures due late November.
ISMDPL stake to rise from 58.33% to 68.1% on completion of capital reduction, expected November 2026, for Rs 1,350 crore consideration. Credit rating upgrades expected in one to two weeks.

Surat mall: 50% leased, completion by 2027 and opening in 2028. Bengaluru Whitefield retail expansion (1-1.5 lakh sq ft): completion by 2027, about 70% leased.
Palladium (Lower Parel) Rise 1 expansion: about 150 stores, 60% leased, rentals expected above Rs 500 psf pm; mall operational in calendar 2027. Rise offices targeted for 2028.
Thane, Chandigarh and Coimbatore malls targeted for operations in calendar 2030. Bengaluru first-phase office (about 400,000 sq ft) and Grand Hyatt Bangalore hotel to become operational.
Lucknow Palassio adds about 100,000 sq ft (about 100 stores) with a further floor; Palladium adds 150 stores. Land spend H1 about Rs 800 crore, construction spend H1 about Rs 700 crore.
demand_pricing: Consumption up 25% YoY to Rs 4,685 crore in Q2 and 28% to Rs 9,415 crore in H1; every mall delivered double-digit consumption growth.
Trading occupancy rose only about 3 percentage points YoY; management attributed not more than 3% of the 25% growth to added trading area.
Fashion and accessories (about 60% of trading area) +22%; F&B +21%; entertainment +16%.

Phoenix Mall of Asia consumption +68%, rental +44%, trading occupancy 96% vs 84%. Bengaluru MarketCity consumption +19%, rental +25%, occupancy 93% vs 82%. Pune Avenue of Stars consumption +21%, rental +16%, occupancy 90% vs 82%.
Trading density crossed Rs 3,300 psf pm. Rent-to-consumption ratio at 13%, against a long-term range of 13.5-14%.
About 50% of retail area lease expiries fall between FY27 and FY29; repricing typically gives about 20% uplift on prior minimum guarantee rents.
September was seasonally weak; 2-3% of quarterly consumption lost to fit-outs, with 5% of leasable area under active fit-out.

qa_highlights.question: Why is residential at Kolkata not yet launched more than three and a half years after land acquisition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited an initial plan change from a different use to pure residential and approval delays linked to elections; launch expected in about two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the pre-leasing status of upcoming malls (Kolkata, Surat, Bengaluru, Palladium)?
qa_highlights.answer: Kolkata about 90% leased, Surat 50%, Bengaluru expansion about 70%, Palladium Rise 1 about 60%.

qa_highlights.question: Is October consumption growth tracking?
qa_highlights.answer: Normalised for Diwali timing, October is expected at least 20% YoY, possibly toward 25%; final figures due late November.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 rental growth exceed the 15% guidance given the 16% H1 growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects guidance to be raised by 1-2 percentage points and is optimistic it can be exceeded, pending festive-season data.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 10-city pipeline raise the 1 million sq ft annual addition guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said land is not yet secured for the new cities, so no timelines or guidance change; new cities expected in the 2035-36 plan. Benchmark per new mall moves to 1.3-1.4 million sq ft.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Rs 1,440 crore H1 capex in the cash flow reconcile with lower construction spend?
qa_highlights.answer: Difference is land: Chandigarh land completion payment of about Rs 700 crore in Q1, plus smaller Coimbatore and Kolkata parcels and an advance for an acquisition under discussion.

503101|2026-03.headline: FY26 consolidated PAT of INR 206 crores, the company's highest ever, alongside INR 900 crores QIP and INR 576 crores FY26 presales (MNRL share).
503101|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as transformational, citing record PAT of INR 206 crores on total income of INR 639 crores and EBITDA of INR 261 crores. The INR 900 crore QIP was used for about INR 340 crores of debt repayment, roughly a third for existing project execution, and about INR 300 crores earmarked for new acquisitions, of which only about INR 54 crores (call also cited ~INR 50 crores) was deployed. The company acquired controlling interests in three Kanjurmarg entities (~INR 70 crores investment) with a six-project pipeline of over INR 840 crores GDV, and took a 90% stake in Sunset Spaces Pvt Ltd. The amalgamation has received no-adverse-observation letters from BSE and NSE and documents have been filed with NCLT, with hearing awaited.

503101|2026-06.headline: Marathon Nextgen Q1 FY27 total income hit INR 217 crores, a multi-quarter high, with PAT of INR 52 crores and INR 900 crores of new redevelopment GDV added.
503101|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 total income of INR 217 crores (multi-quarter high), EBITDA of INR 66 crores and PAT of INR 52 crores. Sales on the existing portfolio were 38,000 sq ft with booking value of INR 86 crores and collections of INR 118 crores (MNRL's 40% share of Monte South); including the merged portfolio, sales were 46,000 sq ft, booking value INR 108 crores and collections INR 146 crores. Two redevelopment projects (Versova and Sewri, INR 450 crores GDV each) were added, and the company says it is debt-free with about INR 200 crores of acquisition capital after a INR 900 crore QIP. The merger with group entities is awaiting NCLT shareholder and creditor meetings in early September 2026.

segments.commentary: Futurex combined sales ~4,000 sq ft, booking INR 19 crores, collections INR 23 crores; Futurex has OC. Millennium sold over 1,000 sq ft, booking INR 3 crores, collections INR 1 crore; under construction.

qa_highlights.question: How large is the redevelopment pipeline beyond INR 900 crores, and how are deals selected?

503101|2026-09.headline: Marathon Nextgen Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue INR145 crore and PAT INR45 crore; Monte South stake to rise from 40% to 100% for INR335 crore.

The Board approved buying Adani Group's 60% stake in Monte South for INR335 crore (INR200 crore already paid), taking Marathon's ownership from 40% to 100%, with completion expected this quarter. The company said it ended September with a net debt-free balance sheet and a positive net cash position.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Pre-sales rose to INR154 crore in Q2 from INR86 crore in Q1 and area sold to 71,000 sq ft from 38,000 sq ft; Monte South run rate about INR300 crore so far, extrapolated to about INR600 crore for FY27, though management gave no formal guidance.

rows.label: New capex announcement

rows.label: Guidance upgrade

rows.label: Guidance downgrade

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Monte South commercial (GDV about INR3,400 crore) is slated for FY28 and Versova and Sewri (about INR900 crore combined) to launch within two financial years, though approvals gate timing and no Q2 launches occurred.

rows.label: Monte South stake step-up to 100%

rows.label: Monte South remaining bookings of about INR7,000 crore

rows.label: Proposed amalgamation NCLT approval

503722|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose to a record Rs1,370 crore-scale year with EBITDA up 22.5% to Rs144 crore; FY27 guided to Rs1,450-1,500 crore.
503722|2026-03.overview: Banswara Syntex reported Q4 FY26 total income of Rs369.3 crore, with EBITDA up 46% YoY to Rs46 crore and PAT of Rs9.6 crore (up 87% YoY). For FY26, EBITDA was about Rs144 crore (margin near 11%) and PAT Rs28.4 crore (up 32.8%) after a one-time Rs9 crore labour code exceptional charge. Fabric and Garment grew, while Yarn volumes and revenue fell on labour shortages in spinning. Management guided to FY27 revenue of Rs1,450-1,500 crore and EBITDA margin of 10.5-11% over the medium term, with near-term margin pressure from raw material pass-through lag.

financial_highlights.value: Rs28.4 crore (after Rs9 crore one-time labour code expense)

financial_highlights.change: vs Rs456 crore a year earlier

financial_highlights.value: 20% on face value, total Rs3.42 crore

segments.name: Yarn
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue Rs113 crore (vs Rs123 crore; management corrected the gap to Rs10 crore), FY26 Rs449 crore vs Rs460 crore (about -2%). Volume 46 lakh kg in Q4 and 194 lakh kg in FY26; utilisation 78% in Q4 and 77% for FY26. Realisations up about Rs30-35/kg.

segments.name: Fabrics
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue Rs154 crore (vs Rs145 crore); FY26 record Rs569 crore, up 5%. Volume 62 lakh meters in Q4 and 230 lakh meters in FY26; utilisation 77% in Q4. Middle East exports affected.

segments.name: Garments
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue Rs96 crore, up 40%; FY26 Rs324 crore, up 18%. Volume 11 lakh pieces in Q4 and 39 lakh pieces in FY26; FY26 utilisation 72% vs about 50% in FY25. Walmart added about Rs15 crore of Q4 revenue.

segments.name: Associate Tesca Textiles (40% stake)
segments.commentary: Management said Tesca had turnover of about Rs100 crore and PAT of about Rs10 crore, with Banswara's share about Rs4 crore. No plan to raise stake.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guided to Rs1,450-1,500 crore, led by Fabric and Garment; FY26 was about Rs1,370 crore.
Management targets about 20% revenue growth in both Fabric and Garment in FY27; Garment division projects 18-20%.
EBITDA margin expected at 10.5-11% over the medium term; near-term margins may dip as raw material costs are passed on.
FY27 capex planned at Rs135-140 crore (an analyst cited Rs130-150 crore); Garment capex only Rs3-5 crore.
Long-term debt expected to rise in FY27 on planned capex and reduce from FY28 onwards; no reduction in total borrowings this year.
Management expects H2 FY27 growth to exceed H1; Garment momentum to improve from Q2 after a subdued Q1.
capex_capacity: Yarn and Fabric capacity was reshaped toward finer counts, Siro Compact yarn (about 200 tons per month) and worsted finishing machines; management says installed capacity fell YoY partly due to mix shift.
Garment capacity: about 70,000 pieces per month available vs 40,000-50,000 jackets used; could go to 80,000 with long runs.
Surat SEZ garment capacity (about 40,000-50,000 jackets and about 100,000 pants) awaits approval; timeline not given, file under process with Industries Commissionerate and Kandla SEZ.
Management said Garment expansion could start mid-year (Q2/Q3 FY27) and that Rs2,000 crore revenue is possible without significant capex, with no firm timeline.
Capex items: zero water discharge project, a 132 KVA power line application, and other infrastructure and sustainability spend.
demand_pricing: Polyester raw material costs up about 25% due to the Middle East conflict; yarn prices raised but not fully passed on.
Wool prices rose sharply, from Australia and China; management says customers take 6 months to 1 year to accept new prices.
Rupee depreciation of about 6-7% helped export realisations without price increases.
Walmart added as a Garment customer; JC Penney (Fabric) and Mango (Garment) already customers; Celio and Marks & Spencer cited as large relationships.
Middle East exposure about Rs100 crore; Rs8-9 crore of Q4 product could not ship on time; management expects Rs10-20 crore lower sales to the region in FY27.
US demand improving; company says it is more competitive than China in spun-synthetic segment.
D2C brand One Mile averages about Rs15 lakh per month; fundraising planned once it reaches about Rs1 crore per month.

qa_highlights.question: Have new export clients been added, such as Walmart?
qa_highlights.answer: Walmart is a new addition; it contributed about Rs15 crore of Q4 Garment revenue. Management aims for 20% growth in Garment and Fabric next year and sees no need for many more large clients.

qa_highlights.question: Why did installed capacity fall YoY despite investments?
qa_highlights.answer: Finer counts and worsted machines lower kg output; capacity is planned around realistic labour availability. Management says labour shortages persist into May.

qa_highlights.question: Is the labour shortage transient or structural?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says automation is not viable given many SKUs; focus is on scaling winning products and shifting from made-to-order to predictive analytics planning.

qa_highlights.question: How will the borrowings be reduced?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said no reduction in FY27 as long-term debt rises on capex; long-term debt to reduce from FY28 on 5-7 year loan tenures. Working capital rise is linked to customer ready inventory; inventory above 90 days is watched.

qa_highlights.question: What are segment-wise margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give exact segment margins due to internal transfers (about 33% of yarn and 25% of fabric is internal). Segment margins are said to be close to company level; Garment was previously at breakeven.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Middle East impact and pass-through?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said polyester costs rose about 25%; price increases partly accepted, and export pricing benefited from rupee weakness. Middle East exposure is about Rs100 crore.

qa_highlights.question: When will FTAs (UK, EU) matter, and can Rs1,800 crore be reached?
qa_highlights.answer: UK FTA expected around September and EU by December end per management, with no certainty. Management hopes for Rs1,800 crore in the year after FY27 and is willing to accept 11% EBITDA to keep 20% growth.

risks_watch: Labour shortages in spinning and garments, particularly in April to June, could keep Yarn utilisation at 77-78%.
Raw material cost pass-through lag of 6 to 12 months may compress margins in H1 FY27.
Middle East logistics and demand; Rs10-20 crore lower sales to the region expected in FY27.
Surat SEZ approval timing is uncertain, and no firm Garment capacity expansion date was given.
Net debt rose to Rs483 crore; the long-term debt reduction only starts from FY28, while FY27 capex is Rs135-140 crore.
FTA benefits (UK, EU) are not yet certain; Q1 FY27 Garment orders expected to be subdued.
503722|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on Garment growth and export wins, but cautious on near-term margins, Q1 FY27 demand, and the Middle East. Management avoided firm timelines on Surat SEZ, FTAs and the Rs2,000 crore revenue target, and declined to give segment margins.
key_quotes: So, we are happy even if we get 11% EBITDA, but we grow 20% for this present financial year because we do not want to stifle the growth by jacking up the prices to an extent where the customers shy away.
Walmart has been definitely a new addition, and we saw the impact of that happening in our quarter four results in the Garment division, where we achieved INR96 crores turnover.
Near-term margins may go down as the raw material costs are being passed on.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Garment capacity is about 70,000 pcs/month against 40,000-50,000 used, so existing headroom covers growth, but Surat SEZ (40-50k jackets, 100k pants) awaits approval with no timeline and Garment expansion has no firm date; Yarn utilisation is only 77%.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management targets about 20% growth in Fabric and Garment and expects H2 FY27 growth above H1, backed by Walmart adding about Rs15 crore of Q4 Garment revenue, though Yarn volumes fell in FY26 (194 lakh kg).

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY27 capex of Rs135-140 crore is already planned (Garment only Rs3-5 crore), and Surat SEZ filing is under process, though a new capex announcement beyond this is not signalled given utilisation of 77%.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue guided at Rs1,450-1,500 crore (about 6-9% over FY26 Rs1,370 crore), and management avoided firm timelines on the Rs2,000 crore target and FTA benefits, with Q1 FY27 Garment orders expected subdued.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Labour shortages persist into May with Yarn utilisation at 77-78%, Middle East sales expected Rs10-20 crore lower in FY27, and Rs8-9 crore of Q4 product could not ship on time.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Yarn shifted toward finer counts with Siro Compact (about 200 tons/month) and worsted finishing machines; D2C brand One Mile at about Rs15 lakh/month with fundraising planned at Rs1 crore/month, but no firm launch dates were given.

rows.why: Management expects UK FTA around September and EU by December end, with no certainty, and hopes for Rs1,800 crore revenue in the year after FY27.

rows.why: Net debt already Rs483 crore (vs Rs456 crore) with FY27 capex Rs135-140 crore; no reduction in total borrowings in FY27, with long-term debt falling only from FY28 on 5-7 year tenures.

tone.note: Management was confident on Garment growth, Walmart and export wins, and the rupee tailwind, but cautious on near-term margins, Q1 FY27 demand, labour shortages and the Middle East; it avoided firm timelines on Surat SEZ, FTAs and the Rs2,000 crore target and declined segment margins.

503722|2026-06.headline: Banswara Syntex Q1 FY27 total income rose 4.1% to INR322.4 crores with PAT of INR4.4 crores versus a loss of INR1.4 crores; management reiterates FY27 revenue of INR1,450–1,500 crores.
503722|2026-06.overview: Total income grew 4.1% YoY to INR322.4 crores and EBITDA was INR29.5 crores (about 9% margin), with PAT of INR4.4 crores against a loss a year earlier. Fabric grew 25% YoY while yarn and garment revenues fell, mainly on labour shortages in spinning, higher internal yarn consumption and garment dispatches delayed by West Asia logistics. Management kept FY27 guidance of about INR1,500 crores revenue and 12% EBITDA, relying on a garment order book booked through November/December and a recovery in H2. Analysts pressed hard on the low top-line growth over a decade and on the pace of garment capacity additions.

segments.name: Yarn
segments.commentary: Revenue INR96 crores (vs INR110 crores YoY); sales volume 36 lakh kg at 70% capacity utilisation. Higher internal transfers to fabric and garments reduced external sales; labour shortage cut output.

segments.name: Fabric
segments.commentary: Revenue INR147 crores (+25% YoY); volume 59 lakh meters (+18% YoY) at 80% utilisation. Growth driven by value-added bi-stretch and wool blends; Q1 margin was in line with the 12–14% target. Roughly 50:50 export and domestic.

segments.name: Garment
segments.commentary: Revenue INR69 crores (vs INR75 crores YoY); 8 lakh pieces at 69% utilisation. West Asia logistics delayed dispatches; margin below target (8–10% expected) due to container availability. About 60% export, 40% domestic.

segments.name: Jackets (within garment)
segments.commentary: Q1 closed at about 135,000 jackets, soft demand. Run rate now upwards of 75,000 a month; FY27 target 800,000–900,000 jackets versus about 600,000 a year on average.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of about INR1,450–1,500 crores maintained; management expects garment at about INR100 crores per quarter for the next three quarters and about INR375–380 crores for the year plus export incentives.
Consolidated EBITDA target of about 12% for FY27 versus 9% in Q1; segment targets: fabric 12–14%, garment 8–10%, yarn 8–10%.
Yarn expected to normalise progressively as labour availability improves; management expects visible improvement from Q2.
Surat facility targeted for DTA use by November/December 2026 and operations from April 2027; main impact in FY28. Restart seen adding about INR200 crores of runway for about INR50 crores investment.
Garment EU operationalisation with Mango, Celio and C&A targeted by end-December 2026/early January 2027.
capex_capacity: Capex of about INR140 crores planned and sanctioned for this year across fabric, garment and common infrastructure.
Management targets about 20–25% garment expansion and about 20% fabric expansion in FY28, with a further 20% in FY28 as stated; yarn to be maintained or marginally grown.
Over the last three years, about INR350 crores invested: about INR150 crores in fabric and about INR130 crores in yarn; management said the modernisation phase is complete.
Surat facility shut to move into DTA; Daman capacity to be fully utilised this year.
demand_pricing: Garment order book fully booked through November and into December; fabric order book shows orders up to November end.
Demand healthy in US and domestic markets; Europe and Middle East softer in fabric.
India-UK FTA effective 15 July 2026; UK fabric exposure about INR70–80 crores a year; UK garment about INR20–25 crores, targeted to double to at least INR50 crores next year.
Two EU anchor garment customers (Mango and Celio) about INR100 crores of revenue; C&A onboarded with trial orders; new UK customers Haggar and NEXT added in fabric.
Domestic yarn realisations improved, partly offsetting lower volumes.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export contribution for fabric and garments, and what are the jacket volumes and segment margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Overall exports 48%; fabric and garment together about 70% of export turnover. Jackets: about 600,000 a year average, FY27 expected 800,000–900,000. Segment margin targets given (fabric 12–14%, garment and yarn 8–10%).

qa_highlights.question: Why is the sequential drop so sharp in garment and yarn, and is the garment shortfall shipment timing or lost demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed Q1 weakness to a weak autumn/winter export season and seasonal domestic lull, plus delayed shipments. July garment sales were on target at about INR30 crores, with quarterly run-rate expected to reach about INR100 crores.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 EBITDA guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets about 12% EBITDA for FY27 on INR1,500 crores revenue; Q1 was 9%, with the rest expected to average out to 12% over the remaining three quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Why is revenue growth muted despite about INR500 crores of capex over five years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yarn capacity was under-used because of labour issues and the investments are now expected to lift top line and bottom line; fabric growth of about 20% a year is expected from its investments.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company different this decade, given flat revenue since FY19 and weak margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed the dissolution of the French JV for lost sales a decade ago, said product mix is much better, and cited import substitution of Chinese goods and FTAs. Garment export share rose from about 20% to about 60%, with a target of 70%.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any update on the Surat facility?
qa_highlights.answer: GIDC approvals and no-objection certificate received; customs duty clearance and SEZ debonding pending, expected within 3–5 months. Restart would involve fresh machinery, adding about INR200 crores of capacity for about INR50 crores.

risks_watch: Garment margin recovery (targeted 8–10%) depends on export mix and on timely container availability; Q1 garment EBITDA fell short.
Yarn utilisation (70% in Q1) depends on labour availability; labour shortages recur each festival and marriage season.
FY27 guidance needs about INR1,000 crores or more of revenue in Q2–Q4 at the stated quarterly run rate, with H2 weighted delivery.
Europe and Middle East fabric demand softer; West Asia logistics disruptions continue to delay shipments.
Surat restart timelines (DTA by Nov/Dec 2026, operations April 2027) and capex of about INR140 crores; benefits seen mainly in FY28.
Debt rising to about INR500 crores per analyst estimate; past capex has not yet translated into revenue growth.

financial_highlights.change: vs loss of INR1.4 crores in Q1 FY26
vs INR110 crores in Q1 FY26 (decline)
vs INR75 crores in Q1 FY26 (decline)

key_quotes: Our order book continues to be robust and is fully booked through to November and even December now, providing us with strong revenue visibility and confidence for the coming quarters.
So imagine if the yarn utilization goes up to 90%, you will have a really good top line and bottom line both happening.
We hope to recover the rest in the 3 quarters that are to come to average out 12%. We are still maintaining that.
So we are looking at closing close to about INR400 crores this year.

Cautious and somewhat defensive on the sharp Q1 shortfall, which management attributed to labour shortages, shipment delays and a weak autumn/winter export season, and on the decade of flat revenue.

rows.why: Fabric volume grew 18% YoY to 59 lakh meters, jackets run rate is above 75,000 a month against a FY27 target of 800,000-900,000 versus about 600,000 a year, and garment order book is booked through November/December.

rows.why: About INR140 crores of capex is already planned and sanctioned this year, and utilisation is only 70% in yarn, 80% in fabric and 69% in garment, so the capex is committed rather than new.

rows.why: Q1 total income was INR322.4 crores and FY27 guidance of INR1,450-1,500 crores needs about INR1,000 crores or more in Q2-Q4, so management is only holding guidance and an upgrade is not supported.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q1 revenue was about 22% of the INR1,500 crore target and garment margin fell short of 8-10%, with yarn at 70% utilisation and labour shortages recurring, so the back-half weighted delivery is at risk.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management referenced new UK customers Haggar and NEXT in fabric, C&A trial orders and garment EU operationalisation with Mango, Celio and C&A by end-December 2026/early January 2027, but no new product launch was specified.

rows.why: India-UK FTA effective 15 July 2026 with UK garment exposure of about INR20-25 crores targeted to at least INR50 crores next year, and EU garment operationalisation with Mango, Celio and C&A targeted by end-December 2026.

rows.label: Garment order book booked through Nov/Dec
rows.why: Garment order book is fully booked through November and into December, and July garment sales were on target at about INR30 crores against a quarterly run rate of about INR100 crores.

rows.label: Debt rising toward INR500 crores
rows.why: Analyst estimate has debt rising to about INR500 crores while capex of about INR140 crores is sanctioned and past INR350 crores of investment has not yet translated into revenue growth.

503722|2026-09.headline: Banswara Syntex Q2 FY27 total income rose 11.2% QoQ to INR358.4 crore; EBITDA INR36.5 crore at 10.2% margin, PAT INR8.1 crore.
503722|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 total income was INR358.4 crore, up 11.2% QoQ, with EBITDA of INR36.5 crore and margin of 10.2% versus 9.1% in Q1. PAT rose to INR8.1 crore from INR4.4 crore in Q1. H1 FY27 total income grew about 3.6% YoY to INR680.8 crore, EBITDA rose 18.9% to INR66 crore, and PAT more than doubled to INR12.5 crore. Net debt rose INR43.28 crore in H1 to INR515 crore, mainly on working capital tied to higher raw material prices. Management reconfirmed FY27 guidance of higher turnover and EBITDA margin expansion, which the call framed as 10.5-11% (per analyst), relying on H2 seasonality, order book and pass-through of raw material costs.

financial_highlights.change: +84% QoQ from INR4.4 crore in Q1 FY27
+INR43.28 crore in H1, mainly working capital

segments.name: Yarn
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR103 crore vs INR112 crore YoY; H1 INR199 crore vs INR222 crore, as internal transfers rose. Capacity utilisation 84% in Q2 vs 81% in Q2 FY26 and 70% in Q1 FY27.

segments.name: Fabric
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR157 crore, up about 5% YoY; H1 up 14% to INR303 crore. Volume was 58 lakh meters in Q2 (vs 59 lakh) and 118 lakh meters in H1 (vs 109 lakh, +8%). Utilisation 82% in Q2 vs 77%; H1 81% vs 73%.

segments.name: Garments
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR90 crore, up 13% YoY and 30% QoQ; H1 INR160 crore vs INR155 crore. Volume up 10 lakh pieces in Q2 and 18 lakh pieces in H1. Utilisation 74% in H1 FY27 vs 78% last year (corrected on call).

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance reconfirmed: turnover and EBITDA margin expected to rise; analyst cited 10.5-11% FY27 EBITDA margin target, which management did not dispute.

Management said it is on course for at least double-digit revenue growth and an overall double-digit EBITDA margin, in response to a question on FY28 (answer was framed as a continuing quarter-by-quarter trend).
Garment FY27 sales expected at INR360-380 crore, growth over FY26.
Surat garment facility, if live next year, expected to add INR75-100 crore turnover in the following year; full ramp over about 2 years to add INR150-200 crore, taking garments to INR550-600 crore.
Capex for Surat expected at INR30-50 crore depending on automation; FY27 capex guidance of INR130-140 crore, with INR36 crore spent in H1 and most projects, including ETP, to complete in H2.
capex_capacity: Capex guidance of about INR130-140 crore for FY27; about INR36 crore spent in H1. Management said there is no delay and that most projects, including ETP and environment-related work, will complete in H2.
Surat garment plant sits in an SEZ; customs NOC expected by end-November 2026, de-notification by Jan-Feb 2027, production targeted for Q1 FY28 (April 2027).
Garment installed capacity described as fully utilised, limited by available labour on machines; order book full.
Yarn utilisation 84% in Q2; internal yarn consumption about 40% of total yarn production. Stretch yarn internal use rose about 150 tons per month to 450-500 tons per month from about 300 tons.
Stretch product sales in fabric up about 30-40% YoY; management said capacity debottlenecking was completed.
demand_pricing: Polyester prices up 25-30% due to West Asia crisis and oil price rise; PTA and MEG inputs also higher. Pass-through to customers lagging in yarn, fabric and garments.
Q2 gross margin described by management as the highest achieved; yarn export orders lower due to freight costs and vessel availability.

Garments: export pickup in Q2; UK and EU FTAs cited as drivers. C&A fully onboarded with about INR5 crore pipeline for FY27 and INR20 crore-plus potential next year. Next onboarded in UK; Marks & Spencer being onboarded. UK garment business about INR20 crore, expected to more than double next year. Polish retailer Reserved onboarded (300-400 stores).
Europe FTA expected to become operational around June-July 2027; management called Europe the biggest growth opportunity.
European and UK garment margins expected at 12-15% EBITDA, with European margins described as healthier.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst (N Square Capital) asked how the company claims a pickup in momentum when all three verticals show volume declines, and whether raw-material inflation masks weak real growth.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said top-line growth came despite lower volume because focus is on value-added products, and gross margin was the highest achieved. It admitted raw-material increases are not fully passed on yet, with pass-through expected in H2. It said no volume growth guidance was given; guidance is for turnover and EBITDA margin growth.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst (KDM Advisors) asked about progress on slow-moving yarn inventory and working capital.
qa_highlights.answer: Management is working on inventory, receivables and cycle time at once. Customers lifted made-to-order goods slower than expected due to West Asia and freight issues, and the company was accommodating. Target is more value-added sales with working capital held or reduced each year.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked which export market offers the strongest growth.
qa_highlights.answer: Europe is the biggest opportunity, with the EU FTA expected by June or July 2027 and strong customer interest. UK FTA is already in effect, and business with Japan and other FTA markets is increasing.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst (Equitree Capital) asked whether capex of INR36 crore in H1 against INR130-140 crore guidance signals delay.
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Kavita Gandhi said there is no delay; spend is need-based and most projects, including ETP, will complete in H2. Management expects to use nearly the full amount.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked for an update on the Surat garment facility, expansion beyond it, capex, and new EU/UK clients.
qa_highlights.answer: Surat is awaiting customs NOC (expected by end-November) and production is targeted for April 2027. Surat adds INR150-200 crore over about 2 years, with INR30-50 crore capex. C&A, Next, M&S and Reserved were onboarded or in process.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst (Jain Securities) asked about FY27 margin drivers and the share of yarn consumed internally.
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to higher stretch-product sales (up about 30-40%) and internal use of value-added yarn. About 40% of yarn is consumed internally, and that share may rise.

qa_highlights.question: Individual investor asked whether double-digit revenue and margin growth is possible over the next 2-3 years.

504028|2026-03.headline: GEE Q4 FY26 turnover rose to INR112 crore and FY26 to about INR370 crore, with EBITDA margin near 9% and a 25-30% revenue CAGR target to FY29.

Management framed FY26 as a stabilisation year after the May 2025 promoter restructuring, and set targets of INR1,000 crore revenue by FY29-30, FY27 revenue above INR500 crore and EBITDA margin above 10%. 504028|2026-06.headline: GEE Ltd Q1 FY27 revenue rose 30% YoY to INR 103 crores, with EBITDA margin up 204 bps to 7.8%.

504028|2026-09.headline: GEE Ltd H1 FY27 turnover rose 24% to INR 204 crore, but Q2 margins compressed on input-cost inflation; management targets 25-30% growth and 12-13% EBITDA margin.
504028|2026-09.overview: Management reported H1 FY27 turnover of about INR 204 crore (up 24% from INR 165 crore), EBITDA of about INR 16 crore (up 17.5% from INR 13.5 crore) and PBT of about INR 10.7 crore (from about INR 7 crore). Management attributed margin pressure in the quarter to steel and oil price spikes linked to the Middle East war, and said gross margins should recover. The Wagle Industrial Estate land was handed to a developer for a real estate project, with management guiding to INR 400 crore-plus of revenue to the company over five years. The call also set out capacity expansion, new product verticals and a INR 1,000 crore revenue target by FY30.

segments.name: Welding consumables (core)
segments.commentary: Consolidated capacity about 59,000 MT (Kolkata plant 38,000 MT; second facility 21,000 MT). Specialised/niche products are about 27% of the basket, targeted at 35-40% in the coming year; conventional products sell at about INR 100-125/kg versus INR 275-1,500/kg for specialised products.

segments.name: Real estate (Wagle Industrial Estate, Thane)
segments.commentary: Land possession handed to developer under area-share revenue model; company expects INR 400 crore-plus revenue over five years, with sales and cash accruals starting from the first quarter of next financial year.

guidance_outlook: Top-line growth target of 25-30% YoY, with roughly 60% from volume and 40% from value per management's split.
Sustainable EBITDA margin of 12-13% targeted in three to four years; management cited 0.5% gain in FY27, a further 0.5-1% in FY28, and double-digit margin in FY28.
Q3 and Q4 FY27 EBITDA margin expected to be restored to 9% and above.
INR 1,000 crore revenue target placed realistically at FY30; capacity to rise from 59,000 MT to 71,000 MT with over 90% utilisation by FY29-FY30.
Export turnover target of 15-20% of total in the next two to three years.

qa_highlights.question: When will the company receive cash from the real estate project and in what form?

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin decline, and what is the margin guidance?

504036|2026-06.headline: Hirect Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 20.3% to INR258.4 crore, but EBITDA fell 45.4% YoY to INR13.2 crore as Elventive France drags margins.

Standalone revenue grew 10.1% to INR236.4 crore and standalone EBITDA rose 3.2% to INR25.1 crore at a 10.6% margin. 504036|2026-09.headline: Hirect Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue up 39% YoY to Rs 315.7 cr, but consolidated EBITDA margin fell to 4.3% as margins were squeezed.

Profitability lagged: consolidated gross margin was 24.1% in Q2 and consolidated EBITDA margin was 4.3%, with H1 EBITDA margin at 4.7%. Drivers cited were higher raw material costs, adverse product mix, the scale-up of Alventure France, and deliberate investment in people. Management guided to near-term EBITDA margin pressure continuing for the next few quarters, with gradual improvement later.

504132|2026-03.headline: Permanent Magnets Q4 standalone revenue rose 47% YoY to INR 66 crores; FY26 revenue INR 225 crores (+13%), with Relays ramp pushed to H2 FY27.

FY26 EBITDA margin was 17% versus 14% a year earlier, helped by product mix and second-half scale-up; Q4 margin was 15%, up YoY but down sequentially. Q4 was dented by a 30 MW captive unit shutdown, a 300 MW turbine maintenance outage in January, seasonal hydro slowdown and the coal mine hitting its 1.8 MTPA approved limit. financial_highlights.change: Approx. INR 162.6 cr revenue and INR 18 cr other income pre-tax; about 25% of INR 110 cr at EBITDA level per CFO

financial_highlights.value: More than INR 2,500 cr as of 30 June 2026

qa_highlights.question: Is realisation per unit falling as more PPAs are signed, given the implied ~INR 8/unit on power sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the back-calculated realisation is wrong because current income includes prior-year adjustments. Full-year power should be assumed at INR 5-6/unit, rising with inflation and peak demand, especially for hydro.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 110 cr one-time benefit's P&L split available, and what is the other-income effect?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue impact was about INR 162.64 cr and other income about INR 18 cr (interest awarded with tariff). EBITDA effect is about 25% of the INR 110 cr, net of tax.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 380 MW of PPAs is at SKS, what tariff applies, and what is the maximum SKS PPA quantity?
qa_highlights.answer: About 330 MW of the 380 MW is at SKS, at INR 5-6/unit. Maximum SKS quantity is 540 MW, and management said it still has to decide how far to commit.

qa_highlights.question: Which coal mines make up the 7.1 Mt target, and is Gare Palma IV/7 expansion to 5 Mt planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Gare Palma IV/7 is 1.8 Mt, Shahpur West 0.6 Mt, Senduri about 0.6 Mt (provisional), and Gare Palma IV/5 about 2.0 Mt. Management said the 1.8 to 5 Mt expansion is not in the immediate plan as new higher-grade mines take priority.

qa_highlights.question: What is the SKS 600 MW to 1,200 MW environmental clearance timeline and construction start?
qa_highlights.answer: TOR submission in about 3 months, then public hearing and 6-8 months for EC, then 6-8 months to appoint a consultant before procedures start. Management did not give a construction start date.

qa_highlights.question: When will the new SKS unit be completed, and will turnover more than double?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated completion by FY31, as stated on the last call. On turnover doubling, management said it should be by that time.

qa_highlights.question: Has Sikkim hydro normalised, and is there residual Q2 impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Sikkim is operating at full capacity. Management does not expect a residual impact in Q2, apart from about 5 days of July generation lost.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 PAT and EBITDA be guided numerically?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said it does not give forward profitability guidance given the volatile market. It said Q2 should be better on hydro and July power prices, and FY27 IPP generation should exceed last year's 415 crore units.

qa_highlights.question: What is the mineral wool revenue, and what are the Q2 and FY27 sales and EBITDA targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Plant is at 60-65% of capacity and not yet profitable. Management guided FY27 revenue of about INR 90-110 cr, said Q2 is hard to comment on, and expects full production in about 6 months.

risks_watch: Delayed monsoon and hydro generation: small hydro was about 1% below last year in Q1, and Q2 depends on rainfall.

Quality of earnings: Q1 PAT included a one-time INR 110 cr net benefit, and the company gave no numerical FY27 guidance.

504614|2026-09.headline: H1 FY27 record EBITDA of INR1,326 crores (up ~4% YoY) and PAT of INR799 crores (up ~5%); Q2 EBITDA INR564 crores, PAT INR320 crores.
504614|2026-09.overview: Management reported the highest-ever half-yearly EBITDA and PAT for H1 FY27, with total income of INR3,221 crores and cash profit of INR1,225 crores. In Q2, captive power operations were recalibrated to market conditions, supporting EBITDA of INR564 crores on total income of INR1,505 crores despite a 47-day shutdown of one 300 MW thermal unit and an 18-day Sikkim hydro outage. Management said energy contributed more than 75% of H1 EBITDA and that higher realisations in thermal and hydro drove profitability. The company entered manganese ore mining via preferred bidder status for the Avagudem block (Andhra Pradesh), and ratings were upgraded (SEML to AA from AA-; Sarda Metals & Alloys to AA- from A, CRISIL).

segments.name: Energy (thermal and hydro)
segments.commentary: Contributed more than 75% of H1 FY27 EBITDA. 600 MW thermal plant had a 47-day shutdown of one 300 MW unit in Q2; management expects H2 thermal profitability to be substantially higher. Hydro H2 profitability expected lower due to seasonality.

segments.name: Iron ore pellets (Raipur)
segments.commentary: Record H1 pellet output of 4,29,059 tons. Q2 realisation about INR9,800/ton, versus above INR10,000/ton in Q1. Management expects pellet output to remain broadly flat in H2.

segments.name: Ferro alloys / metals (steel billets, wire rods, flats)
segments.commentary: Billet and wire rod plants were not operated for part of Q2 as power was sold in the market. Management described flat steel as more buoyant than long products, with flat steel near INR75,000-77,000/ton and long products near INR54,000 in some Mumbai markets.

segments.name: Mining (coal and manganese)
segments.commentary: Shahpur West high-grade coal mine targeted for commissioning before end of FY27; Bartunga Hill expected by end of FY28. Avagudem manganese block (4,50,000 tons extractable reserves) won via auction; operations expected in 12-14 months.

guidance_outlook: Management gave no forward numerical guidance on revenue or EBITDA for FY27.
FY27 thermal generation expected to exceed 420 crore units; H1 generation was 202 crore units.
No major thermal shutdown expected for the rest of FY27; one 300 MW unit to be shut for 30-40 days in FY28.
Environmental clearance for 600 MW to 1,200 MW thermal expansion expected within FY27 after MoEF terms of reference.
Avagudem manganese mine expected to save INR200-400/ton on low-grade ore; start in 12-14 months, subject to approvals.
Management expects H2 FY27 power prices to be much better than H1 realisations.
Logistics and raw material cost pressure expected to ease in 2-3 months per management; next quarter described as unpredictable.
capex_capacity: Expansion of 600 MW thermal to 1,200 MW: terms of reference approved by MoEF; environmental clearance expected within FY27. Brownfield, funded from internal accruals.
50 MW captive solar project expected to be commissioned next quarter, subject to right-of-way issues on transmission line.

Three small hydro projects in Chhattisgarh (aggregate 74 MW) approvals progressing as scheduled. Recently acquired 66 MW hydro project in Arunachal Pradesh: key approvals in place, land acquired, approach road work started.
Replaced 3 MW turbogenerator at Raipur commenced operations in August 2026 at full capacity.
Gare Palma IV/5 and Senduri coal block regulatory approvals progressing as planned.
demand_pricing: Thermal: about 60% of saleable thermal power capacity tied up under contracts; spot realisation in Q2 about INR5.20-5.50/unit per management.
Hydro: all hydro projects tied up except Sikkim (113 MW), which the company is keeping on the spot market; Sikkim earned above INR6/unit over H1 on average.
National context per management: power generation up 11% YoY to about 536 billion units in the quarter; peak demand up 18% to 270 GW; solar generation up 39%.

Coking coal and freight costs rose sharply: bulk freight near USD36-38 versus usual USD18-22 per vessel, due to high crude prices and West Asia tensions. Indian mine output affected by monsoon flooding.
Iron ore pellet realisation: above INR10,000/ton in Q1 FY27, about INR9,800/ton in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: How will Avagudem manganese mine strengthen raw material integration, and when will cost benefits show?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the mine (4,50,000 tons extractable reserves) would save about INR200-400/ton on low-grade ore, providing raw material security for four to five years. Start depends on paperwork; no investment figure disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: What was the revenue impact of the 300 MW shutdown in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO estimated lost revenue of about INR120-140 crores from the 300 MW unit shutdown in the quarter. Steel billet and wire rod plants were not run for part of the quarter because power was sold in the market.

qa_highlights.question: Will the thermal shutdown affect FY27 generation?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said FY27 generation would exceed last year's, with no major shutdown planned for the rest of the year; one unit is expected to need a 30-40 day shutdown in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What are realisations and tie-ups for H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Thermal realisation was about INR5.30/unit in Q2 and above INR6/unit for hydro. About 60% of saleable thermal capacity is tied up; H2 prices are expected to be better than H1.

qa_highlights.question: Can FY27 revenue exceed INR2,500 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give any numerical forward guidance, calling the question speculative.

qa_highlights.question: What were pellet realisations in Q1, Q2 and October?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 pellet realisation was above INR10,000/ton and Q2 about INR9,800/ton; October figures were not given.

risks_watch: Raw material and logistics cost squeeze from high crude, freight costs and Australian coking coal prices; management expects easing in 2-3 months but next quarter is unpredictable.
Environmental clearance for the 600 MW to 1,200 MW expansion expected within FY27; timing not firm.
Avagudem manganese mine: approvals and start timing (12-14 months) still uncertain; costs not disclosed.
Sikkim hydro remains untied to contracts and is exposed to spot prices and seasonal rainfall (H2 hydro profitability guided lower).
Shahpur West coal mine commissioning targeted before FY27 year-end; Bartunga Hill by end FY28.
Investor perception of shutdown timing: a retail investor questioned the Q2 shutdown during peak-price months; management said it was intimated in the prior call.

504903|2026-03.headline: Rathi Steel FY26 total income rose ~41.7% to INR716 crore; Q4 PAT INR7.45 crore at 3% margin, with mills still only ~51-52% utilised.
504903|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 total income of about INR716 crore (+41.7% YoY), EBITDA of INR28.9 crore (+18.8%) and PAT of INR12.87 crore (+39.24%, excluding prior-year exceptional items). Q4 total income was INR244.57 crore (+63.3% YoY, +52.7% QoQ), EBITDA INR9.89 crore (+22% YoY, +54% QoQ) and PAT INR7.45 crore, with PAT margin of about 3%. Growth was attributed to the restart of the idle TMT rolling mill in April 2025, which lifted rolling output about 117% to roughly 1,02,000 tons. Utilisation remains low at about 51-52% for both rolling and melting, which management sees as the main lever for margins.

segments.name: Rolling mill (TMT and stainless wire rod)
segments.commentary: Capacity ~2,00,000 tons per annum, utilisation ~51.4% in FY26; output grew ~117% YoY to ~1,02,000 tons after the TMT mill restart. Management did not split volumes between TMT and stainless.

segments.name: Steel melting shop (SMS)
segments.commentary: Capacity ~85,000 tons per annum, utilisation ~53% in FY26 (50-52% cited in opening remarks); about 40-45% backward integrated. Target is ~80% utilisation.

segments.name: Stainless steel vs TMT revenue mix
segments.commentary: Management estimated ~60% of FY26 revenue from B2B (mainly stainless) and ~40% from TMT bars, an approximate figure.

guidance_outlook: Rolling mill utilisation targeted at ~65-70% this year (fallback ~60-65%), up from ~51%.
Steel melting shop utilisation to move from ~50-52% towards ~80%.
Aspiration for ~20-25% average annual growth, using FY25 as base; earlier guidance was ~20% CAGR over three years.
Direct charging on the TMT mill expected to save ~INR3,000-4,000 per ton, or ~6-7% of TMT selling price including yield benefits, on the directly charged volume.
Capex of ~INR20 crore+ a year expected to continue for a few years, mainly replacement and debottlenecking; SMS expansion under study subject to approvals.
Refinancing talks under way with the existing lender at 16% cost of borrowing, with new lenders being explored at lower rates.
capex_capacity: Melting capacity ~85,000 tpa and rolling ~2,00,000 tpa at a ~12.5-acre NCR (Ghaziabad) site; FY26 utilisation ~51-52% for both divisions.
FY26 capex of INR20 crore+, mostly replacement and debottlenecking; the TMT restart cost ~INR5-7 crore in FY25.
Direct charging being implemented on the TMT mill, following its success in stainless wire rod.
SMS capacity expansion being evaluated at costs well below industry benchmarks; a larger melting unit is under consideration subject to demand visibility and statutory clearances.
Rooftop solar feasibility under study, indicatively 1-2 MW; open-access renewable power is over one-fourth of total power consumption.
demand_pricing: Management says domestic steel demand is healthy, with TMT and rebar pricing recovering after a prolonged soft patch.
Imports, mainly from Asia, are pressuring the industry; management says few rebar or stainless long products are imported into NCR, so the direct impact is limited.
Stainless steel pricing comes under pressure above a certain utilisation level; the company is shifting to a more balanced product mix to reduce reliance on any one category.
TMT sold mainly in NCR because freight limits longer-distance sales; stainless also sold in other states.
Institutional buyers are increasingly asking for GreenPro-certified products, which the company obtained for its Rathi Powertech 550 grade TMT bars (CII GreenPro Type-1 Ecolabel).
Fuel costs have roughly doubled over two to three months due to the Iran situation, which management cited as a margin headwind.

qa_highlights.question: What were TMT and stainless volume growth and spreads?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no separate TMT and stainless volumes; overall rolled output grew ~117% to ~1,02,000 tons. Margins are expected to improve with higher utilisation, subject to fuel costs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost of borrowing and the finance cost reduction target for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Current cost of borrowing is 16% from a single lender. Talks are under way to refinance and secure additional need-based facilities at lower cost; no reduction target was quantified.

qa_highlights.question: What are the GST disputes and how much is under dispute?
qa_highlights.answer: Disputes relate to alleged input ITC issues at various adjudication stages; some are stayed by higher courts. Management does not expect any demand to crystallise. No amount was given.

qa_highlights.question: What are the payment and inventory cycles?
qa_highlights.answer: Average debtor period is ~25-30 days across products (receivables ~1 month). Payables ~60 days; inventory ~25-30 days (about one month overall).

qa_highlights.question: What are the key competitors and how does Rathi compete?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited NCR proximity for delivery, brand recall and distribution network as edges; cost will be at par with peers once direct charging is in place on TMT.

qa_highlights.question: What are the challenges to reach 75-80% utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited establishing product acceptance for the restarted TMT mill and stainless supply pressure from IBC-driven acquisitions two years ago, with demand expected to catch up with supply.

risks_watch: Fuel cost spike (Iran-related) eroding the direct-charging saving and the margin recovery.
Stainless steel pricing pressure as utilisation rises, given new supply from IBC acquisitions.
Single-lender dependence at 16% cost of borrowing; refinancing outcome is pending.
Unquantified GST input-credit disputes with adjudication and stays still pending.
Management did not give a Q4 volume split between TMT and stainless, or Q4 raw material cost; key data gaps.
Slow utilisation ramp (51% to 65-70% target) and the 550D premium-grade product push.
Plant ageing; ongoing replacement capex needed.

504903|2026-06.headline: Rathi Steel & Power Q1 FY27 total income rose 24.6% to INR193.67 crores, PAT up 84.5% to INR3.48 crores, with volumes up ~30% to 28,372 MT.
504903|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 showed strong volume growth, driven by TMT bars, which more than doubled to about 18,677 MT from about 8,200 MT a year earlier. Total income reached INR193.67 crores (+24.6% YoY), EBITDA INR7.77 crores (+24.83%), and PAT INR3.48 crores (+84.5%), taking PAT margin to 1.8% (+58 bps). Stainless steel volumes were soft, down roughly 10-12% YoY to about 9,000 MT, mainly due to export-linked end-users hit by freight costs and West Asia disruption. Management reiterated a rolling mill utilisation target above 60% for FY27 and a 20% revenue CAGR aspiration, while the TMT 550D direct-charging integration is still in trial and expected to ramp post-monsoon.

financial_highlights.change: vs 21,864 MT in Q1 FY26, ~+30% YoY
vs ~8,200 MT in Q1 FY26, more than doubled
Q1 and Q4 respectively; not disputed by management

segments.name: TMT bars
segments.commentary: Volumes more than doubled to ~18,677 MT; roughly 47-48% of revenue, sold ~100% in NCR, largely to real estate. Brand portion is only 48-50% integrated; 550D integration trial runs done, full ramp expected post-monsoon.

segments.name: Stainless steel
segments.commentary: Volumes ~9,000 MT, down 10-12% YoY on export-linked end-user weakness; roughly 52-53% of revenue. Management says it is more margin-accretive due to higher integration; 80-90% of range is 200 series.

Target of 20% revenue CAGR over the next two to three years, measured from FY25 base; management says achievable.
EBITDA margin improvement of 2-3 percentage points over about two years (FY27-FY28) cited as aspiration, from a range-bound 4-4.5%.
Expected FY27 capex of around INR15 crores plus, against INR4-5 crores spent so far, excluding new value-added projects.
Full-scale TMT 550D direct-charging ramp expected by Q4 FY27 after monsoon and pollution-related construction halts.
Melt shop expansion considered once utilisation exceeds 70-75%; refinancing with existing lenders being discussed to lower borrowing cost.

Renewable power ~20-25% of consumption via open access and exchanges, adjusted to price.
demand_pricing: Management expects softer steel realisations, volatile energy prices and geopolitical uncertainty to persist.

Raw materials sourced ~100% domestically in Q1 to limit currency exposure; ferro alloys hedged against order book.

qa_highlights.question: What monthly dispatch run rate in July-August, and is Q1 momentum sustaining?

qa_highlights.question: Rolling mill utilisation and exit rate for FY27?

qa_highlights.question: Capex spent so far and full-year plan?

qa_highlights.question: Margin levers and EBITDA target?

qa_highlights.question: Working capital funding for the 30% volume increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Met mainly through extended supplier credit; management plans refinancing with existing lenders to get cheaper bank limits.

504973|2026-03.headline: Chola MS FY26 combined ratio rose to 115.2% (112.2% ex-1/n) on motor claims and crop loss; PBT Rs454 crore, ROE 10.4%.
504973|2026-03.overview: Chola MS reported Q4 GDPI of Rs2,048 crore and FY26 GDPI of Rs7,762 crore, with the loss of crop business after re-tender cutting Rs124 crore in Q4 and over Rs590 crore for the year. The FY26 claims ratio rose about 2.71 percentage points, driven by motor OD claims and a stepped-up motor third-party reserve, pushing the combined ratio to 115.2%. FY26 PBT was Rs454 crore after labour-code gratuity provisioning, and ROE was 10.4% against a 3-year average peak of about 14.4%. Management will seek forbearance to move statutory accounting to Ind AS from April 1, 2027, and Rajive Kumaraswami takes over as MD from June 1.

financial_highlights.change: higher YoY; overall claims ratio up about 2.71 pp

financial_highlights.metric: FY26 ROE on average net worth

segments.name: Motor
segments.commentary: Market share 5.25%; mix of cars 49%+, CVs 40%+, 2-wheelers about 10.5%. Motor OD share grew to about 5.89% while TP share fell about 0.5 pp. 2-wheeler share cut from 19.6% to about 10.6%.

segments.name: Long-term non-motor
segments.commentary: Premium received in advance rose to about Rs570 crore at March 2026 from Rs250 crore at March 2025. Non-motor market share 3.3% for the year, with premium received in advance of Rs410 crore for the year.

segments.name: Crop
segments.commentary: Lost crop business after re-tender, a hit of about Rs598 crore for FY26 per the Q&A. Management expects to participate in the next tender cycle across states, awaiting Government of India guidelines.

segments.name: Commercial vehicles
segments.commentary: CV book about 40-42% of motor mix and stable. Management sees pricing pressure and is managing line sizes while using newly secured reinsurance capacity on favourable terms.

guidance_outlook: Management does not give formal forward guidance on combined ratio; medium- to long-term intent is to maintain ROE of 15%+.
Motor OD price realisation up about 7-8% over the last 2-3 months; management expects motor OD loss ratio to start falling within about 6 months.
Statutory accounting to move to Ind AS from April 1, 2027 (FY28) under forbearance; significant drop in combined ratio expected in the year of adoption, then levelling out.

Dividend withheld, with earnings retained to support growth and solvency.
demand_pricing: Direct premium declined in FY26; GWP growth came mainly from reinsurance inward business.
Motor TP premium unchanged for about 4-5 years; management is pressing regulator and government for two-way TP pricing correction.
Motor OD claims ratio rose across industry; Chola's rise about 10% versus about 5-7% for peers, per management.

Management says expected IFRS adoption (DAC and discounting of motor TP) will benefit P&L.

qa_highlights.question: Will the approach change under EOM compliance, and which lines will recover market share for growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects crop business to return from the next tender cycle and aims to grow direct crop; motor 2-wheeler cut is near its floor; car and CV books to keep growing.

qa_highlights.question: How can ROE rise to 16-17% if leverage falls to 5.5% and combined ratio is 108-109%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says the OD claims ratio is the area of correction (about 10% above peers), with 7-8% price realisation gains and a target ROE of about 15%. TP reserving is prudent and cash is unaffected.

qa_highlights.question: What will the claims ratio look like under Ind AS/IFRS?
qa_highlights.answer: Motor TP provisions are discounted under IFRS, which brings a significant one-time benefit on transition and later P&L benefit through the unwind; no quantified figure given.

qa_highlights.question: Why did solvency drop to 1.96x and how will it recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher claims growth consumed more capital; solvency should recover with better claims ratio and retained earnings.

qa_highlights.question: Guidance on combined ratio?
qa_highlights.answer: No combined ratio guidance; will aim for 15%+ ROE medium to long term, managing float income and combined ratio as EOM changes.

Crop tender outcome and timing uncertain; GWP growth depends on winning back crop business.
